No parent required." - path: mIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mIsDisabled value: false - path: mPriority value: 0 - path: mTags value: - KMods.EventOnly # --- UKAPIDeliveryTask common fields --- - path: mAdaMessages value: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete - path: mToastIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mToastText value: "You completed the Root Task." - path: mCoordinate value: X: -2 Y: -1 # mParentTask / bRequireAllParents intentionally omitted the root has no parent, and # bRequireAllParents is ignored once there's nothing to require. - path: bIsEndless value: false # --- One-Time fields (bIsEndless: false) --- - path: mRewards value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 50 # mCosts omitted empty cost list makes this tree entry free. - id: DeliveryTask_Above class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mName value: "Single-Parent Child" - path: mDescription value: "Requires only the Above parent (Root)." - path: mIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mIsDisabled value: false - path: mPriority value: 0 - path: mTags value: - KMods.EventOnly - path: mAdaMessages value: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete - path: mToastIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mToastText value: "You completed the Single-Parent Child task." - path: mCoordinate value: X: -2 Y: 0 # Above -> (-2, -1): Root - path: mParentTask value: Above - path: bRequireAllParents value: true - path: bIsEndless value: false - path: mRewards value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 50 - path: mCosts value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 20 - id: DeliveryTask_Right class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mName value: "Endless Sibling Child" - path: mDescription value: "Requires only the Left parent (Root). Endless variant demonstrates every Endless field." - path: mIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mIsDisabled value: false - path: mPriority value: 0 - path: mTags value: - KMods.EventOnly - path: mAdaMessages value: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete - path: mToastIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mToastText value: "You completed another round of the Endless Sibling Child task." - path: mCoordinate value: X: -1 Y: -1 # Left -> (-2, -1): Root - path: mParentTask value: Left - path: bRequireAllParents value: true - path: bIsEndless value: true # --- Endless-only fields (bIsEndless: true) --- - path: mPoolElements value: - mItem: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C mAmountRange: LowerBound: Type: Inclusive Value: 50 UpperBound: Type: Exclusive Value: 200 mRequiredTas: -1 # INDEX_NONE eligible from the very first roll - path: mTaskRewards value: - mRewards: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 25 mRequiredTask: -1 # INDEX_NONE granted on every completion - path: mMaxTasks value: 10 # INDEX_NONE/-1 would mean uncapped concurrent slots - path: mAmountMultiplierCurve value: DeliveryTaskAmountMultiplier - path: mAbsolutMaxItemAmount value: RF_SOLID: DeliveryTaskAmountMultiplier RF_LIQUID: DeliveryTaskAmountMultiplier - id: DeliveryTask_AboveAndLeft class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mName value: "Two-Parent Child" - path: mDescription value: "Requires both the Above and Left parents at once (AND semantics)." - path: mIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mIsDisabled value: false - path: mPriority value: 0 - path: mTags value: - KMods.EventOnly - path: mAdaMessages value: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete - path: mToastIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mToastText value: "You completed the Two-Parent Child task." - path: mCoordinate value: X: -1 Y: 0 # Above -> (-1, -1): Right, Left -> (-2, 0): Above - path: mParentTask # multiple flags set in parallel value: - Above - Left - path: bRequireAllParents value: true # AND: both parents must be completed first - path: bIsEndless value: false - path: mRewards value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 100 - path: mCosts value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 40 - id: DeliveryTask_UnlockSuperIngot class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mName value: "Unlock: Pure Super Ingot" - path: mDescription value: "Force-unlocks the Pure Super Ingot schematic on completion." - path: mIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mIsDisabled value: false - path: mPriority value: 0 - path: mTags value: - KMods.EventOnly - path: mAdaMessages value: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete - path: mToastIcon value: DeliveryTaskIcon - path: mToastText value: "Pure Super Ingot production unlocked!" - path: mCoordinate value: X: -1 Y: 1 # Above -> (-1, 0): AboveAndLeft - path: mParentTask value: Above - path: bRequireAllParents value: true -

sections.heading: Instanced dependencies and unlocks
sections.text: Delivery-task data assets accept dedicated dependencies: and unlocks: lists alongside properties:. They append to mTaskDependencies and mUnlocks; generic property ops cannot construct these instanced subobjects. assets: - id: DeliveryTask_AboveAndLeft class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask dependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: - path: mSchematics value: - Schematic_MyPrerequisite unlocks: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlockGiveItem properties: - path: mItemsToGive value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 25 Known native paths automatically remap to Blueprint implementations; exact Blueprint paths remain valid. See Base-Game Unlock Classes and Availability Dependency Classes.

sections.heading: How completing a task unlocks more of the tree
sections.text: A node becomes available once its mParentTask requirement is satisfied: - bRequireAllParents: true (the default) every flagged parent must be completed first (AND). DeliveryTask_AboveAndLeft above needs both Above and Right done. - bRequireAllParents: false any one flagged parent completing is enough (OR). Useful for a node reachable from more than one earlier branch, whichever the player finishes first. - mRequiredParentCompletions: 1 (the default) completion count each marked parent must reach. Raise it for branches behind repeatable tasks; AND/OR semantics then compare parents against same threshold. - mTaskDependencies (an availability-dependency list, checked via AreTaskDependenciesMet) adds further gating on top of the parent-tree check itself a schematic purchase, a research unlock, whatever the dependency subclass checks. Parent completion and mTaskDependencies are independent gates: both must pass. For an endless node (bIsEndless: true), "unlocking more" also means more concurrent task slots: mMaxTasks caps how many of that node's rolled tasks can be active/queued at once (INDEX_NONE/-1 for uncapped), and mAmountMultiplierCurve / mAbsolutMaxItemAmount scale the reward amounts up as the player completes more rounds of it so the effective "how much can I get from this node" grows over time even though the node itself doesn't move in the tree.

sections.heading: Unlock example force-unlocking a schematic
sections.text: DeliveryTask_UnlockSuperIngot above is the unlock example: its mSchematics force-unlocks Schematic_PureSuperIngot via HandleUnlock on completion, regardless of whether the player could normally research or purchase it another way the same mechanism unlocks: / dependencies: use on schematics themselves, just triggered from a delivery-task completion instead. mRewards/ mCosts on that same node are the plain item grant/cost, independent of the schematic unlock.

pages.title: End-to-End Pack
pages.description: One real pack that combines an item, recipe, schematic, sink points, translation, a dynamic data asset, and RRDA editing, plus how to rename an id safely.

sections.heading: End-to-End Pack
sections.text: The individual type pages ( Items , Resources , Buildings , Unlocks , Recipes , Schematics , Research Trees , Sink Points , Game Tags , Localization , Data Assets ) each explain one document type in isolation. This page shows the thing that actually matters day to day: how several of them live together in one pack and reference each other without any include: juggling, because the stage order already handles it for you. A single pack folder holds every file below side by side, one document type per file, all under one pack root: <your-mod>/DataForge/ pack.yml super-ingot.item.yml super-ingot.recipe.yml super-ingot.schematic.yml super-ingot.sinkpoints.yml de.localization.yml cleaner.dataasset.yml faster-boilers.cdo.yml Note Every file above is shown separately for clarity, but that’s a choice, not a requirement. Any of them can be merged into one file with --- separators (see Multiple Documents Per File ). For example, super-ingot.item.yml and super-ingot.sinkpoints.yml could just as well be a single super-ingot.yml with two type: -tagged documents, useful for small, self-contained additions where a whole folder of one-liners feels like overkill. This page keeps them split because the individual type pages link straight to their matching file.

sections.heading: pack.yml
sections.text: pack.yml is optional. A folder without one just forms an implicit pack named after its directory. Once you care about save compatibility across versions, though, you want one. Three fields matter here. ref is the stable pack reference embedded in every generated class path ( /KDataForge/Gen/<ref>.Gen_<ref>_<Id> ) that this pack produces. name is the human readable display name. version is an informational semver value used in conflict reports. This pack declares its ref up front, so the redirect added later has something stable to anchor to: ref : MyPack # the save-persistence contract generated classes embed this ref name : My Content Pack version : 1.0.0

sections.heading: The item
sections.text: An item document generates a brand-new ItemDescriptor subclass and sets its CDO properties in one step. super-ingot.item.yml parents a new item off the vanilla iron ingot and configures three things on it. It gets a localized display name using block key , ns , and source fields rather than a plain string, so the German translation below can target it. It also gets a description, and an SS_HUGE stack size, which is an EStackSize enum value rather than a plain count: super-ingot.item.yml type : item items : - id : MySuperIngot parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mDisplayName value : key : MySuperIngot_Name ns : MyPack source : Super Ingot - path : mDescription value : A far superior ingot. - path : mStackSize value : SS_HUGE # EStackSize enum, not a plain count This generates /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot . The path is deterministic and id-based, so every other file below can reference it safely regardless of load order.

sections.heading: The recipe
sections.text: A recipe document describes ingredients, products, craft duration, and which buildable(s) can craft it, all as CDO properties on a generated FGRecipe subclass. This one consumes 2 iron ingots, produces 1 of the item generated above, takes 4 seconds, and runs in a Smelter Mk.1: super-ingot.recipe.yml type : recipe recipes : - id : Recipe_MySuperIngot properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Ingot - path : mIngredients value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount : 2 - path : mProduct value : - ItemClass : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot Amount : 1 - path : mManufactoringDuration value : 4.0 - path : mProducedIn value : - /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/SmelterMk1/Build_SmelterMk1.Build_SmelterMk1_C No include: is needed here. Items always finishes before Recipes starts, so the product reference above just works.

sections.heading: The schematic (with an FGUnlockRecipe unlock)
sections.text: A schematic document generates a milestone and, through an inline unlocks: list, wires up what it grants. Here that is an FGUnlockRecipe unlock pointing back at the recipe generated above. Completing this schematic is what actually makes the recipe available to the player: super-ingot.schematic.yml type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_MySuperIngot properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Ingot Smelting - path : mTechTier value : 2 - path : mTimeToComplete value : 60 - path : mCost value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount : 50 unlocks : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties : - path : mRecipes value : - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Recipe_MySuperIngot register: true , which is the default, registers this schematic. From there, SML’s auto-propagation takes over: the recipe and its items register right along with it.

sections.heading: Sink points for the item
sections.text: A sinkpoints document is a small standalone table of AWESOME Sink point values keyed by item class. This one gives the freshly generated ingot 8 points on the Default track: super-ingot.sinkpoints.yml type : sinkpoints track : Default entries : - item : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot points : 8 Remember that this one specifically needs a session restart to take effect. See Sink Points for why.

sections.heading: German translation
sections.text: A localization document maps translation keys (or exact source-text overrides) to translated strings for one namespace and culture . Here the culture is de , which prefix-matches so it also covers de-DE : de.localization.yml type : localization namespace : MyPack culture : de # prefix-matched: also applies for de-DE entries : MySuperIngot_Name : ' Superbarren ' KeyWithSource : source : ' Super Ingot Smelting ' text : ' Superbarren-Verhüttung ' # override by source text The item’s mDisplayName used localized FText fields ( key: MySuperIngot_Name , ns: MyPack , and source: ), so the simple key entry above translates it directly. This one is loaded at session start: you can iterate on translations without restarting.

sections.heading: Dynamic data asset: KAPI cleaner item
sections.text: A dataasset document creates a brand-new UPrimaryDataAsset instance (not a class) of any KAPI subclass and announces it to the asset registry. A conditions: block with hasMod: KAPI gates the whole document so it cleanly skips if KAPI isn’t installed, rather than erroring: cleaner.dataasset.yml type : dataasset conditions : hasMod : KAPI assets : - id : CleanerItem_MyFluid class : /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription # any UPrimaryDataAsset subclass properties : - path : mProductionTime value : 4.0 - path : mInFluid value : ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount : 1000 This creates a real PrimaryDataAsset instance and announces it to the asset registry. KDataForge then triggers KAPI’s own rescan, so it picks the new asset up. See Data Assets for the full mechanism and every KAPI asset type it applies to.

sections.heading: Editing RefinedR&D data assets (RRDA)
sections.text: Existing data-asset instances from other mods are edited with a plain cdo document too, using allAssetsOfClass: to hit every instance of a class at once. This patch halves the cook time of every RefinedR&D boiler, whether it is RefinedPower’s, FicsitFarming’s, or anyone else’s built on RefinedRDApi. It is gated the same way, behind a conditions: block with hasMod: : faster-boilers.cdo.yml type : cdo conditions : hasMod : RefinedRDApi patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/RefinedRDApi.RRDABoilerDataAsset properties : - path : mDuration op : multiply value : 0.5 # every RefinedPower/FicsitFarming boiler produces twice as fast No RefinedRDApi dependency is needed in your .uplugin . The rescan that picks this up runs via reflection, gated purely by the hasMod condition.

sections.heading: Renaming an id later: redirects:
sections.text: Renaming the file super-ingot.item.yml is always safe. Renaming the id MySuperIngot , however, changes the generated class path, which would orphan any save that already has the item. Declare the rename in pack.yml instead: # pack.yml (version 2.0.0 of this pack) ref : MyPack name : My Content Pack version : 2.0.0 redirects : MySuperIngot : SuperIngotMk2 # OldId: NewId The class is now generated as Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotMk2 , and FCoreRedirects resolves the old class path in existing saves to it. Items already in old saves load without warnings.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Something in this pack didn’t apply? /kdf report in chat prints every warning and error, along with the file and line that caused it. A broken file only skips itself: the rest of the pack still loads. Renamed an id and now old saves complain? That’s exactly what redirects: is for, as covered above. If you forgot to add one before shipping the rename, you can add it retroactively: it’s read at load time, not baked into the save. Ready to go deeper on one piece of this? Jump to the type page for whichever document you’re extending: Items , Recipes , Schematics , Sink Points , Localization , or Data Assets .

pages.title: Adding KAPI Data Assets
pages.description: Real, copy-pasteable "type: dataasset" examples for every KAPI data asset type air collector, cleaner, modular miner, slug breeding, extractor/resource allow-lists, and delivery-task tree nodes.

sections.heading: Adding KAPI Data Assets
sections.text: This page is worked type: dataasset examples, creating brand-new instances, for every KAPI data asset type. Editing *existing* instances via type: cdo is already covered on Data Assets. Four of the five examples below use real property values from actual shipped Satisfactory Plus / KLib content, so the numbers are realistic, not placeholders. The fifth (extractor/resource allow-lists) is illustrative since no shipped instance of that type exists to read from.

sections.heading: UKAPIAirCollectorData: air collector production
sections.text: Each Air Collector resource is its own UKAPIAirCollectorData instance the DataAsset registers a new gas/resource the Air Collector can extract, it does not patch an existing one. See the full property reference for every field; the example below mirrors Satisfactory Plus's own shipped "Air Collector extract Toxic Air via Resource Nodes" asset. Note bUseHightBasesdProduction selects one of two mutually exclusive production models — here it's false, so mMaxHit/mProductionPerHit are the active fields and mProduceItemCountMin/Max/Base (the other model) are omitted entirely, not just left at defaults. # file: air-collector-toxic-air.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: AirCollector_ToxicAirNode class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIAirCollectorData properties: - path: mRecipePrio value: 100 - path: mRangeToScan value: 2500 - path: bCheckNodes value: true - path: mTraceChannel value: - ObjectTypeQuery1 - ObjectTypeQuery2 - ObjectTypeQuery9 - ObjectTypeQuery6 - path: mItemClass value: /KLib/Assets/Ressources/Raw/Gas/Desc_ToxicAir.Desc_ToxicAir_C - path: mProductionTime value: 6 - path: bUseHightBasesdProduction value: false - path: mMaxHit value: 2 - path: mProductionPerHit value: 6000

sections.heading: `UKAPICleanerItemDescription`: Filtrator (Cleaner) recipes
sections.text: A dataasset document targeting KAPICleanerItemDescription creates a brand-new Filtrator recipe: which input fluid it consumes, what it outputs, and any bonus items produced alongside the main conversion. See the full property reference for every field, including FKAPICleanerInfo. The example below reproduces Satisfactory Plus's own "Filtrator filter Wastewater" recipe: 6000 wastewater in, 4000 clean water out over 6 seconds, plus two bypass products (crushed zinc and crushed caterium) that come out independent of the main fluid conversion. mCleanerItemInfo is left out entirely here, it's optional, and this real recipe ships with no extra cleaner item required (mCleanerItemInfo.mProduceItem is None in the shipped asset). # file: filtrator-wastewater.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: CleanerItem_WasteWater class: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties: - path: bSkipUnlockCheck value: false - path: mProductionTime value: 6 - path: mInFluid value: ItemClass: /KLib/Assets/Ressources/Raw/Fluids/Desc_Wastewater.Desc_Wastewater_C Amount: 6000 - path: mOutFluid value: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount: 4000 - path: mBypassProducts value: - mProduceItem: /KLib/Assets/Parts/Production/Crushed/Desc_CrushedZinc.Desc_CrushedZinc_C mProductionTime: 12 mProduceAmount: 6 - mProduceItem: /KLib/Assets/Parts/Production/Crushed/Desc_CrushedCaterium.Desc_CrushedCaterium_C mProductionTime: 12 mProduceAmount: 6

sections.heading: UKAPIModularMinerDescription: modular miner ore entries
sections.text: Full property reference. Each UKAPIModularMinerDescription instance registers one raw-resource entry the KAPI modular miner can extract, its rarity/found flavor text, node screenshot, which attachment modules are required or blocked, and the minimum drill tier needed. The example below mirrors a real shipped Cryolite raw-ore entry: # file: modular-miner-cryolite.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: MM_Cryolite class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIModularMinerDescription properties: - path: mRarityText value: 'Common' - path: mFoundText value: 'Can be found in every biome.' - path: mNodeScreenshot value: /SatisfactoryPlus/AssetDatas/Miner/UI/TXUI_Wiki_ResourceNode_Cryolite.TXUI_Wiki_ResourceNode_Cryolite - path: mIsFallbackDescriptor value: false - path: mNeededModules value: - /KAPI/Attachments/ModularMiner/Attachment_MM_MiningHead.Attachment_MM_MiningHead_C - path: mPreventModules value: - /KLib/Assets/Buildings/ModularExtractor/Modules/Smelter/Build_SmelterModule.Build_SmelterModule_C - path: mResourceClass value: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/RawQuartz/Desc_RawQuartz.Desc_RawQuartz_C - path: mDrillTier value: 1 mFluidInfo and mModuleInformation are optional TMap fields (keyed by an item class and a waste-producer module class respectively) for entries that feed fluid or waste-producer modules, see the property reference for their map-key/value shapes. A resource entry that doesn't use either module type, like this one, works fine without them. mScannerTier is unused and left out entirely.

sections.heading: UKAPISugHatchingData: slug breeding & incubation
sections.text: Defines a slug species end to end: what it hatches from, how the incubator raises it, and its breeding-cycle behavior. See the full property reference for every field, including the fluid-incubator properties (mTankTier, mFluidConsume, mFluidClass, mFluidConsumeTime) left out below since bRequireFluid is false here. The example reproduces the shipped Red Slug breeder, trimmed to two mPossibleSlugs entries for readability. # file: kapi-slug-red.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: RedSlugBreeder class: /Script/KAPI.KAPISugHatchingData properties: - path: mSlug value: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Red.SlugDesc_Red_C - path: mEgg value: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Eggs/EggDesc_Red.EggDesc_Red_C - path: mEggColor value: R: 1 G: 1 B: 1 A: 1 - path: mSlugTier value: -1 - path: mHatchDuration value: 10 - path: mPowerConsume value: 0.1 - path: mIncubatorTier value: 1 - path: bRequireFluid value: false - path: mPossibleSlugs value: - mSlug: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Red.SlugDesc_Red_C mProductionCount: 1 mProbability: 100 mFixedChanceMultiplier: 0.1 bShouldUseFixedChance: true - mSlug: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Orange.SlugDesc_Orange_C mProductionCount: 1 mProbability: 0.38 mFixedChanceMultiplier: 1 bShouldUseFixedChance: true - path: mProductionCountEggs value: 1 - path: mBreedingTime value: 40 - path: mDieTime value: 100 - path: mRequiredFood value: /KLib/Assets/Parts/Production/Food/Desc_SnailFood_Tier_20.Desc_SnailFood_Tier_20_C - path: mFoodConsumePerCycle value: 2 - path: mFoodDuration value: 20 - path: mComfortableWith value: - /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Orange.SlugDesc_Orange_C - path: mMinHumidity value: 0.8 - path: mMaxHumidity value: 0.85 - path: mMinHeat value: 80 - path: mMaxHeat value: 100 - path: mDayTime value: Any # EKAPISlugTime enum name (Any/Day/Night), not a raw number; Any is also the default

sections.heading: UKAPIExtractorAllowList: Registering new Extractors and Resources
sections.text: Unlike the other examples on this page, no shipped instance of this asset exists to read from the wiki data export has zero UKAPIExtractorAllowList entries. SF+ ships its own default allow-list as an existing default asset that mods normally type: cdo patch instead (see Data Assets); creating a brand new instance from scratch, as below, is mainly useful for a self-contained mod that wants its own allow-list rather than editing SF+'s. The values below are illustrative adjust the class paths to your own mod's classes. See Extractors → Properties for the full property reference. This is the same "hooking up a new resource type" scenario described on that reference page: a new custom extractor building needs to go in mAllowedExtractors before SF+ will treat it as a valid extractor, and a new resource descriptor needs to go in mAllowedResources before any extractor will recognize it as extractable: # file: my-extractor-allowlist.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: MyModExtractorAllowList class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIExtractorAllowList properties: - path: mAllowedExtractors value: - /Game/YourMod/Buildable/Build_YourExtractor.Build_YourExtractor_C - path: mAllowedResources value: - /Game/YourMod/Resource/Desc_YourResource.Desc_YourResource_C # mDisallowExtractors and mDisallowResources omitted no exclusions. - path: mPriority value: 0 mPriority defaults to 0; raise it only if another mod's allow/disallow list needs to be overridden for this class (see the priority note on the reference page).

sections.heading: `UKAPIDeliveryTask`: research-tree / delivery-task nodes
sections.text: UKAPIDeliveryTask places one node on a 2D coordinate grid and links it to a parent node (or several, at once) via mParentTask a bitmask property (EKAPIDeliveryTaskParent: Above/Left/Right/Bottom/AboveLeft/AboveRight/BelowLeft/BelowRight). Like UKAPIExtractorAllowList above, there's no shipped instance to read real values from this feature isn't part of Satisfactory Plus, it only needs KAPI + KPrivateCodeLib so the example below is illustrative. The interesting part is mParentTask accepting more than one flag at once. Use one scalar name for one parent or a YAML sequence for several. With WITH_METADATA, retained property metadata, and the enum already loaded, KDataForge resolves and ORs names or |-joined strings ("Above|Left"). This enum declares mask values: Above (1) and Left (2) combine to 3. Raw integer masks such as 3 are accepted by set only; append/prepend and remove require named flags. Stripped metadata or an unresolved enum leaves ordinary integer conversion without named bitmask forms or mutations. Shipping builds must retain metadata for these named examples. See Property Types for mask-value versus bit-index rules and width limits. bRequireAllParents then switches between AND (true, every flagged parent required; default) and OR (false, any one is enough) semantics. mRequiredParentCompletions defaults to 1 and requires that many completed runs from each marked parent. Values above 1 are intended for branches behind endless tasks and count completed runs, not queued repeats. See Value Forms for the full grammar. Every flag on mParentTask must resolve to a real sibling node at the matching coordinate offset (Above → the node directly above, Left → directly left, etc.) or the node is rejected at load time, so a small tree needs coordinates laid out to match: # file: showcase-delivery-task.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: DeliveryTask_Root class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mCoordinate value: X: 0 Y: 0 - path: mName value: "Root Task" - id: DeliveryTask_Child_Above class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mCoordinate value: X: 0 Y: 1 - path: mName value: "Single-Parent Child" - path: mParentTask value: Above - path: bRequireAllParents value: true - id: DeliveryTask_Child_Right class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mCoordinate value: X: 1 Y: 0 - path: mName value: "Sibling Child" - path: mParentTask value: Left # points back at (0, 0): the root - path: bRequireAllParents value: true - id: DeliveryTask_Child_AboveAndLeft class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mCoordinate value: X: 1 Y: 1 - path: mName value: "Two-Parent Child" - path: mParentTask # multiple flags set in parallel value: - Above # points to (1, 0) - Left # points to (0, 1); both nodes must exist in the tree - path: bRequireAllParents value: true # AND: both parents must be completed A one-time task (bIsEndless: false, the default) can also force-unlock a schematic and grant rewards on completion, via mSchematics/mRewards/mCosts: - id: DeliveryTask_UnlockSuperIngot class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: - path: mCoordinate value: X: 1 Y: 2 - path: mName value: "Unlock: Pure Super Ingot" - path: mParentTask value: Above - path: bRequireAllParents value: true - path: mSchematics # force-unlocked on completion value: - /Game/YourMod/Schematics/Schematic_PureSuperIngot.Schematic_PureSuperIngot_C - path: mRewards value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 500 - path: mCosts value: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 100 The full property set (including the Endless-only fields mPoolElements/mTaskRewards/mMaxTasks/ mAmountMultiplierCurve/mAbsolutMaxItemAmount) is demonstrated in [KDataForge's own reference sample pack](/kdataforge/getting-started), showcase-delivery-task.dataasset.yml.

pages.title: Power & Machines
pages.description: Editing examples for buildables, power, manufacturing speed, generators, extractors, pipelines, power storage, and runtime actor patches.

sections.heading: Power & Machines
sections.text: This page covers patching stats on buildables that already exist. That includes power consumption, manufacturing speed, generator output, extraction rate, pipeline throughput, and storage capacity, all through a plain type: cdo document. This is the far more common thing to want. If you’re instead looking to add a genuinely new building/buildable descriptor class to the build menu, that’s a different mechanism. Type: building covers generation. This page never generates anything: it only patches CDOs. Buildable CDOs expose factory tuning: mPowerConsumption , mPowerConsumptionExponent , mManufacturingSpeed , significance/overclock settings, mDisplayName , mDescription . ℹ️ Verify property names against your game version. The buildable examples on this page use real FactoryGame properties, but game updates occasionally rename or move them. If a target: path or path: doesn’t resolve, nothing breaks. The load report tells you exactly which patch failed ( /kdf report , see Getting Started → Troubleshooting ). Confirm the effect in-game after every patch.

sections.heading: Combining an exact target with a subclass-wide target in one document
sections.text: A single cdo document can mix a precise, single-building target: with a native base-class target: that fans out via applyToSubclasses: true . Below, the Mk.1 Smelter gets its own power draw and speed tweaks by exact class path. A second patch entry reaches every resource node and deposit through their shared native base class AFGResourceNode , doubling the extraction multiplier for miners across the board, vanilla and modded alike, in one pass: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/SmelterMk1/Build_SmelterMk1.Build_SmelterMk1_C properties : - path : mPowerConsumption op : multiply value : 0.75 - path : mManufacturingSpeed op : multiply value : 1.25 # Double the extraction yield of every resource node/deposit via the native base class: - target : /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceNode applyToSubclasses : true # FGResourceDeposit derives from FGResourceNode too properties : - path : mExtractMultiplier op : multiply value : 2

sections.heading: Power generator output
sections.text: All fuel-burning generators (coal, fuel, biomass burner) derive from AFGBuildableGeneratorFuel . The produced megawatts live on the generator base as mPowerProduction : type : cdo patches : - target : /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableGeneratorFuel applyToSubclasses : true # coal, fuel, biomass, modded fuel generators properties : - path : mPowerProduction op : multiply value : 2 # double output; fuel burn rate scales with it Target a single generator class (e.g. Build_GeneratorCoal.Build_GeneratorCoal_C ) instead when you don’t want the subclass blast radius. See Targeting .

sections.heading: Extractor cycle speed
sections.text: mExtractCycleTime is the seconds per extraction cycle. This property lives on the miner buildable itself, not the resource node. Halving it doubles the output rate: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/MinerMk1/Build_MinerMk1.Build_MinerMk1_C properties : - path : mExtractCycleTime op : multiply value : 0.5

sections.heading: Pipeline flow limit
sections.text: Every pipeline mark derives from AFGBuildablePipeline . mFlowLimit is the throughput cap in m³/s (Mk.1 = 300 m³/min = 5 m³/s): type : cdo patches : - target : /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildablePipeline applyToSubclasses : true # Mk.1 + Mk.2 + modded pipes properties : - path : mFlowLimit op : multiply value : 2

sections.heading: Power storage capacity
sections.text: Power Storage buildables cap how many megawatt-hours they can bank before topping out. mPowerStoreCapacity is that ceiling. This patch omits op: entirely, so it defaults to a plain set overwrite rather than a relative scale: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/PowerStorage/Build_PowerStorageMk1.Build_PowerStorageMk1_C properties : - path : mPowerStoreCapacity value : 200 # MWh (vanilla: 100)

sections.heading: Drone station logistics
sections.text: AFGBuildableDroneStation is an ordinary buildable, so its per-trip cargo/fuel tuning is a plain cdo patch like anything else: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/DroneStation/Build_DroneStation.Build_DroneStation_C properties : - path : mTransferSpeed op : multiply value : 2 # faster cargo load/unload - path : mStackTransferSize value : 4 # items moved per transfer tick - path : mTripPowerPerMeterCost op : multiply value : 0.5 # cheaper long-haul routes

sections.heading: Runtime actor patches (values that saves/archetypes would override)
sections.text: CDO edits only affect newly built actors when the value is serialised into the save. Placed buildings keep their saved values. applyToSpawnedActors re-applies the ops to every instance the moment it spawns: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/StorageContainerMk1/Build_StorageContainerMk1.Build_StorageContainerMk1_C applyToSpawnedActors : true # re-applied to every instance the moment it spawns applyToSubclasses : false # exact class only properties : - path : mInventorySizeX value : 12 - path : mInventorySizeY value : 8 All targeting modifiers are documented in Targeting . Belt speed, also a buildable patch but balance-flavored, lives in Balancing . To generate a brand-new building/buildable descriptor class instead of patching an existing one, see Type: building .

pages.title: Repeat-Purchase Schematic (KLIB)
pages.description: A complete UKLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases pack with generated cost and reward curves.

sections.heading: Full example: Repeat-Purchase Schematic
sections.text: UKLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases from KLib combines two float curves with an instanced schematic unlock. It makes its schematic repeatable, limits total purchases, changes complete reward and cost lists at selected purchase levels, adds one-time costs to exact levels, and scales those lists with curves. Rewards are deposited once into the Trading Post storage; overflow spawns in a crate beside it. Gate the pack on KLib because /Script/KLib.KLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases only exists while that mod is loaded. ref also determines generated curve object paths: pack.yml ref : RepeatRewards name : Repeatable Rewards version : 1.0.0 conditions : hasMod : KLib Create cost and reward multiplier curves in one Assets-stage document. Curve X is the number of completed purchases, so X=0 controls first purchase, X=1 second, and X=2 third: repeat-purchase-curves.curve.yml type : curve curveType : float curves : - id : RepeatPurchaseCost keys : - time : 0 value : 1 - time : 1 value : 2 - time : 2 value : 3 - id : RepeatPurchaseReward keys : - time : 0 value : 1 - time : 1 value : 2 - time : 2 value : 3 Reference both generated curves from one UKLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases instance: repeat-purchase.schematic.yml type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_RepeatableRewards properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Repeatable Rewards - path : mType value : EST_Milestone - path : mTechTier value : 3 - path : mTimeToComplete value : 30 - path : mCost value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount : 50 unlocks : - class : /Script/KLib.KLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases properties : - path : mMaxPurchaseCount value : 3 - path : mAmounts value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/CopperSheet/Desc_CopperSheet.Desc_CopperSheet_C Amount : 20 - path : mCostMultiplierCurve value : /KDataForge/GenAssets/RepeatRewards.Gen_RepeatRewards_RepeatPurchaseCost - path : mRewardMultiplierCurve value : /KDataForge/GenAssets/RepeatRewards.Gen_RepeatRewards_RepeatPurchaseReward - path : mRewardItemsByLevel value : - mPurchaseLevel : 2 mItemsToGive : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlateReinforced/Desc_IronPlateReinforced.Desc_IronPlateReinforced_C Amount : 5 mAdditionalCosts : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/Cable/Desc_Cable.Desc_Cable_C Amount : 10 - mPurchaseLevel : 3 mItemsToGive : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/Rotor/Desc_Rotor.Desc_Rotor_C Amount : 2 bOverrideCosts : true mCosts : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/ModularFrame/Desc_ModularFrame.Desc_ModularFrame_C Amount : 5 Result: Purchase Curve X Final cost Reward deposited into Trading Post storage 1 0 50 Iron Plates 20 Copper Sheets 2 1 100 Iron Plates + 20 Cable 10 Reinforced Iron Plates 3 2 15 Modular Frames 6 Rotors mAmounts and schematic mCost are level-one defaults. At each later purchase, mRewardItemsByLevel selects the highest mPurchaseLevel not above current 1-based purchase level. mItemsToGive replaces complete reward list. A level with bOverrideCosts: true replaces complete raw cost list from that level onward. mAdditionalCosts is added only when its mPurchaseLevel exactly matches current purchase; it does not carry into later levels. Both raw cost lists are combined before cost curve is applied, so 10 Cable becomes 20 on purchase 2. Rewards are granted once to Trading Post storage; any amount that does not fit spawns in an inventory crate beside storage. mMaxPurchaseCount: 3 prevents further repeat purchases. Values at or below zero mean unlimited. Null curve properties use multiplier 1. See Curves for curve field grammar and Schematics for generic unlocks: behavior.

sections.heading: Unlocks Catalog
sections.text: The Unlocks Catalog has been split into two pages: The complete UKLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases pack now lives at Repeat-Purchase Schematic (KLIB) . The base-game FGUnlock catalog now lives at Base-Game Unlock Classes .

pages.title: Features
pages.description: One page per capability KDataForge supports, the value you put after `type:` in a YAML document, plus the cross-cutting mechanics every document shares.

sections.heading: Features
sections.text: Every KDataForge YAML document starts with a type: field, and that single field decides which of the pages below covers it. type: item behaves nothing like type: gametag : each has its own entries key, its own load stage, and its own session-start behavior. This section gives every one of those type: values its own page, plus a handful of pages for mechanics that cut across all of them. Those cross-cutting pages cover the property codec every value: is parsed through, the 22 operations a patch can apply, the selectors that pick what gets patched, and the conditions/pack-manifest options that sit above any single document. Read a page here to understand what a capability does and why it is shaped the way it is . For complete packs that combine several capabilities, use Examples . Task Guides walk specific goals step by step. For normative field and API details, use Reference .

sections.heading: Patch mechanics
sections.text: type: cdo is the workhorse document that every other type either resembles or builds on internally. These five pages cover the parts that make a patch a patch: what a value looks like, what an operation does to it, how a target is selected, when a document applies at all, and how the pieces fit together in one patch entry. Property Types : every value shape the property codec accepts, including bool, all numeric widths, enums, strings, FText (plain and localized), object/class/soft references, all three struct forms, arrays, sets, maps, and gameplay tags. Operations : what each of the 22 op: values does and which property kinds accept it, covering numeric math and clamping, container mutation, string concatenation, array reordering, and cross-property copy/move. Targeting : every way to select what a patch applies to, a class CDO, a single asset instance, every asset of a class, tag matching, subclass expansion, and spawned-actor propagation. Conditions & Packs : conditions: for gating whether a document, a whole pack or a single list entry applies (including config: conditions), pack.yml manifest fields (description and icon), redirects: for safe id renames, and include: ordering between files in one pack. Patching (type: cdo) : how a patches: entry ties target selectors, modifiers, and a properties: list together, plus the current snapshot and restart boundaries.

sections.heading: Pack configuration and templates
sections.text: Two pages cover making a pack adjustable by players and reading live data from YAML. Pack Configuration : *.config.yml definitions with text, number, slider, boolean, select, multi-select, list and tag fields, categories, the values file players edit, hot and cold values, cold game properties, and how values reach clients in multiplayer. Templates and Typed References : cfg: references and {prefix:body} templates that read pack configuration, game settings, and properties or function results of game classes, with nesting, escaping and YAML quoting rules. For the Blueprint side see the Blueprint Config API , for the condition grammar Config Expressions , and for a guided build Player-Configurable Balancing .

sections.heading: Runtime documents
sections.text: Wwise Sounds : import pack-relative PCM16 WAV files as audio events for ADA voice-over and finite 2D playback. Complete ADA example . Two document types register something into a global engine system rather than patching an object directly. Both are unusual enough about when they take effect to deserve their own page. Game Tags : registering new gameplay tags at runtime, how that registration survives the engine’s tag-tree rebuilds, and why the GameTags stage always runs first. Localization : new or overridden display text per namespace and culture, source-hash matching for overrides, and culture prefix-matching rules.

sections.heading: World and startup control
sections.text: Two root types affect world content without generating a class. Both must run from matching packs on every multiplayer process. Resources and Resource Nodes : type: resourcenode removes matching world nodes by effective resource descriptor and optional node type, with explicit save-persistence and occupied-node safeguards. Sublevels : type: sublevel blocks selected RefinedRDLib or KBFL sublevel descriptor assets before their levels stream in. Removing Content : remove: on recipe , schematic , and research documents takes registered content out of the game, by exact class or by filter rule, with the save implications of each kind and how they combine.

sections.heading: Content creation
sections.text: These seven types generate a brand-new class at runtime, or, for the last three, register an existing one you didn’t generate. This is the actual “add new stuff to the game” side of KDataForge. All seven share the same id/parent/properties shape and the same save-stable generated-class identity. Items : generating new FGItemDescriptor classes, the parent/required-base rules, and the generated-class identity every other content-creation type shares. Resources and Resource Nodes : generating FGResourceDescriptor classes, patching node actor classes, scanner unlocks, and removing matching world nodes with type: resourcenode . Buildings : generating new building/buildable-descriptor classes, what a generated building actually is, and the hard limit on genuinely new meshes or components. Unlocks : generating a standalone, reusable FGUnlock subclass, and why a schematic’s own inline unlocks: list is what most packs actually want. Recipes : generating new recipes, registering existing recipe classes, and how registration into SML’s content registry actually happens. Schematics : generating new schematics/milestones, registering existing ones, and the instanced unlocks: list that wires a recipe up to a schematic. Research Trees : generating new M.A.M. research trees, registering existing ones, and why a schematic doesn’t “point at” a tree the way a recipe points at a schematic.

sections.heading: Sink points, the escape hatch, data assets, and curves
sections.text: These pages round out the type list with a narrow registry document, a general class escape hatch, object-instance assets, and Unreal curves. Sink Points : setting AWESOME Sink point values for items, its registration timing, and why this is separate from Resource Nodes. Custom Classes : generating a class of any kind from any parent (native or Blueprint), with optional registerAs: for the three registered kinds, the escape hatch beyond the preset types above. Data Assets : editing every KAPI PrimaryDataAsset type, creating new instances with type: dataasset , loading 2D images with type: asset , and RefinedR&D (RRDA) integration. Float and Vector Curves : creating or editing UCurveFloat and UCurveVector assets with key interpolation, tangents, defaults, and extrapolation. Tip Not sure which page you need? If you already know the type: value from a YAML file, jump straight to its page above. If you’re starting from a goal instead (“I want players to unlock a new item”), Task Guides walks the whole chain instead of making you piece it together from several of these pages yourself.

pages.title: Actor instance selectors
pages.description: Patch selected live actors by ordinary actor tags, world bounds, and their current production recipe.

sections.heading: Actor instance selectors
sections.text: Use actorSelector: inside a type: cdo patch to change selected actor instances without changing their class defaults. For example, change the power consumption of iron-ingot smelters inside a particular factory area while leaving other smelters alone. type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true actorSelector: sphere: center: [120000, -40000, 15000] radius: 25000 currentRecipe: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: - path: mPowerConsumption op: multiply value: 0.75 Replace the bounds with coordinates from your world. Coordinates and distances use Unreal world centimetres: 100 is one metre. The selector checks the actor origin, not its mesh or collision box. Use properties available on the target class in your game's reflection data. Property operations have the same constraints as ordinary CDO patches; changing a property does not automatically call a machine-specific setter or rebuild derived state.

sections.heading: Fields and matching
sections.text: At least one selector field is required. Every supplied field must match. | Field | Accepted value | Match | | tags | Non-empty string or non-empty list of non-empty strings | Actor has every listed ordinary AActor.Tags tag. | | sphere | Map with finite center: [x, y, z] and finite positive radius | Actor origin lies inside or on the sphere. | | box | Map with finite min: [x, y, z] and max: [x, y, z] | Actor origin lies inside or on the axis-aligned box. Each minimum must be smaller than its maximum. | | currentRecipe | Recipe class reference or non-empty list of recipe classes | Actor's current recipe equals any listed class. Subclasses do not match automatically. | tags uses ordinary actor tags, not gameplay tags. Tags must already exist on the instance; the selector does not add them. Tag names follow Unreal FName matching. Empty entries and None are rejected. Recipe references must resolve to FGRecipe subclasses. Actors without a compatible mCurrentRecipe class property, or without a selected recipe, do not match currentRecipe. Recipe classes must be available when the entry registers. If another document generates the recipe during this same load, add deferOneGameTick: true beside applyToSpawnedActors: true. This delays recipe resolution until after content generation, then visits existing actors too. This patch requires both actor tags and a box match: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true actorSelector: tags: [FactoryNorth, PowerBudget] box: min: [100000, -50000, 0] max: [140000, -10000, 30000] properties: - path: mPowerConsumption value: 2

sections.heading: Required patch settings
sections.text: - target: must resolve to an actor class, or a non-empty list of actor classes. Direct object and asset targets are rejected. All targets must resolve before the entry is registered. - applyToSpawnedActors: true is required. - applyToSubclasses defaults to false; enable it when targeting a native base class. - properties: must contain the operations to apply. - allAssetsOfClass, ofClass, matchAssets, tagProperty, and the CDO/asset filters cannot be combined with actorSelector. Use separate patch entries for CDO changes. - Unknown selector and bounds fields, malformed vectors, non-finite numbers, empty lists, and invalid bounds are rejected. Inspect /kdf report for diagnostics.

sections.heading: When changes apply
sections.text: Selectors run for actors already present when the world starts, actors spawned afterwards, and actors present after /kdf reload. Instance matching waits until the actor has begun play, so construction and save restoration finish before tags, location, and recipe are read. This is a lifecycle selector, not continuous monitoring. Moving an actor into a region, adding a tag, or selecting a different recipe later does not automatically apply or remove a patch. Reload to re-evaluate existing actors. A freshly built machine without a selected recipe cannot match a recipe selector at spawn; select the recipe, then reload. Each matching entry is applied at most once per actor between reloads. Repeated visits do not compound multiply, append, or similar operations. Different entries can still apply to the same actor, in pack/document order. Reload restores KDataForge's captured property baselines before matching and applying the current entries again. Removing an entry therefore restores its captured values on surviving actors during reload; this can also overwrite gameplay changes made to those same properties since the snapshot. If deferOneGameTick: true is present, deferred registration also visits existing actors without repeating entries already applied to them. Starting another reload cancels deferred work from the previous load, so a removed or edited entry cannot run afterwards from an old queue.

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: Selected actor operations run on the authoritative host or dedicated server. Clients receive changes only through replication already provided by the target actor/property. A selector does not make an unreplicated property replicate or add a client RPC. Use identical packs on host and clients, and verify the chosen property in multiplayer when its client presentation matters. See Targeting for class and asset selection, and Operations for the property-operation syntax.

pages.title: Type: building
pages.description: Generating new building/buildable descriptor classes from YAML, covering what you actually get and the hard limits on what a generated building can be.

sections.heading: Type: building
sections.text: This is the Items stage, at priority 20 , the last of the five generation types ( class → unlock → item → resource → building ). It loads changes only during session initialization, so changes need a restart. The entries key is buildings , and the default parent is /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildingDescriptor , which is also the required base class (or a subclass of it). Register-only mode ( class: ) is not supported here, use id: instead. Don’t confuse this with editing an existing buildable’s stats. That’s a plain cdo patch, and it’s the far more common thing to want (see Power & Machines and Type: cdo ). type: building is specifically for creating a new FGBuildingDescriptor -derived class: a genuinely new entry in the build menu, not a tweak to one that already exists.

sections.heading: Read this before you start: the hard constraint
sections.text: A generated class copies its parent’s layout exactly: same components, same mesh slots, same everything except CDO default values. type: building is worth reaching for when you want a second build-menu entry for an existing buildable, with its own display name and description. Players can then have both the original and the new entry at once. The placed building stays the parent’s actor, unchanged. It is not a way to add a new mesh, a new component, or genuinely new behaviour: a generated class has no new reflected properties and no new components beyond what the parent already defines. KDataForge is also 2D-only by design, so there’s no way to bring in new meshes either. For a new mesh, new component, or new gameplay behaviour, you need actual C++/Blueprint content: type: building can’t get you there.

sections.heading: Worked example: a second Storage Container entry
sections.text: A building document’s buildings: entries follow the same id / parent / properties shape as every other generation type. id names the new descriptor, parent is the existing descriptor class it clones the layout from, and properties applies CDO overrides to the clone. Here a plain Storage Container Mk1 gets a second build-menu entry with its own name and description: type : building buildings : - id : CrimsonStorage parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/StorageContainerMk1/Desc_StorageContainerMk1.Desc_StorageContainerMk1_C properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Crimson Storage Container - path : mDescription value : A second Storage Container Mk1 entry in the build menu. This generates /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_CrimsonStorage , a new FGBuildingDescriptor subclass. The mDisplayName and mDescription overrides apply to the descriptor only. The generated class adds no mesh, no components, and no capacity or paint change. Placing it spawns the parent’s actor, Build_StorageContainerMk1_C , exactly as it is. The entry only appears in the build menu once a recipe and schematic unlock it (see Troubleshooting).

sections.heading: Practical note: descriptor vs. buildable
sections.text: FactoryGame splits “the thing in your build menu” ( UFGBuildingDescriptor , what this document generates) from “the thing placed in the world” ( AFGBuildable* , the actor). Parenting a building entry must be a descriptor. Desc_StorageContainerMk1 is an FGBuildingDescriptor whose mBuildableClass points at the Build_StorageContainerMk1 actor, so the generated descriptor places that same actor. Giving the actor path ( Build_*_C ) as parent: is an error: kdf lint reports it and suggests the matching Desc_*_C , and the game refuses the entry when the pack loads. Your mDisplayName and mDescription overrides change the build-menu entry only. Actor-only properties such as mInventorySizeX belong to the actor ( FGBuildableStorage ) and are not valid on a descriptor. You’re not generating a new AFGBuildable subclass, and for a simple variant you never need to. When you do want a separate buildable class, with its own CDO defaults on the actor and its own save identity, generate one from an existing Build_*_C parent with type: class and point the descriptor’s mBuildableClass at it. The full chain (buildable → descriptor → build recipe → production recipes → schematic → sinkpoints) is walked step by step in A Complete Building .

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: The new building doesn’t show up in the build menu at all : check /kdf report first. If the class generated successfully but you don’t see it, this is very likely a build menu category or recipe registration question, not the building document itself. A building descriptor needs a recipe (see Type: recipe ) that produces it, and a schematic that unlocks that recipe before it becomes buildable in a fresh game. Stats didn’t change : same rule as everywhere else. An unsupported op or a bad path: is a diagnostic, never a silent failure, and /kdf report tells you exactly which patch failed. Want to bulk-tune a whole family of existing buildings instead (all miners, all belts, all generators)? That’s applyToSubclasses: on a plain cdo patch. See Targeting .

pages.title: Category Ordering
pages.description: Assign menu categories and deterministic one-based ordering to items, recipes, schematics, and user settings.

sections.heading: Category Ordering
sections.text: type: category_reorder keeps category placement separate from general cdo patches. One document selects a content kind, assigns one main category and optional subcategory, then writes priorities from the order array: first entry gets 1, second gets 2, and so on. type: category_reorder subType: items category: /Game/MyMod/Categories/Cat_Pipelines.Cat_Pipelines_C subCategory: /Game/MyMod/Categories/SC_SpecialPipes.SC_SpecialPipes_C categoryPriority: 4 subCategoryPriority: 2 order: - /Game/MyMod/Pipes/Desc_PipeMk1.Desc_PipeMk1_C - /Game/MyMod/Pipes/Desc_PipeMk2.Desc_PipeMk2_C The handler runs in CDOChanges after ordinary cdo handlers. This makes the declared array the final category order even when another patch previously changed the same priority fields.

sections.heading: Supported subtypes
sections.text: | subType | order entries | Main category | Subcategory | Priority field | | items | UFGItemDescriptor class paths, including buildings and equipment | UFGCategory | optional UFGCategory | mMenuPriority | | recipe | UFGRecipe class paths, including customization recipes | UFGItemCategory | not supported | mManufacturingMenuPriority | | schematic | UFGSchematic class paths | UFGSchematicCategory | optional UFGSchematicCategory | mMenuPriority | | settings | UFGUserSetting asset paths | UFGUserSettingCategory | optional UFGUserSettingCategory | WidgetsToCreate[0].MenuPriority | items, recipe, and schematic entries are class paths and normally end in _C. settings entries are Primary Data Asset object paths and do not end in _C.

sections.heading: Settings preserve other placements
sections.text: A user setting can appear in more than one menu location. category_reorder updates only WidgetsToCreate[0].CategoryClass, optional SubCategoryClass, and MenuPriority. It does not replace the array, change later placements, or change SubOptionTo links. The setting must already have a WidgetsToCreate[0] entry. Use a general cdo object patch when creating a placement from scratch. type: category_reorder subType: settings category: /Game/MyMod/Settings/Cat_Gameplay.Cat_Gameplay_C subCategory: /Game/MyMod/Settings/SC_Logistics.SC_Logistics_C order: - /Game/MyMod/Settings/US_PipeHints.US_PipeHints - /Game/MyMod/Settings/US_AutoConnect.US_AutoConnect

sections.heading: Category priorities
sections.text: categoryPriority changes mMenuPriority on the main category class. subCategoryPriority does the same for subCategory and therefore requires that field. Both accept fractional values. Omitting subCategory leaves each target's existing subcategory unchanged. Supplying it replaces the subcategory list for items and schematics with one entry; settings update only the first menu placement. Recipes reject both subcategory fields because UFGRecipe has no equivalent property. Every order array must be non-empty and contain unique paths. Missing class targets are watched and applied if their class loads later. Settings are asset instances, so an unresolved settings path is reported as an error instead of becoming a class-load watch.

pages.title: Conditions & Packs
pages.description: Every condition form for gating whether a document applies, pack manifest options, id redirects, and include: ordering between files in the same pack.

sections.heading: Conditions & Packs
sections.text: Two mechanisms sit above the individual document types covered elsewhere in this section. The conditions: block decides whether a single document applies at all. The pack.yml manifest describes the folder of documents around it: a stable ref for save persistence, a load-order priority, and optional dependencies on other packs. Both are cross-cutting, so they work the same way no matter which document type: ( cdo , item , gametag , …) they’re attached to.

sections.heading: Conditions: gating whether a document applies at all
sections.text: A conditions: block lets a document skip itself when the environment doesn’t match: a required mod isn’t loaded, the game version is too old, or a class from another mod doesn’t exist. It accepts one object or an array of objects. Keys inside each object are AND-combined; conditionBehaivor selects AND or OR across objects and defaults to AND . Ranges use SML’s semver syntax ( >= , ^ , ~ , exact versions, || unions). The example below exercises every supported key, including both the scalar and sequence forms of hasMod / hasClass : type : cdo conditions : gameVersion : ' >=1.0.0 ' # semver range vs FactoryGame version hasMod : KAPI # single mod (loaded check) # hasMod: # sequence ALL must be loaded # - KAPI # - RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 # inline version constraint modVersion : # explicit version map form SML : ' >=3.12.0 ' KAPI : ' >=2026.0.0 ' hasClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator # hasClass: # sequence ALL must exist # - /Game/FicsitFarming/Buildable/FarmPlot/Build_FarmPlot.Build_FarmPlot_C patches : - target : /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator properties : - path : mDefaultPotentialExtractionPerMinute op : multiply value : 1.5 The map form above remains the compact form for ordinary positive conditions. Use an array of condition objects when some requirements must match and another must not match: conditionBehaivor : AND # optional; AND is the default conditions : - hasMod : - KAPI - KLib # both mods must be loaded - hasMod : IncompatibleMod # this object must NOT match ifNotMatch : true - hasMod : ' OptionalIntegration@^2.0.0 ' # reject only matching 2.x versions ifNotMatch : true Keys inside each object are AND-combined, then ifNotMatch: true negates that object’s combined result. conditionBehaivor combines the resulting objects and accepts AND or OR (case-insensitive); it defaults to AND . Correctly spelled conditionBehavior is accepted as an alias. Therefore, the example applies only when KAPI and KLib are loaded, IncompatibleMod is absent, and OptionalIntegration is either absent or outside ^2.0.0 . Inversion applies to the whole object, not each list entry. To reject several mods independently, put each hasMod check in its own object with ifNotMatch: true . Invalid keys, value types, or version ranges are configuration errors and are never converted into matches by inversion. Use OR when any one condition object may enable the document: conditionBehaivor : OR conditions : - hasMod : RefinedPower - hasMod : FicsitFarming This applies when RefinedPower, FicsitFarming, or both are loaded. ifNotMatch still runs per object before OR combines the results. Invalid behavior values or malformed condition objects always fail closed, even when another OR object matches. With an empty condition array, AND passes and OR does not. Failing conditions skip the document with an Info -severity diagnostic. However, /kdf report filters Info diagnostics out of its printed output entirely, so a condition skip is currently not visible there. The only signal is a lower-than-expected “document(s) applied” count. See Debugging a Pack That Won’t Apply for the workaround.

sections.heading: Conditions that read pack configuration: config:
sections.text: config: is one more key of a condition object. Its value is an expression over the fields of your pack configuration and over game settings, or a list of expressions that must all be true. It combines with hasMod , gameVersion , modVersion , hasClass , ifNotMatch and conditionBehaivor like any other key. gated.cdo.yml type : cdo conditions : - hasMod : KAPI - config : features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed >= 2 patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.9 A config: condition works in pack.yml , in a document’s conditions: , and on single entries of lists (next section). It does not work inside a config definition file. Two practical rules: Conditions on a whole pack, or on documents that generate content ( item , recipe , schematic , …), run at load time. Use a cold field there. A hot field works through /kdf reload but is reported as restart advised , and the editor warns with config.hot-in-condition . Hot fields are the right choice for conditions on entries inside cdo patches, data assets and operation lists, which are re-applied on every reload. A pack that its own config: condition switched off still lists its settings (marked as not active), so a player can switch it back on. session: and ags: settings do not exist on the main menu; a config: condition that reads one is not an error there, the pack or document is deferred until a save is loaded ( ifNotMatch: true does not turn such an unknown value into a match). modules.config.yml type : config category : SampleFeaturesCategory fields : - id : modules.enableBalance type : boolean name : Enable the balance module description : Turns the rebalancing documents of this pack on or off. Needs a restart. default : true pack.yml ref : KDFSample name : KDataForge Sample Pack version : 1.0.0 conditions : config : modules.enableBalance

sections.heading: Conditions on single list entries
sections.text: The keys conditions , conditionBehavior and conditionBehaivor are allowed on any map entry of any list , at any depth: operations, patches, ingredients, unlocks, nodes, members of a value payload, and so on. Before the document is applied, an entry whose condition is false is removed; for an entry whose condition is true, the condition keys are stripped. An entry condition that fails to evaluate removes the entry and logs an error. gated-ingredients.recipe.yml type : recipe recipes : - id : Recipe_GatedPlate parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronPlate.Recipe_IronPlate_C properties : - path : mIngredients value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount : 3 - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/Screw/Desc_Screw.Desc_Screw_C Amount : 2 conditions : config : features.enableBonus # only present while the bonus is on Entry conditions accept the same keys as document conditions. Limits: they are not looked for inside conditions: blocks, an entry-level hasClass cannot see classes that KDataForge itself generates, and operands of where: filters resolve cfg: references but not apply-time templates.

sections.heading: pack.yml: the pack manifest
sections.text: A pack.yml at a detected pack root turns it into a named pack instead of the loader’s fallback. The implicit ref and name come from the detected root’s parent directory. The manifest gives a group of documents a stable identity across saves, a load-order priority relative to other packs, and dependency ordering. The fields below are read directly by the pack scanner: ref : MyOverhaul # stable ref the save-persistence and conflict-report contract name : My Overhaul Pack version : 2.1.0 description : A short, player-facing summary of what the pack changes. # optional; shown by settings screens icon : icon.png # optional; pack-relative png/jpg/jpeg/tga/bmp or a /Game/... texture path priority : 200 # higher than default (100) → applies earlier in every stage enabled : true conditionBehaivor : AND # optional; controls condition-object aggregation dependencies : - KDFSample # packs that must load before this one conditions : # same grammar/evaluator as a document's conditions: see above hasMod : RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 description is a string or a localized {key, ns, source} map. icon is a file inside the pack folder ( png , jpg , jpeg , tga or bmp ; a path that leaves the folder is rejected) or an object path of a UTexture2D that starts with / . Both are shown by pack settings screens, see Pack Configuration . The editor reports a missing icon file as pack.icon-missing . dependencies: are hard ordering constraints. A pack is rejected if a dependency is missing, self-referential, or already invalid; that rejection propagates to transitive dependants. Packs in a dependency cycle are also rejected. The remaining packs are topologically ordered so every dependency runs first. Among packs whose dependencies are ready, priority descending is the tie-break, followed by ref ascending. priority defaults to 100.

sections.heading: pack.yml conditions: gating a whole pack
sections.text: pack.yml accepts the exact same conditions: map-or-array and evaluator as a document. Every key from Conditions: gating whether a document applies at all above ( gameVersion , hasMod , modVersion , hasClass ) plus condition arrays, ifNotMatch , and conditionBehaivor works here unchanged. It’s evaluated once, before any file in the pack is even read . A failing pack is skipped entirely with a single Info -severity diagnostic naming the pack, instead of every document in it failing its own copy of the same condition: pack.yml ref : MyRefinedPowerAddon name : My RefinedPower Addon version : 1.0.0 conditions : - hasMod : RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 - hasMod : LegacyRefinedPowerBridge ifNotMatch : true This whole pack loads only when RefinedPower 4.0+ is present and LegacyRefinedPowerBridge is not loaded. Use pack conditions for “this whole pack is a compat/addon layer for mod X” instead of repeating a conditions: block with hasMod: X at the top of every document. A document can still carry its own conditions: on top of the pack’s. Pack and document gates must both pass; each gate uses its own conditionBehaivor value.

sections.heading: redirects: renaming generated-content ids
sections.text: Generated class names are id-based ( Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> ), so renaming an id would orphan save data. A redirects: entry in pack.yml feeds FCoreRedirects so old class paths in existing saves resolve to the renamed class. Renaming a file never needs a redirect. Only id renames do: ref : MyOverhaul name : My Overhaul Pack version : 3.0.0 redirects : OldItemId : NewItemId # OldId: NewId Full worked example (rename MySuperIngot → SuperIngotMk2 across a save): End-to-End Pack → Renaming an id .

sections.heading: include: file ordering inside a pack
sections.text: Documents in the same stage use deterministic relative-path order unless include: adds an ordering constraint. List another file’s path under include: (relative to the pack root) when this document must apply after it, even though both stay in the same stage: overrides/late-tweaks.cdo.yml type : cdo include : - base/base-values.cdo.yml # relative to the pack root; applies first (same stage) patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply # multiplies the value base-values.cdo.yml already set value : 2.0

sections.heading: Tags registered elsewhere in the same pack
sections.text: A gametag document doesn’t need include: ordering against the documents that use its tags. The GameTags stage always runs before every other stage, so a tag registered anywhere in a pack is already usable via matchTag: or tag-container ops in that same pack’s cdo documents. The full syntax for registering tags, how registration survives the engine’s tag-tree rebuilds, and worked examples of tagging content and then bulk-patching by tag all live on their own page: Type: gametag .

pages.title: Float and Vector Curves
pages.description: Create and edit UCurveFloat and UCurveVector assets with keys, interpolation, tangents, defaults, and extrapolation.

sections.heading: Float and Vector Curves
sections.text: type: curve creates or edits Unreal curve assets during the Assets stage. Set curveType: float for UCurveFloat or curveType: vector for UCurveVector . Every entry uses exactly one selector. id: creates a runtime asset at /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> and announces it to the asset registry. target: loads and edits an existing cooked curve by object path. A generated curve from the current pack can also be addressed by its bare id. The keys: list replaces all existing keys on that curve.

sections.heading: Float curves
sections.text: type : curve curveType : float curves : - id : DamageFalloff defaultValue : 0 preInfinityExtrap : constant postInfinityExtrap : linear isEventCurve : false keys : - time : 0 value : 1 interpMode : constant - time : 10 value : 0.5 interpMode : cubic tangentMode : user arriveTangent : -0.05 leaveTangent : -0.05 Reference generated curve from any object property: value : /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_DamageFalloff

sections.heading: Repeat-purchase schematic (KLIB)
sections.text: KLib’s UKLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases can consume generated float curves for level-dependent costs and rewards. See the full combined example for pack gating, both curve assets, complete schematic YAML, and calculated purchase results.

sections.heading: Vector curves
sections.text: Vector values and tangent fields accept an X / Y / Z map or a three-number sequence. One key defines all three component curves at same time and with same interpolation metadata. type : curve curveType : vector curves : - id : CameraOffset defaultValue : X : 0 Y : 0 Z : 0 keys : - time : 0 value : X : 0 Y : 0 Z : 0 - time : 1 value : - 100 - 0 - 50 interpMode : cubic tangentMode : auto

sections.heading: Editing an existing curve
sections.text: type : curve curveType : float conditions : hasMod : SomeMod curves : - target : /SomeMod/Curves/Curve_ProductionRate.Curve_ProductionRate keys : - time : 0 value : 1 - time : 60 value : 2 target: must resolve to class selected by curveType . A float document cannot edit a UCurveVector , and a vector document cannot edit a UCurveFloat .

sections.heading: Key and curve fields
sections.text: Field Accepted values Default time finite number, unique within entry required value finite number for float, X/Y/Z value for vector required interpMode constant , linear , cubic linear tangentMode auto , smartAuto , user , break auto tangentWeightMode none , arrive , leave , both none arriveTangent , leaveTangent float or X/Y/Z value 0 arriveTangentWeight , leaveTangentWeight float or X/Y/Z value 0 Entry-level preInfinityExtrap and postInfinityExtrap accept none , constant , linear , cycle , cycleWithOffset , or oscillate . defaultValue uses same shape as key values. isEventCurve is valid only for float curves.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Curve type mismatch: Confirm object path points to UCurveFloat or UCurveVector matching document curveType . Duplicate time: Each entry can contain only one key per time. File order does not matter. KDataForge sorts keys before applying them. Reference does not resolve: Generated curve assets have no _C suffix. Use exact /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> object path. Existing keys disappeared: Replacement is intentional. Include every key that must remain. See YAML Schema for normative field grammar.

pages.title: Type: class
pages.description: Generating classes of any kind from YAML, any parent (C++ or Blueprint), optional content registration via registerAs, and where the preset types stop and this escape hatch begins.

sections.heading: Type: class
sections.text: This type runs first in the Items stage at priority 50 , ahead of unlock , item , resource , and building . Later generation types can therefore use a custom generated class as their parent, and recipe , schematic , and research can reference it. Changes load during session initialization, so restart after editing YAML. Its entries key is classes . There is no default parent , so every entry must set parent: explicitly. There is no required base class either: every parent works, whether native C++ or Blueprint. Register-only mode ( class: ) is not supported; use id: instead, and register existing classes via Type: recipe , schematic , or research . The preset types ( item , resource , building , unlock , recipe , schematic , research ) remain the recommended, ergonomic forms. They pick the right parent, stage priority, and registration for you. class is the escape hatch for everything else: equipment descriptors, vehicle descriptors, item and schematic categories, FGUnlock subclasses, custom classes from other mods gated behind hasMod , reparented buildables, and any other class kind KDataForge has no preset for. type : class debug : true # optional log every applied op (see Getting Started → Debugging) classes : - id : MyCustomThing parent : /Script/FactoryGame.FGEquipmentDescriptor # ANY class: native C++ or /Game/...Thing_C registerAs : recipe # OPTIONAL: recipe | schematic | research queues SML content # registration for kinds that need it; omit for everything else properties : - path : mDisplayName value : My Equipment # cdo-style op entries applied to the new class's CDO Everything that holds for the preset generation types holds here too: Same save-stable identity : package /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef> , class Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> . Reference it elsewhere as /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> . The global manifest, tombstone reconstruction, and redirects: in pack.yml all apply.
