Layout-copy constraint : the generated class copies the parent’s layout exactly, with no new reflected properties and no new components. All variation lives in the CDO defaults that properties: sets. registerAs: is only for the three kinds SML’s UModContentRegistry tracks: recipe , schematic , and research . If you generate one of those through class instead of the preset type, set it so registration is queued. Everything else, such as descriptors, categories, and unlocks, just needs to exist and be referenced.

sections.heading: Example 1: an equipment descriptor from a C++ parent
sections.text: my-equipment.class.yml type : class classes : - id : Desc_MyGadget parent : /Script/FactoryGame.FGEquipmentDescriptor properties : - path : mDisplayName value : key : MyGadget_Name ns : MyPack source : Portable Gadget - path : mStackSize value : SS_ONE # equipment is conventionally non-stacking - path : mEquipmentClass value : /Game/FactoryGame/Equipment/JetPack/Equip_JetPack.Equip_JetPack_C The result is a real UFGEquipmentDescriptor subclass, usable in recipes, schematics, and sinkpoints like any other descriptor. Because of the layout-copy constraint, mEquipmentClass has to point at an existing equipment actor, here the jetpack. You are re-parametrising existing equipment behaviour, not writing new equipment logic.

sections.heading: Example 2: a build-menu / item category
sections.text: There is no preset type for categories, which makes them the textbook class use case: my-category.class.yml type : class classes : - id : Cat_MyPackParts parent : /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemCategory properties : - path : mDisplayName value : key : Cat_MyPackParts_Name ns : MyPack source : MyPack Parts - path : mMenuPriority value : 999 Point generated items at it from the same pack. The Items stage guarantees the category class exists before any later stage references it. Within the stage, include: orders documents when one Items-stage document needs another: type : item include : - my-category.class.yml # the category must generate before this item references it items : - id : MySuperGadgetPart properties : - path : mCategory value : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Cat_MyPackParts

sections.heading: Example 3: a modded parent class, gated behind hasMod
sections.text: Any loaded mod’s classes work as parents. Gate the document so it is skipped cleanly (Info diagnostic) when the mod is missing: ff-crop.class.yml type : class conditions : hasMod : FicsitFarming classes : - id : Desc_MyCustomCrop parent : /Game/FicsitFarming/Descriptors/Crops/Desc_Berry.Desc_Berry_C # Blueprint parent properties : - path : mDisplayName value : My Custom Crop

sections.heading: registerAs: (generating a registered kind through class )
sections.text: If you generate a recipe, schematic, or research class via class , for example because you want a specific modded subclass as the parent, queue its registration with registerAs: . It does exactly what the preset type’s default register: true does: type : class classes : - id : Recipe_MySpecial parent : /Game/SomeMod/Recipes/Recipe_SpecialBase.Recipe_SpecialBase_C registerAs : recipe # queued into UModContentRegistry before the freeze properties : - path : mDisplayName value : My Special Recipe

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: “parent is required” : unlike the preset types, class has no default parent. Every entry needs an explicit parent: . “My generated recipe/schematic never shows up” : you generated it via class without registerAs: . Only the preset types register automatically. class registers nothing unless you ask. Wanting new components, meshes, or logic : not possible. See the layout-copy constraint above and the honest scope callout in A Complete Building . Preset-type pages for the ergonomic forms: Type: item , Type: recipe , Type: schematic , Type: building .

pages.title: Data Assets
pages.description: Editing KAPI data asset types, creating new UDataAsset instances with type dataasset, loading 2D images with type asset, and RefinedR&D (RRDA) mod integration.

sections.heading: Data Assets
sections.text: Most of the reference pages nearby cover generated classes such as buildings, recipes, and schematics. Data assets are different: they are UDataAsset instances , meaning objects rather than classes. KDataForge accepts any UDataAsset subclass for type: dataasset . KAPI and many RefinedR&D assets are UPrimaryDataAsset subclasses, so consumer subsystems can discover them through the asset registry and rescan them after KDataForge creates or edits instances. KDataForge can both edit existing instances, using plain cdo documents just like any other object, and create brand-new ones with type: dataasset . Use dataasset when a mod needs a fresh instance rather than an edit to an existing one. This page also covers the other asset-stage document, type: asset , which loads 2D images from your pack folder into real textures that you can point icon properties at.

sections.heading: Editing KAPI data assets
sections.text: KAPI is the biggest single consumer of PrimaryDataAsset instances in the mod ecosystem. It drives modular miners, cleaner buildings, air collectors, manufacturer tuning, slug breeding, extractor allow-lists, and tooltip injection entirely from data assets rather than code. This lets other mods, including KDataForge packs, retune all of it without touching KAPI’s own source. Because they’re ordinary UObject instances, KDataForge reaches them with the exact same three selectors documented in Targeting : target: with the asset object path (note: no _C suffix, since these are instances, not classes). allAssetsOfClass: to patch every asset of a given KAPI type at once. matchTag: + ofClass: to select by gameplay tag. KAPI assets carry their tags on mTags and are read like any other IGameplayTagAssetInterface object, so tags match directly.

sections.heading: UKAPIDataAssetBase : common base properties
sections.text: Every KAPI data asset instance, whatever its concrete type, inherits the same handful of admin fields from UKAPIDataAssetBase . There’s a display mName and mDescription (both FText , shown in whatever UI surfaces the asset), an mIcon (soft texture reference), a hard on/off switch mIsDisabled , a tie-break mPriority ( int32 , where higher wins when more than one asset could apply), and mTags ( FGameplayTagContainer ), the same field matchTag: reads. Because these five fields exist on every KAPI asset, a single patch document can disable one specific asset by path while also bulk-adjusting every asset carrying a particular tag: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : # Disable one specific KAPI data asset by object path: - target : /KLib/Assets/MinerDescriptions/DA_MinerDesc_Iron.DA_MinerDesc_Iron properties : - path : mIsDisabled value : true # Bump priority on every KAPI asset tagged as event-only: - matchTag : KMods.EventOnly ofClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPIDataAssetBase properties : - path : mPriority op : add value : 100

sections.heading: UKAPIModularMinerDescription : modular miner resources
sections.text: Each instance describes one resource variant that a KAPI modular miner can extract: which resource class it targets, what item it actually produces, which drill and scanner tiers and which modules are required or excluded, and its fluid coolant/byproduct behavior. The mResourceClass field is the asset’s identity. Never set it to none , since KAPI hard-crashes on a null resource class (see the key-field warning below). Retuning throughput across every modular miner resource at once is a single allAssetsOfClass patch: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPIModularMinerDescription properties : - path : mNormalFluidCountPerSecond op : multiply value : 1.5 Other properties on this type worth knowing about: mProductionItem , mDrillTier , mScannerTier , mNeededModules , mPreventModules , mModuleInformation , mFluidInfo , mTryProductionDynamic , mTrashItem , mIsFallbackDescriptor , mFoundText , mRarityText , mNodeScreenshot .

sections.heading: UKAPICleanerItemDescription : cleaner recipes
sections.text: This is effectively a recipe for KAPI’s cleaner building: an input fluid, an optional item that gets consumed alongside it, a production time, and the item(s) produced in return. mInFluid is a struct rather than a class reference, so its nested ItemClass member is the actual key field. Keeping mInFluid.ItemClass valid matters exactly the same way mResourceClass does on a miner description. Multiplying mProductionTime and clamping the input fluid amount both work as ordinary numeric ops, including through the nested path: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties : - path : mProductionTime op : multiply value : 0.75 - path : mInFluid.Amount # nested struct member on an asset instance op : max value : 1000 Other properties: mOutFluid , mNeedCleanItem , mProduceItem , mProduceAmount , mBypassProducts , mCleanerItemInfo .

sections.heading: UKAPIAirCollectorData : air collector production
sections.text: Air collectors harvest a resource passively over time from the surrounding air rather than from a node. This asset governs how much: production per hit, a hit cap, the trace range used to scan for valid targets, and min/max output bounds around a base count. clamp is the natural op for a range-scan property like mRangeToScan , since it lets you pin the value inside sane bounds in one step instead of chaining min / max : type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPIAirCollectorData properties : - path : mProduceItemCountMax op : add value : 2 - path : mRangeToScan op : clamp min : 1000 max : 50000 Other properties: mItemClass , mActorClass , mProductionTime , mProductionPerHit , mMaxHit , mTraceChannel , mRecipePrio , mProduceItemCountBase , mProduceItemCountMin .

sections.heading: UKAPIManufacturerModifications : manufacturer I/O tuning
sections.text: Rather than editing every recipe a manufacturer building runs, this asset lets you scale an entire building class’s throughput at once. Solid, fluid, and gas connections each get their own multiplier, plus there are separate slot-icon overrides for solid and fluid connectors. It’s the tool of choice when the goal is “every recipe on this building runs faster/slower” instead of “this one recipe”: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPIManufacturerModifications properties : - path : mSolidMultiplier op : multiply value : 2 Other properties: mTargetClass , mInput , mOutput , mFluidMultiplier , mGasMultiplier , mSolidSlotIcons , mFluidSlotIcons .

sections.heading: UKAPISugHatchingData : slug breeding/hatching
sections.text: This is the largest KAPI data asset type by property count, since it drives a full breeding-simulation mechanic. It covers which slug and egg pair it describes, breeding/hatching/die durations, the environmental comfort window (heat, humidity, compatible neighbors) the pair needs, food and fluid/power consumption rates, incubator/tank tier requirements, and the output counts and odds for the resulting eggs or slugs. Breeding time and hatch chance are the two levers most packs touch first: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPISugHatchingData properties : - path : mBreedingTime op : multiply value : 0.5 - path : mChance op : max value : 0.1 The full property set: mSlug , mEgg , mEggColor , mSlugTier , mChance , mProbability , mHatchDuration , mDieTime , mDayTime , mMinHeat / mMaxHeat , mMinHumidity / mMaxHumidity , mComfortableWith , mRequiredFood , mFoodConsumePerCycle , mFoodDuration , mFluidClass , mFluidConsume , mFluidConsumeTime , mPowerConsume , mIncubatorTier , mTankTier , mProductionCount , mProductionCountEggs , mFixedChanceMultiplier , mPossibleSlugs .

sections.heading: UKAPIExtractorAllowList : scanner/extractor allow lists
sections.text: Rather than a per-resource property, this asset is a compatibility table: which resource types a given extractor building is allowed (or explicitly disallowed) to mine, and the mirror image of which extractors a given resource accepts. That makes it the right place to hook up a new resource type, or a new miner added by another mod, so they recognize each other. Do this by appending to the relevant list instead of replacing it wholesale: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPIExtractorAllowList properties : - path : mAllowedExtractors op : append value : - /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/MinerMk3/Build_MinerMk3.Build_MinerMk3_C Other properties: mAllowedResources , mDisallowResources , mDisallowExtractors .

sections.heading: UKAPTooltipWidgetInjector : tooltip widget injection
sections.text: This one doesn’t tune gameplay numbers at all. It injects an extra UI widget into item tooltips for a filtered set of classes, at a chosen position in the tooltip’s widget list. mWidgetClass is the key field here (the widget that actually gets inserted), so it carries the same never-null guarantee as mResourceClass and mInFluid.ItemClass above: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPTooltipWidgetInjector properties : - path : mInjectAtIndex value : 0 Other properties: mClassFilter .

sections.heading: FKDFRandomData note & key-field warning
sections.text: FKAPIRandomData (with its mProbability field) appears nested inside several of the asset types above rather than as its own top-level asset. Edit it the same way as any other nested struct member, through a dotted path like mSomething.mProbability . ⚠️ KAPI crashes intentionally (fgcheck) when a key field is null: mResourceClass on miner descriptions, mInFluid.ItemClass on cleaner items, mWidgetClass on tooltip injectors. Never set these to none . Use mIsDisabled: true to turn an asset off instead.

sections.heading: KMods native gameplay tags
sections.text: KAPI registers a handful of gameplay tags itself at startup, so they’re usable in matchTag: (and in any tag-container op) immediately, without your pack needing its own gametag document first. These are KMods.ExcludeFromNodeRandomization , KMods.Disabled , KMods.AlternateRecipe , KMods.PlannerExclude , KMods.WikiExclude , KMods.Deprecated , KMods.WIP , KMods.Cheat , and KMods.EventOnly . Since mTags lives on the common UKAPIDataAssetBase , any of them works as a matchTag: selector across every KAPI asset type shown above, not just the one it was originally meant for: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : KAPI patches : - matchTag : KMods.Cheat # hide all cheat-tagged KAPI content ofClass : /Script/KAPI.KAPIDataAssetBase properties : - path : mIsDisabled value : true See Game Tags for how matchTag: and tag-container ops work in general, and Tag-Based Bulk Balancing for a full worked example built around this exact tag list.

sections.heading: Creating new instances: type: dataasset
sections.text: Editing only gets you so far. Sometimes a pack genuinely needs a new data asset instance that doesn’t exist yet, such as a new modular miner resource, a new cleaner recipe, or a new slug pairing. A dataasset document creates a real UDataAsset instance at runtime in package /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef> under a save-stable name Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> , and announces it to the asset registry. Primary-asset behavior still belongs to the chosen class; if the class derives from UPrimaryDataAsset , consumers that scan the registry for that asset type can pick the new instance up on their next scan: cleaner.dataasset.yml type : dataasset conditions : hasMod : KAPI assets : - id : CleanerItem_MyFluid class : /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription # any UDataAsset subclass properties : - path : mProductionTime value : 4.0 - path : mInFluid value : ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount : 1000 dataasset runs in the Assets stage, the second stage in the pipeline, right after GameTags and before Localization / CDOChanges . This means a generated instance already exists by the time any later cdo , item , or recipe document in the same load needs to reference it. YAML changes are loaded on the next session start. The same example appears inside the end-to-end pack in End-to-End Pack . There it sits next to the item/recipe/schematic files it belongs with. Remember: dataasset is only for creating new instances. Existing data assets, whether UPrimaryDataAsset or plain UDataAsset , are already editable via the cdo selectors shown above. There’s no need to “recreate” one just to change a value on it.

sections.heading: 2D image assets: type: asset
sections.text: Generated items and buildings need icons, and those icons have to come from somewhere. Your pack doesn’t ship a .uasset , it ships a plain image file instead. An asset document loads an image file shipped inside your pack and turns it into a real, referenceable UTexture2D . This is the missing piece for giving generated content its own icon instead of borrowing one from an existing item: <your-mod>/DataForge/ pack.yml # ref: MyPack icons/ my-icon.png my-icons.asset.yml my-icons.asset.yml type : asset assets : - id : MyIcon file : icons/my-icon.png # relative to the pack root; png / jpg / tga / bmp The result is a transient UTexture2D at /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> , announced to the asset registry the same way a dataasset instance is: Image changes are decoded on the next session start. file: is pack-relative. Absolute paths and .. traversal outside the pack are rejected. The texture object stays stable for the running GameInstance. A new session recreates the transient object and resolves YAML references again. 2D only : no FBX/glTF, ever (design policy). Only PNG, JPG/JPEG, TGA, and BMP are decoded today. DDS and WAV aren’t supported yet, and an unrecognized extension fails validation with the supported-format list in the error message.

sections.heading: Using a loaded image as an item icon
sections.text: Point any object-reference icon property, most commonly an item descriptor’s mSmallIcon / mPersistentBigIcon , at the generated texture’s path, exactly like referencing any other asset: type : cdo patches : - target : MySuperIngot # a generated item short id, same as /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot # …or any existing one: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mSmallIcon value : MyIcon # short id same as /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MyIcon - path : mPersistentBigIcon value : MyIcon Both target: and the icon values above use the bare id: because everything referenced was generated by this same pack. See Generated Content Short Ids for cross-pack resolution and the full path form. For a generated item you can just as well put these two entries straight into the item document’s properties: instead (see Items ), same ops, one file less.

sections.heading: Automatic consumer rescans
sections.text: Neither KAPI nor RRDA notice a new or changed data asset on their own. Somebody has to tell their scanning subsystem to look again, and KDataForge does that for you. After the initial load, it checks whether any data assets were modified or added and only then triggers a rescan. You never have to poke a subsystem yourself: KAPI : rescanned via reflection only when the KAPI mod is actually loaded, no hard dependency needed. RefinedRDApi : rescanned only when the RefinedRDApi mod is actually loaded, with no link dependency needed on it. It’s what covers RefinedPower / FicsitFarming boiler/cooler/heater/turbine/generator/dirt data assets, below.

sections.heading: Editing RefinedR&D data assets (RRDA)
sections.text: RefinedPower and FicsitFarming machine tuning lives in the same kind of PrimaryDataAsset instance KAPI uses, just under RRDA’s own classes: RRDABoilerDataAsset , RRDACoolerDataAsset , RRDAHeaterDataAsset , RRDATurbineDataAsset , RRDAGeneratorDataAsset , and RRDADirtDataAsset . All of these are editable with plain cdo documents exactly like the KAPI types above. Because the rescan that picks up your changes runs entirely via reflection (see above), a hasMod condition is all the gating a pack needs. There’s no RRDA API dependency to add: faster-boilers.cdo.yml type : cdo conditions : hasMod : RefinedRDApi patches : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/RefinedRDApi.RRDABoilerDataAsset properties : - path : mDuration op : multiply value : 0.5 # every RefinedPower/FicsitFarming boiler produces twice as fast Heater and turbine assets work identically: swap the class ( allAssetsOfClass: /Script/RefinedRDApi.RRDAHeaterDataAsset , …RRDATurbineDataAsset ) and patch their properties the same way. /kdf report lists every matched asset so you can confirm the selection before tuning values. See Editing Another Mod’s Data Assets for a full walkthrough that starts from “I don’t know this mod’s class names yet” and ends with a working balance pack.

pages.title: Event rules
pages.description: Run bounded server-side actions when a world starts or a schematic is purchased, with optional once-per-save execution.

sections.heading: Event rules
sections.text: Use type: eventrule to connect a gameplay event to a schematic grant or a diagnostic log entry. Rules run on the host or dedicated server. Clients do not execute the actions independently; schematic changes use the game's existing unlock and replication path.

sections.heading: First rule
sections.text: Place this document in a pack YAML file: type: eventrule rules: - id: world-start-log event: worldReady actions: - log: Factory rules are active in this save. The message appears in the game log once for this pack and save. It does not create a toast or player-facing message. log is diagnostic text, not localized UI text.

sections.heading: React to a schematic purchase
sections.text: type: eventrule rules: - id: progression-followup event: schematicPurchased schematic: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C actions: - unlockSchematic: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_2-3.Schematic_2-3_C - log: Follow-up schematic granted. Replace the class references with schematics appropriate for your progression. unlockSchematic grants access without paying its material cost; choose this action only for an intended reward. The game must allow the grant when the event occurs. This rule does not bypass a mod's CanGiveAccessToSchematic restrictions. An already purchased schematic is a successful no-op. The schematic filter is optional. Omitting it listens to every future schematic purchase. Schematics bought before the rules subscribed are not replayed. Use worldReady with requiresSchematics when you explicitly want to check progress already stored in a save.

sections.heading: Conditions and repetition
sections.text: type: eventrule rules: - id: log-existing-progress event: worldReady once: false requiresSchematics: - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C actions: - log: Required progression is present at world start. Every requiresSchematics entry must already be purchased when the event is handled. The list is an AND condition; an empty or omitted list imposes no condition. A failed condition performs no actions and does not mark the rule completed. Conditions are evaluated at events, not every frame. once defaults to true: a successful rule's identity is stored in the save. Its identity is the pack ref plus rule id, compared without case. Reloading YAML, changing action contents, moving the document, or removing and later restoring the rule does not reset that history. Give an intentional new rule a new id. Keep a stable pack ref. With once: false, the rule may run again on later events. Within one originating event and all schematic purchases triggered by its actions, each matching rule is attempted at most once. This bounds feedback loops even for repeating rules. A dispatch cascade accepts at most 128 events; excess nested events are dropped with a warning.

sections.heading: Fields and limits
sections.text: | Field | Required | Meaning | | rules | Yes | Sequence of 1–256 rules per document. | | id | Yes | 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, ., _, or -; unique across the pack, ignoring case. | | event | Yes | Exactly worldReady or schematicPurchased. | | schematic | No | Schematic class filter; only valid with schematicPurchased. | | once | No | Boolean, default true. | | requiresSchematics | No | Sequence of up to 64 schematic class references. | | actions | Yes | Sequence of 1–32 actions. | Each action is a map containing exactly one key: unlockSchematic with a concrete schematic class, or log with nonblank text up to 2,048 characters. Unknown rule and action fields are errors. Field names and event names use the exact case shown above. Class references support the usual KDataForge class resolver, including generated content already created by earlier loader stages. The entire document is rejected if any rule is malformed, a class reference cannot resolve, or its rule IDs collide with rules already registered by another document. No actions run while loading or dry-running a document; validation and loading only register rules.

sections.heading: World lifecycle and reload
sections.text: worldReady fires after gameplay actors have begun play and the schematic manager is available. It is a world-load event. It does not fire again when YAML reload completes. Therefore a new worldReady rule added by live reload starts on the next world load. Updated purchase rules handle subsequent purchase events immediately after reload; earlier purchases are not replayed. On world travel or shutdown, subscriptions and pending events are removed. Once-per-save history belongs to the save, not the local configuration. On a client, these rules do not produce an independent reward or separate completion history. All schematic grants are checked before any action in a rule executes. If a grant cannot start, the rule logs a warning, executes no actions, and remains incomplete. If the game unexpectedly rejects a grant after the checks, earlier actions remain applied, later actions stop, and the rule remains incomplete. It may retry on a later matching event; already purchased grants are skipped. This is not an atomic rollback mechanism. Arrange dependent schematic grants as separate rules when the second grant only becomes valid after the first succeeds. The supported events are world start and schematic purchase. Delivery completion, arbitrary function calls, timers, continuous factory scans, and UI popups are not event-rule actions.

pages.title: Type: gametag
pages.description: Registering new gameplay tags at runtime, syntax, implementation, and ordering guarantees.

sections.heading: Type: gametag
sections.text: A gametag document runs in the GameTags stage, which always runs first , before every other document type. The entries key for this document type is tags , given as a sequence. Changes are loaded on the next session start.

sections.heading: Minimal example
sections.text: A gametag document is a flat list of tag names to register. You can write each entry either as a bare string or as a map with an optional comment: for documentation purposes: tags.gametag.yml type : gametag tags : - tag : MyOverhaul.Machines.Tier2 # map form with an optional comment comment : Marker for tier-2 machine rebalancing - MyOverhaul.Simple # scalar shorthand, no comment Each entry is either a plain tag-name string, or a map with tag: (required) and comment: (optional). The comment is purely documentation, shown in the tag picker/editor. The tag name itself must be a valid dot-separated gameplay tag string ( Namespace.Category.Leaf... ). Invalid strings are rejected at validation time, with the engine’s own suggested fix included.

sections.heading: How registration actually works
sections.text: Registering a tag at runtime normally isn’t possible: the engine’s gameplay tag tree is built once at boot and isn’t designed to be extended afterward. KDataForge works around this by adding the tag directly to the tag settings in memory and forcing a tree rebuild, entirely without touching any config file on disk. In practice, this gives you three consequences to keep in mind: Tags exist only for the running session. They are not written to disk anywhere. Remove the YAML and the tag stops being registered on the next boot. It is not retroactively unregistered from a session that already rebuilt the tree with it present. Registration is idempotent: a tag already in GameplayTagList is skipped. There is no tombstone or removal mechanism, unlike generated classes. Gameplay tags are cheap and additive, and the engine has no supported “unregister a tag” operation.

sections.heading: Ordering guarantee: use a tag the moment you register it
sections.text: The GameTags stage always runs before every other stage . This means a tag registered in one file is immediately available to matchTag: (and to mGameplayTags ops) in any cdo document in the same pack. No include: is needed for the gametag file itself. First, put the tag on some content: # file: tag-recipes.cdo.yml put the tag ON some content type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : - MyOverhaul.Machines.Tier2 Then a second cdo document can select everything carrying that tag and patch it in bulk: # file: buff-tagged.cdo.yml match everything carrying the tag type : cdo include : - tag-recipes.cdo.yml # both files are in the CDOChanges stage order them explicitly patches : - matchTag : MyOverhaul.Machines.Tier2 ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe tagProperty : mGameplayTags properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.8 tag-recipes.cdo.yml and buff-tagged.cdo.yml are both cdo documents, meaning both are in the CDOChanges stage. That is why they need include: ordering between each other. The gametag document itself never needs it, since GameTags runs before CDOChanges unconditionally.

sections.heading: Tag container ops on mGameplayTags
sections.text: Once a tag exists, whether it is yours or a native KMods.* one (see Data Assets for the full native list), every tag-container op works on any FGameplayTagContainer property. append adds tags without disturbing existing ones. remove takes a single tag back out. clear empties the container entirely, and the default set op replaces the whole container: - path : mGameplayTags # append add tags (sequence or scalar) op : append value : - MyOverhaul.Simple - KMods.WikiExclude - path : mGameplayTags # remove take one tag out op : remove value : KMods.WikiExclude - path : mGameplayTags # clear empty the container op : clear - path : mGameplayTags # set (default) replace ALL tags value : - MyOverhaul.Machines.Tier2

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: “Invalid tag” at load time : the error message includes the engine’s own suggested fix, since this is usually a malformed dot-separated string with a stray space or an extra dot. Fix the string in your YAML, not the tag itself. There’s nothing to “clean up” on the engine side. A tag works this session but the pack is gone and it’s still there : this is expected, since nothing is unregistered mid-session, and gameplay tags have no supported “remove” path. It will stop appearing on the next full restart once the YAML is gone. matchTag: finds nothing : double check that ofClass: is actually the class (or an ancestor of the class) the tag was applied to. Also check that the gametag document registering the tag is a .gametag.yml file, not accidentally named .cdo.yml , since KDataForge infers type: from the filename when type: itself is omitted.

sections.heading: Reference
sections.text: Registering your own tags, and using them the same pack over, is also part of the end-to-end walkthrough in End-to-End Pack . Bulk-editing content by tag is covered in Targeting → matchTag and Balancing .

pages.title: Type: item
pages.description: Generating new item classes from YAML, covering parent/required-base rules, generated class identity, and property defaults.

sections.heading: Type: item
sections.text: The item document type runs in the Items stage at priority 30 , after class ( 50 ) and unlock ( 40 ), and before resource ( 25 ) and building ( 20 ). Documents load during GameInstance initialization. Restart the session after changing YAML. Entries live under the items key, and each one defaults to a parent of /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor , which is also the required base class (or a subclass of it). Register-only mode ( class: ) is not supported here; items are always generated, so use id: instead. item creates a genuinely new UFGItemDescriptor -derived class at runtime. This is the same kind of class every base-game part or component is. It shares the entry grammar with resource , building , unlock , recipe , schematic , and research (see YAML Schema → Content Creation ). However, item (along with resource , building , and unlock ) can only generate a class, never register an existing one. That register-only mode is reserved for recipe / schematic / research , see Recipes .

sections.heading: Minimal example
sections.text: A pack that wants a new tier-2 ingot needs exactly one items: entry. The id: field gives the class a stable identity, parent: seeds it from an existing item’s mesh, icon, and form, and properties: overrides only what should actually differ: super-ingot.item.yml type : item items : - id : MySuperIngot # required, stable id parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C # optional properties : # ordinary cdo-style ops - path : mDisplayName value : key : MySuperIngot_Name ns : MyPack source : Super Ingot - path : mDescription value : A far superior ingot. - path : mStackSize value : SS_HUGE # EStackSize enum see Balancing → Items for the full value list id: is required and forms the save-persistence contract, see below. parent: defaults to plain FGItemDescriptor if omitted. Giving an existing item’s class (like Desc_IronIngot above) copies its mesh, icon, form, and category defaults, so properties: only needs to override what actually differs. properties: uses the exact same op grammar as cdo patches. Every UFGItemDescriptor property is fair game. The common ones ( mStackSize , mForm , mEnergyValue , mResourceSinkPoints , mCategory , mGameplayTags , …) are cataloged with more examples in Balancing → Items .

sections.heading: Generated class identity (the save-persistence contract)
sections.text: Every generated item lands in a deterministic package and class name, derived purely from the pack’s ref and the entry’s id: , never from file path or load order. That means the same YAML always regenerates the exact same class path on every load and across every machine: The class lives in package /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef> and is named Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> . This is deterministic and id-based , never derived from file path or load order. Reference it from anywhere else (a recipe’s mProduct , a schematic’s mCost , a sinkpoints entry, another pack’s YAML) as /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> . Or, from within the same pack (or if the id is unique across packs), just the bare id: itself, e.g. MySuperIngot . See Generated Content Short Ids . Renaming the YAML file is always safe. Renaming the id: changes the generated class path, though, and that would orphan any save that already references it. Declare the rename as a redirects: entry in pack.yml instead ( FCoreRedirects resolves the old path transparently). See End-to-End Pack → Renaming an id . Classes are created at GameInstance INITIALIZATION , strictly before any save loads, so save data referencing them resolves correctly the moment the save starts loading. Constraint: a generated class has exactly the parent’s layout. There are no new reflected properties and no new components. All customisation lives in the CDO defaults properties: sets. If you need a building with a genuinely different mesh or a new component, reparent an existing buildable instead of trying to add one, see Buildings .

sections.heading: Why Items runs before Recipes / Schematics / Research
sections.text: class , unlock , item , resource , and building all generate in the same Items stage, priority-ordered as class → unlock → item → resource → building . This ordering exists specifically so that later stages can reference whatever they generated. For example, a recipe document can put a freshly generated item in its mProduct without any include: , because the Items stage has already finished by the time Recipes runs.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: “class: is only valid for recipe/schematic/research” : you tried the register-only mode on an item entry. Items can only be generated ( id: ), never just registered from an existing class. If you already have a class you want KDataForge to leave alone, you don’t need this document type for it at all. Just reference the class path directly wherever you’d otherwise reference the generated one. Item generated fine, but a properties: entry silently didn’t apply : this is the same as any cdo patch. Check /kdf report for a rejected op or a bad path: . Nothing about generation changes how property ops are validated. Need this item in a recipe or schematic right away? No include: is needed, ever, see “Why Items runs before…” above. If a reference still fails to resolve, double-check the id spelling matches exactly ( Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> is case-sensitive). Made an item but don’t see it anywhere in-game : this almost always means nothing unlocks it yet. An item and a recipe producing it are not enough on their own. Walk through Item + Icon + Recipe + Tier-1 Unlock for the complete chain, including the schematic step that’s usually missing.

pages.title: Type: localization
pages.description: Runtime text entries per namespace and culture, overriding existing texts by source string, and culture matching.

sections.heading: Type: localization
sections.text: The Localization stage runs after GameTags / Assets and before CDOChanges . Its entries key is entries , a map from key to either a scalar or a block map with source and text fields.

sections.heading: Simple key entries: new text
sections.text: The scalar form registers a brand new localized text under namespace: and key. This works for your own content’s FText keys, or anyone else’s, as long as the namespace and key match: de.localization.yml type : localization namespace : MyPack culture : de # prefix-matched: also applies for de-DE, de-AT, … entries : MySuperIngot_Name : ' Superbarren ' MySuperIngot_Desc : ' Ein weit überlegener Barren. '

sections.heading: source + text map: overriding an EXISTING text
sections.text: The map form overrides a text that already exists (vanilla or modded) by its original source string: type : localization namespace : MyPack culture : de entries : IronIngot_Renamed : source : ' Iron Ingot ' text : ' Eisenbarren (überarbeitet) ' SchematicOverride : source : ' Super Ingot Smelting ' text : ' Superbarren-Verhüttung ' ⚠️ Source-hash matching. UE identifies a localized text by its namespace/key plus a hash of the original source string. The source: you give must be byte-identical to the current original text: spacing, punctuation, and capitalisation all matter. If a game update changes the source string, the override silently stops matching. Copy the exact string from the game, don’t retype it. Omitting source: uses text: as the source too, which only works for new keys. The scalar form above is the same thing written shorter.

sections.heading: How it’s applied
sections.text: Localization entries are applied through the same mechanism the engine’s own localization system uses to load .locres files, so there is nothing KDataForge-specific for the game to special-case.

sections.heading: Bidirectional prefix matching for culture:
sections.text: culture : de # matches current language de, de-DE, de-AT, … culture : pt-BR # matches only pt-BR (a more specific prefix than pt) # omit culture: # entries apply for EVERY language The match is bidirectional prefix matching : either the current language starts with culture: , or culture: starts with the current language. culture: de applies when the running game is set to de-DE , and culture: de-DE would also apply if the game were set to plain de . Whichever side is the shorter prefix wins the comparison. In practice, prefer the shortest culture code that covers your translation, de rather than de-DE , unless you specifically need a regional variant. Documents whose culture: doesn’t match the current language are skipped with an Info diagnostic. This is not a warning: it’s expected, not an error.

sections.heading: Loading changes
sections.text: Localization changes are loaded on the next session start. A complete worked translation (item + schematic + German locale file, applied together) is part of the end-to-end pack in End-to-End Pack .

sections.heading: Localizing configuration text
sections.text: The name , description , tooltip and option label of a pack configuration field can use the localized text form, exactly like a text property: name : key : Config_IronSpeed_Name ns : KDFSample source : Iron smelting speed source is the text shown when no translation exists. Translate it with a localization document that uses the same namespace and key (the source of the map form must equal the text in the definition): config-texts.localization.yml type : localization namespace : KDFSample culture : de entries : Config_IronSpeed_Name : source : Iron smelting speed text : Eisen-Schmelzgeschwindigkeit The same works for a pack’s description in pack.yml and for category class names.

sections.heading: Config values and templates in text entries
sections.text: Text entries are string values, so templates work in them. The pre-pass providers ( cfg , session , ags , option ) are replaced before the entries are registered, which lets a translation show the player’s current settings: config-values.localization.yml type : localization namespace : KDFSample culture : en entries : Config_Summary : ' Iron smelts at {cfg:balance.ironSpeed}x, milestone in tier {cfg:features.tier}. ' Config_Literal : ' Write \{cfg:balance.ironSpeed} to show the speed. ' {0} -style text arguments are not templates and pass through unchanged. Apply-time providers such as {item:...} are not expanded in localization entries; they work in operation values (an item description, for example), see Templates . Localization documents are one of the places where a hot field is allowed ( Hot and cold values ): the text is rebuilt every time KDataForge loads.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: My override isn’t taking effect. This is almost always the source-hash mismatch described above. Copy the original string straight out of the game, or the base-game source if you have it, rather than retyping it from memory. A single missing period or extra space is enough to break the match silently. Translation shows in one culture but not another. Check for a stray culture: on the file. Omitting it entirely is usually what you want, unless you’re intentionally splitting translations per locale across files. New key works, but overriding an existing key doesn’t. New keys, using the scalar form, don’t need source: to match anything since there’s nothing to match yet. Overrides, using the map form, do need it. If you’re not sure which one you need, ask yourself: does this text already exist in the game?

pages.title: Operations
pages.description: What each of the 25 property operations does, which property kinds support it, and one working example apiece.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.text: Every entry in a type: cdo patch's properties: list names a target path and an operation (op:) that decides how the entry's value (or its other arguments) combines with whatever is currently stored at that path. If you leave op: out, it defaults to set, a plain overwrite. That is why most of the simple examples elsewhere in these docs never mention an op at all. This page walks through all 25 operations the engine recognizes. They are grouped by the kind of property they act on: numeric math and clamping, container mutation for arrays, sets, maps, and tag containers, string concatenation, array reordering and deduplication, and cross-property copy or move. See Patching (type: cdo) for the full patch structure these entries live inside. See Property Types for what each underlying property looks like in YAML.

sections.heading: Select every gameplay tag container
sections.text: Use the quoted operation path '@tagContainers' to apply the same operation to every top-level FGameplayTagContainer on each target. Inherited fields are included. With applyToSubclasses: true, KDF selects fields again for each subclass, including additional fields on classes loaded later. An object without matching fields is a no-op. type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor applyToSubclasses: true properties: - path: '@tagContainers' op: append value: [KMods.PlannerResource] Register tags before using them, for example through a type: gametag document. Supported operations are set (also the default), append, prepend, remove and clear. Tag containers are sets: adding an existing tag does not create duplicates. Each selected field gets its own normal snapshot and patch record for rollback. Use consecutive remove and append entries to replace one set of tags with another. The selector does not recurse into nested structs, objects or arrays and cannot be combined with a suffix such as .Child or [0]. It is only an operation destination, not a concrete property path for where, from, templates or single-property read/edit APIs. Use an actual field name in those contexts. Keep quotes: YAML does not allow an unquoted scalar starting with @.

sections.heading: append_unique: array
sections.text: Appends each incoming value only if no equal element is already present. Existing duplicates and their order stay unchanged; repeated incoming values are added at most once. This matches a MergeUnique-style update without deduplicating the destination array: - path: mAllowedResourceForms op: append_unique value: [RF_GAS] For example, [RF_LIQUID, RF_LIQUID] becomes [RF_LIQUID, RF_LIQUID, RF_GAS]. Applying the same operation again leaves it unchanged. value accepts one element or a sequence; an empty sequence is a successful no-op. Equality uses the reflected element type, including enum, struct and object identity. Arrays only: use ordinary append for sets/maps. Inline {class, properties} subobject creation is rejected; reference an existing object or use append to create a new instance. Malformed operands fail without leaving a partial array edit.

sections.heading: update_where: array of structs
sections.text: update_where checks every struct element in an array and partially updates every match. The where path is relative to one element, not the patched object. value must be a struct mapping; members omitted from that mapping keep their current values: - path: mProduct op: update_where where: path: ItemClass equals: /OldMod/Items/Desc_Old.Desc_Old_C value: ItemClass: /NewMod/Items/Desc_New.Desc_New_C Use a sequence under where to AND several clauses. Clauses accept the same operators as target filters: equals, notEquals, numeric comparisons, contains, notContains, in, notIn, matches, and isEmpty. Nested paths and [*] reads are supported inside the element. Every matching element is updated. No match is an error, protecting patches against upstream array changes. Invalid predicates or values roll back the whole array operation; partial writes are not kept. Only arrays whose elements are reflected structs are supported. This operation is useful for recipe mIngredients and mProduct arrays because it does not depend on element order.

sections.heading: replace_refs: reflected reference trees
sections.text: replace_refs searches below one property and replaces every exact matching object or class reference. It follows reflected structs, arrays, sets, maps, and instanced objects. This makes the same operation usable for recipe inputs/outputs and for nested schematic unlock or dependency objects without knowing array indexes or concrete unlock subclasses: - path: mUnlocks op: replace_refs from: /OldMod/Recipes/Recipe_Old.Recipe_Old_C value: /NewMod/Recipes/Recipe_New.Recipe_New_C Use path: mIngredients or path: mProduct for recipes, and the appropriate unlock or dependency array on schematics and data assets. path is also the traversal boundary: unrelated properties on the target are never searched. Both hard and soft object/class references are supported. Instanced objects are traversed, but KDF does not follow ordinary external object references into unrelated assets. from and value must be scalar references. The replacement must satisfy every matched property's reflected class type. Zero matches, incompatible targets, or excessive nesting fail the operation. All matched references are validated before writing; a failure keeps original values.

sections.heading: set (default): everything
sections.text: set overwrites the property outright. It works on any property type, which is why it can be left implicit. On mDisplayName (an FString), setting a value simply replaces the string: - path: mDisplayName value: 'Reinforced Iron Ingot' # op: set is implied

sections.heading: Bitmask operations
sections.text: set accepts one flag name or a sequence of flag names. KDataForge resolves and ORs names from the property's BitmaskEnum. Raw numeric masks are accepted by set only. Plain integer bitmask handling requires WITH_METADATA, retained property metadata, and an already-loaded enum; missing metadata or an unresolved enum leaves ordinary integer conversion. See Property Types for named mask/index forms, width limits, and Shipping-build limitations. - path: mParentTask value: Above - path: mParentTask value: - Above - Left

sections.heading: add / subtract: numeric
sections.text: add and subtract do in-place arithmetic on a plain numeric property. They add or subtract value from whatever is currently stored. Both reject enum-backed integers (see the callout below), since there is no meaningful "current + 1" for an enum ordinal: - path: mTechTier op: add value: 1 - path: mTimeToComplete op: subtract value: 30

sections.heading: multiply / divide: numeric
sections.text: multiply and divide scale a numeric property by value. Setting mManufactoringDuration to a fraction of itself halves the crafting time, while dividing mEnergyValue doubles the effective fuel efficiency. Dividing by 0 is rejected outright, rather than producing infinity or NaN: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.5 - path: mEnergyValue op: divide value: 2

sections.heading: min / max: numeric (result = min/max of current and value)
sections.text: min enforces a ceiling: the property is replaced with whichever is smaller, the current value or value. max enforces a floor, replacing the property with whichever is larger. Neither can push the property past value in the opposite direction, which makes them useful for "never exceed" or "never fall below" balancing passes across many objects at once: - path: mResourceSinkPoints op: min value: 100 # cap at 100 - path: mResourceSinkPoints op: max value: 50 # raise to at least 50 :::caution Enum-backed properties don't count as numeric. mStackSize on FGItemDescriptor is an EStackSize enum (SS_ONE…SS_HUGE/SS_FLUID), not a plain int min/max/clamp/ add/subtract/multiply/divide are all rejected on it (op not supported); only set with an enum value name works. See Property Types → Enums. :::

sections.heading: clamp: numeric
sections.text: clamp is the two-sided version of min/max: instead of a single value, it takes min and max keys and pins the current value inside that range in one step: - path: mMenuPriority op: clamp min: 0 max: 999

sections.heading: append: array / set / map / string / tag container / bitmask
sections.text: append adds to the end of a container, or concatenates onto a string. It behaves differently depending on the target property's kind. For arrays and sets, value can be a single item or a sequence to add several items at once. For strings, it concatenates text. For tag containers, it adds tags. For maps, value must be a map, and KDataForge merges those key/value pairs into the existing map: - path: mIngredients # array: adds element(s) at the end op: append value: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Coal/Desc_Coal.Desc_Coal_C Amount: 1 - path: mDisplayName # string: concatenates op: append value: ' (rebalanced)' - path: mGameplayTags # tag container: adds tags op: append value: - MyPack.Rebalanced - path: mSomeMap # map: merges entries op: append value: Iron: 10 - path: mParentTask # bitmask: OR-adds flags op: append value: - Above - Left For bitmasks, append ORs named flags into current mask. It does not accept raw integer masks. For instanced UObject arrays, an appended value can be a { class, properties } map; KDataForge constructs the new subobject before inserting it into the array: - path: mUnlocks op: append value: class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties: - path: mRecipes value: - Recipe_MyGeneratedRecipe :::note String operations on FText properties (like mDisplayName when it is a localized text field) produce plain culture-invariant text the original localization key/namespace is dropped, so an append/prepend/clear on a translated string stops it from tracking further translation updates. See Localization if you need the result to stay localizable instead. :::

sections.heading: prepend: array / set / string (tag containers and bitmasks: same as append)
sections.text: prepend mirrors append, but it adds at the front instead of the end for arrays, and inserts before the existing text for strings. Tag containers treat it identically to append, since a tag container has no ordering. Sets also treat it like append, because sets have no ordering. Bitmasks also treat it like append and OR-add named flags. Maps do not support prepend at all: only append merges into a map. - path: mDisplayName op: prepend value: '[MP] '

sections.heading: insert: array
sections.text: insert places one or more elements at a specific index inside an array, rather than always at the end, and shifts later elements back. An out-of-range index fails with an error, instead of clamping to the array's bounds. Instanced UObject array entries may use the same `{ class, properties } map accepted by set, append, and prepend`: - path: mIngredients op: insert index: 1 value: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreCopper/Desc_OreCopper.Desc_OreCopper_C Amount: 1

sections.heading: remove: array (by value) / set (by value) / map (by key) / tag container / bitmask
sections.text: remove deletes by content rather than by position. On arrays and sets, it deletes every element that matches value exactly. An array remove that matches nothing fails, rather than silently doing nothing. On maps, value is the _key_ to delete, and on tag containers, value is the tag (or list of tags) to remove. On bitmasks, it clears every named bit with AND-NOT: - path: mIngredients # removes every element equal to the value op: remove value: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C Amount: 1 - path: mSomeMap # map: value is the key op: remove value: Iron - path: mGameplayTags op: remove value: KMods.WikiExclude - path: mParentTask # bitmask: clears named bits op: remove value: Left

sections.heading: remove_at: array
sections.text: remove_at deletes the element at a specific position instead of matching by value. It is the right tool when you know the slot but not, or don't want to spell out, the exact contents: - path: mProduct op: remove_at index: 1

sections.heading: clear: array / set / map / string / tag container / bitmask
sections.text: clear empties a container-shaped property entirely: arrays, sets, maps, and tag containers all lose every element. Strings are reset to empty, rather than to their class-default text. On a metadata-recognized bitmask, clear writes 0: - path: mSubCategories op: clear - path: mParentTask # bitmask: sets mask to 0 op: clear

sections.heading: swap: array
sections.text: swap exchanges the elements at two positions, index and with, in an array without touching anything else in the list. It is useful for reordering a couple of entries without rewriting the whole array: - path: mIngredients op: swap index: 0 with: 1

sections.heading: replace: array
sections.text: replace overwrites the element at index with a new value, keeping every other element and the array's length unchanged: - path: mProduct op: replace index: 0 value: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/SteelIngot/Desc_SteelIngot.Desc_SteelIngot_C Amount: 2

sections.heading: duplicate: array (copies element to the end)
sections.text: duplicate copies the element at index and appends the copy to the end of the same array. It is handy for cloning an existing ingredient or product entry as a starting point, before tweaking it with a follow-up replace: - path: mProduct op: duplicate index: 0

sections.heading: sort / reverse: array
sections.text: sort reorders an array in ascending order. Numeric and string inner types sort by their actual value. Anything else, such as structs or object references, sorts by its exported text form. reverse simply flips the current order of every element: - path: mRelevantEvents # numeric/string inner types sort by value; others by text form op: sort - path: mSubCategories op: reverse

sections.heading: unique: array (removes later duplicates; sets: no-op)
sections.text: unique walks an array and removes any element that is byte-identical to an earlier one, keeping the first occurrence of each value. Running it on a set is always a no-op, since a set is already guaranteed to contain no duplicates: - path: mSubCategories op: unique

sections.heading: copy: any property (from another path on the same object)
sections.text: copy reads the value at another property path (from) on the same object and writes it into the target property. When source and destination are exactly the same property type, it copies the raw value directly. Otherwise, it round-trips through each property's text representation. This means copying between compatible but different types, for example a plain string into a name, can still work, as long as the text parses back cleanly for the destination type: - path: mAbbreviatedDisplayName op: copy from: mDisplayName

sections.heading: move: copy, then reset the source to its default
sections.text: move performs the exact same copy as copy, then additionally clears the source property back to its default value. This makes it the right choice when a value should live at the new path _instead of_ the old one, rather than in both places: - path: mDescription op: move from: mScannerDisplayText

pages.title: Pack Configuration
pages.description: Let players tune a pack without editing YAML. Typed config fields, the values file, categories, hot and cold values, cold properties, and multiplayer behavior.

sections.heading: Pack Configuration
sections.text: A pack normally ships fixed numbers. Pack configuration lets you expose some of them as typed settings . A config definition ( <name>.config.yml ) declares fields such as a speed slider, a checkbox, or a tier dropdown. KDataForge stores the player’s choices in one small values file per pack, and your other documents read those choices through typed references and templates or config: conditions . A mod (or you, in Blueprint) can build a settings screen from the same definitions with the Blueprint Config API . Configuration is the first thing a pack loads. Definitions and values are read before pack conditions, before any document is parsed, and before the stages run, so everything in the pack can already use them. For a guided build of the example used on this page, follow Player-Configurable Balancing .

sections.heading: Quick start
sections.text: Three files turn a hard-coded value into a setting. The category class groups the field in a settings screen, the config definition declares the field, and the patch reads it. # sample-config-category.class.yml (excerpt of the sample pack) type : class classes : - id : SampleBalanceCategory parent : /Script/FactoryGame.FGCategory properties : - path : mDisplayName value : key : SampleBalanceCategory_Name ns : KDFSample source : Sample Balance - path : mMenuPriority value : 10 # iron.config.yml (excerpt of kdf-sample.config.yml) type : config fields : - id : balance.ironSpeed type : number valueType : float name : Iron smelting speed description : How many times faster the Iron Ingot recipe runs than in the base game. category : SampleBalanceCategory default : 2 min : 0.25 max : 4 step : 0.25 display : slider apply : hot # iron-ingot-faster.cdo.yml (excerpt of the sample pack) type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : divide value : cfg:balance.ironSpeed On the first load KDataForge creates FactoryGame/Configs/Packs/KDFSample.config.yml with the default. Change ironSpeed there, run /kdf reload , and the recipe follows. The cfg: value is a typed reference : because it is the whole unquoted scalar, it becomes the number 2.0 , not text.

sections.heading: Definition files
sections.text: Every file named <name>.config.yml (or .config.yaml ) anywhere below a pack root is a config definition . These files are not ordinary documents. They are always read first, they never appear in the document list, and a pack can have as many as it likes. Field ids are unique across all of them. Key Required Meaning type no If present it must be config . Any other type in a *.config.yml file is an error. category no Default category for every field in the file (see Categories ). conditions , conditionBehavior no Static conditions only ( gameVersion , hasMod , modVersion , hasClass ). A config: condition is an error here: a definition cannot depend on its own values. debug no Same as in other documents. fields yes A non-empty list of fields. type: config in a file that is not named *.config.yml is an error and the document is dropped. The reverse holds too: a *.config.yml file with another explicit type is skipped. A broken field is reported as an error and only that field is skipped. The rest of the file, and the rest of the pack, still load.

sections.heading: Common field keys
sections.text: Key Required Meaning id yes Segments of letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit), joined by dots: balance.ironSpeed . Unique per pack, ignoring case. A field may not also be the prefix of another ( a.b and a.b.c clash). true , false , in and contains are reserved because expressions use them. type yes text , number , boolean or select . valueType no The stored type. Allowed values depend on type (see below). name yes Display name: a string, or the localized form {key, ns, source} . description yes One or two sentences for the settings screen. Same text forms as name . tooltip no {title, text} , each a string or localized form. category yes* A UFGCategory subclass. *Not needed on a field when the document sets a default. default yes The value used until the player changes it. A list when multiple: true . apply no hot or cold . Defaults to cold (see Hot and cold values ). order no Whole number that sorts fields inside a category. Defaults to the declaration order across the pack’s config files (files sorted by path). multiple no true turns select into a multi-select and text or number into a list. Not allowed for boolean . name and description are mandatory so that every setting is explained in the UI. Keys descriptionClass and properties are reserved for a later version and ignored with a warning. Unknown keys are ignored with a warning too.

sections.heading: Field types at a glance
sections.text: type valueType Extra keys Blueprint class text string (default), text , name multiline (only text ), maxLength (default 1024, at most 1024) UKDFConfigTextDescription text tag tagRoot UKDFConfigTagDescription number int32 (default), int8 , int16 , int64 , uint8 , float , double min , max , step , decimals , display UKDFConfigNumberDescription , or UKDFConfigSliderDescription boolean bool (default), uint8 none UKDFConfigBooleanDescription select any of the above plus bool (default string ) options , minSelected , maxSelected UKDFConfigSelectDescription select + multiple as above as above UKDFConfigMultiSelectDescription text or number + multiple as the single field minCount , maxCount UKDFConfigListDescription The Blueprint Config API lists the getters and setters of every class.

sections.heading: Every field type in one file
sections.text: This file declares one field of each kind. Copy the part you need. demo.config.yml type : config category : SampleFeaturesCategory # default for every field below fields : # ----- text ----- - id : demo.title type : text # valueType defaults to string name : Title description : A short single-line text. default : Hello maxLength : 40 apply : hot - id : demo.motto type : text valueType : text # a localizable FText; multiline needs valueType: text multiline : true maxLength : 200 name : Motto description : A longer text that can span several lines. default : Forged from YAML. apply : hot - id : demo.internalName type : text valueType : name # an FName name : Internal name description : A name value. default : MyThing - id : demo.marker type : text valueType : tag # one gameplay tag below tagRoot tagRoot : KDF.Sample name : Marker tag description : Pick one tag below KDF.Sample. default : KDF.Sample.Test apply : hot # ----- number ----- - id : demo.count type : number # int32 input: no min+max pair, so no slider name : Count description : A whole number. default : 10 min : 1 max : 100 apply : hot - id : demo.speed type : number valueType : float display : slider # needs min < max min : 0.25 max : 4 step : 0.25 decimals : 2 name : Speed description : A slider with a step. default : 1 apply : hot - id : demo.ratio type : number valueType : double display : input name : Ratio description : A free decimal number. default : 0.125 decimals : 3 apply : hot # ----- boolean ----- - id : demo.enabled type : boolean name : Enabled description : A checkbox. default : true apply : hot # ----- select ----- - id : demo.difficulty type : select # valueType defaults to string name : Difficulty description : Exactly one option. default : easy options : - value : easy label : Easy - value : hard label : key : Demo_Hard ns : KDFSample source : Hard # the localized label form - id : demo.tier type : select valueType : int32 # option values are typed name : Tier description : A numeric choice. default : 2 options : - { value : 1 , label : Tier 1 } - { value : 2 , label : Tier 2 } - { value : 3 , label : Tier 3 } # ----- multi-select ----- - id : demo.enabledTiers type : select valueType : int32 multiple : true # several options minSelected : 1 maxSelected : 2 name : Enabled tiers description : Pick one or two tiers. default : [ 1 , 2 ] options : - { value : 1 , label : Tier 1 } - { value : 2 , label : Tier 2 } - { value : 3 , label : Tier 3 } apply : hot # ----- lists ----- - id : demo.names type : text multiple : true # a list of strings minCount : 1 maxCount : 4 name : Names description : Between one and four names. default : [ Alpha , Beta ] apply : hot - id : demo.multipliers type : number valueType : float multiple : true # a list of numbers; min and max apply to every element min : 0 max : 10 name : Multipliers description : A list of factors. default : [ 1 , 1.5 ] apply : hot - id : demo.tags type : text valueType : tag multiple : true # a list of gameplay tags tagRoot : KDF.Sample name : Tags description : Any number of tags below KDF.Sample. default : [ KDF.Sample.Test ] apply : hot

sections.heading: Numbers
sections.text: Integer widths take whole numbers. min and max of an integer field must be whole numbers. step must be greater than 0. decimals (0 to 9) controls how many fractional digits are shown and stored. Without it, the digits of step are used, otherwise 4 for float and 6 for double . display: slider needs min and max with min < max . If you leave display out, a field with both bounds is a slider and any other number field is a plain input. A slider cannot be combined with multiple . Values outside the range are clamped and reported as a warning when read from the values file. Setting a value in Blueprint also clamps (the setter still returns true ). In a number list, min , max , step and decimals apply to every element.

sections.heading: Text, tags and selections
sections.text: multiline: true is only valid with valueType: text . Typing more than maxLength characters is rejected. A tag field accepts valid gameplay tag strings. With tagRoot , only tags below that root are allowed. The tags do not need to be registered when the value is read, so a pack can offer tags that its own gametag document registers. options need a unique value of the field’s valueType and a label . default must be one of the option values (every element of it for a multi-select). minSelected and maxSelected exist only with multiple: true . minCount and maxCount bound a list. Text and option values are compared case-sensitively : Hard and hard are different values. Field ids stay unique ignoring case ( Speed and speed cannot both exist).

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: These limits keep the values small enough to be saved and sent to players. A field that breaks one is an error and is skipped; the rest of the pack still loads. A field id has at most 200 characters. A pack that defines configuration needs a ref of at most 50 characters. maxLength is at most 1024 . A list or multi-select holds at most 64 entries: maxCount and maxSelected must not be above 64, and a list without maxCount is limited to 64 entries.

sections.heading: Localized names
sections.text: name , description , tooltip and option label accept the same localized form as any FText : name : key : Config_IronSpeed_Name ns : KDFSample source : Iron smelting speed Translate it with a localization document that uses the same namespace and key.

sections.heading: Categories
sections.text: Every field needs a category : a Blueprint-style UFGCategory subclass. Settings screens use it as a section heading and sort sections by the category’s mMenuPriority (lower first). Define categories with an ordinary type: class document whose parent is /Script/FactoryGame.FGCategory , as in the quick start. The mDisplayName and mMenuPriority of the class become the heading and its position. Where the category is written: categories-demo.config.yml type : config category : SampleFeaturesCategory # document default fields : - id : cat.a type : boolean name : Uses the document default description : No category key, so SampleFeaturesCategory applies. default : true - id : cat.b type : boolean name : Uses its own category description : The field level key wins over the document default. category : SampleBalanceCategory default : false A category can be written as a bare id of a class generated in the same pack ( SampleBalanceCategory ), a full class path ( /Script/FactoryGame.FGCategory itself or a Blueprint category), or /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> . Generated classes exist only after the Items stage, so categories are resolved at the end of the load. An unknown or wrong class is an error; the field is then listed under the plain UFGCategory bucket so it stays reachable.

sections.heading: The values file
sections.text: Players change values in one file per pack: <GameFolder>/FactoryGame/Configs/Packs/<PackRef>.config.yml It is created at the first load of a pack that has at least one field. Dotted ids become nested maps and lists become sequences. The generated # header lists every field with type, range, default and hot or cold. # KDataForge pack configuration for 'KDFSample' # Hot fields apply with '/kdf reload' or when applied in game; cold fields need a game restart. # ... one comment line per field: id, type, default, hot or cold, name ... balance : ironSpeed : 2.0 features : enableBonus : true tier : 1 tags : extra : - KDF.Sample.Test texts : motto : Forged from YAML. Stacks high, sinks well. How the file is read and written: A missing key uses the default . A value of the wrong type uses the default and logs a warning. An out-of-range number is clamped with a warning. 3.0 is accepted for an integer field. Keys that no field uses are kept. KDataForge rewrites the file in a canonical form, so your values and unknown keys survive but the comments are regenerated. The file is written atomically (temp file, then rename), as UTF-8 without BOM, and only when its content changes. A file that is not valid YAML is never overwritten, not even when you apply changes in a settings screen or adopt host values (the apply result reports an error and the pending changes are dropped). Defaults apply and a warning names the file. Fix or delete it. Only your own saved choices are written. Values received from a multiplayer host or set in a UI but not yet applied never end up in this file. The file name uses the pack ref. If two refs differ only in letter case, the second pack’s settings are disabled with a warning.

sections.heading: Using values
sections.text: A field is read by its id. Inside a pack the bare id is enough. From another pack use <pack>:<id> . Three forms exist: tuning.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : # 1. Typed reference: the whole unquoted scalar becomes the typed value. - path : mManufactoringDuration op : divide value : cfg:balance.ironSpeed # 2. Element condition: the op exists only while the setting is on. - path : mProduct[0].Amount op : multiply value : 2 conditions : config : ' features.enableBonus ' # 3. A list field becomes a list. - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : cfg:tags.extra super-ingot.item.yml type : item items : - id : SuperIngot parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : # 4. Template: {cfg:...} inside a string is replaced by the value as text. - path : mDescription value : ' {cfg:texts.motto} Smelts like {item:/Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C:GetItemName} at {cfg:balance.ironSpeed}x speed. ' A list field that is empty (for example default: [] ) is still a list. With append , prepend or insert an empty list adds nothing and is not an error; leaving value out is. See append . Conditions can also gate a whole document. The same config: key works in pack.yml to gate a whole pack (use a cold field there, see Hot and cold values ): bonus-only.cdo.yml type : cdo conditions : config : ' features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed >= 2 ' patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.9 The templates page covers typed references, {cfg:} and the other template providers in detail. The expression reference covers the config: condition grammar. A pack that its own config: condition switched off keeps its settings in the list (marked as not active), so a player can turn it back on.

sections.heading: Hot and cold values
sections.text: Every field is hot or cold . apply: hot apply: cold (default) Changing the value Saved to the values file, then KDataForge reloads and the content follows within the session. Saved to the values file. The running game keeps the value it loaded with and reports restart required . /kdf reload after editing the file Applies the new value. Reports restart required. Use it for Numbers and texts that live in properties: of a patch: durations, amounts, stack sizes, descriptions. Anything the game reads once: generated class ids, registrations, tiers, which documents exist. Value lifecycle, in the terms the Blueprint API uses: the default from the definition, the stored value from the file, a pending value (set in a UI, not yet applied), a host value (multiplayer), and the effective value, the one the loaded content was built with. GetValue() returns pending, else host, else stored. A cold field keeps its effective value after the first load, so a saved change differs from it until the next start.

sections.heading: Which fields may feed what
sections.text: A hot field only stays hot where KDataForge can re-apply it. These places can follow a hot value: values inside cdo , dataasset , curve , asset and localization documents; values inside properties: subtrees and operation lists of item , resource , building , unlock , class , recipe , schematic and research documents, including element conditions there. These places are cold contexts : ids, parents and the document structure of generating kinds, document-level conditions of those kinds, the gametag , sublevel , resourcenode and sinkpoints documents, remove: entries, redirects: and pack.yml . A hot field used there still works, but KDataForge reports it as restart advised . The editor warns about it while you type ( config.hot-in-cold-stage , config.hot-in-condition ). Cold fields are fine everywhere.

sections.heading: Restart-advised results
sections.text: When a hot field feeds a cold context or a cold property, the apply result lists it in mRestartAdvisedKeys , /kdf config apply prints Restart advised: ... , and /kdf report lists the places. The change is applied; the advice only says that some of its effects need a restart to be complete.

sections.heading: Cold properties
sections.text: Some game properties are read once and cached, or are only used when an object is created. Writing them while the game runs succeeds, but nothing visible changes. KDataForge ships a cold property catalog that names them, and the VS Code extension uses it to warn you. Class Property Reload Why FGSchematic mUnlocks cold Unlocks are granted when a schematic is purchased. Schematics bought earlier keep what they granted. FGItemDescriptor mStackSize hot KDataForge resets the cached stack size after every write. FGItemDescriptor mForm cold Inventories, conveyors and pipes read the form when they are set up. FGRecipe mProducedIn cold Producer recipe lists are built when recipes become available. Matching includes subclasses. The reload column means: hot : applies live (an explicit allow-list entry). cold : needs a restart, or does not change existing state. newActors : only newly spawned actors see it. Besides the table, one rule applies: a property of an AActor or UActorComponent class default is newActors unless the patch sets applyToSpawnedActors: true (then existing actors are patched as well) or the catalog lists it explicitly.
