Buildings that are already placed keep the value they were spawned with. stack-tuning.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : # mStackSize is on the allow-list as hot: a hot config value is fine here. - path : mStackSize value : SS_HUGE # mForm is cold: a restart is required, no matter what feeds it. - path : mForm value : RF_SOLID The editor reports: Situation Editor diagnostic An operation path: targets a cold or newActors property property.cold (information; configurable) A hot config value feeds that operation config.hot-into-cold-property (warning) The reflection export carries the same classification ( kdf.reload on every property) and the catalog itself ( catalog/cold_properties.json ), see Reflection Export .

sections.heading: Pack name, description and icon
sections.text: pack.yml accepts two optional fields that settings screens show next to the pack: pack.yml ref : KDFSample name : KDataForge Sample Pack version : 1.0.0 description : Exercises every KDataForge document type, plus pack configuration. icon : mod-logo.png description is a string or the localized form {key, ns, source} . icon is a pack-relative png , jpg , jpeg , tga or bmp file (it must stay inside the pack folder), or an object path of a UTexture2D that starts with / . Icons are decoded when a UI first asks for the pack info and are skipped on dedicated servers. An icon file may be at most 16 MB and 4096 x 4096 pixels; larger images are rejected with a warning in the log.

sections.heading: Changing values
sections.text: Way Who Effect Edit the values file, then /kdf reload (or KDF.Reload ) Single player, host, server admin Hot values apply. Cold values report restart required. A settings screen built with the Blueprint Config API Anyone allowed to edit (see Multiplayer ) Set pending values, then apply. /kdf config dump [pack] Anyone Lists fields with default, effective and pending values. /kdf config set <pack>:<id> <value> Host or dedicated-server admin Sets a pending value. Arrays take comma separated elements. /kdf config apply [pack] Host or dedicated-server admin Saves pending values and reloads when a hot field changed. KDF.Config.Dump , KDF.Config.Set , KDF.Config.Apply Console The same three actions. KDF.Template "<text>" [pack] Console Expands templates, to test them. KDF.Config.Expr "<expression>" [pack] Console Evaluates a config: expression. /kdf config dump KDFSample /kdf config set KDFSample:balance.ironSpeed 3 /kdf config set KDFSample:tags.extra KDF.Sample.Test, KDF.Sample.Plain /kdf config apply KDFSample KDF.Template "Speed {cfg:balance.ironSpeed}x" KDFSample KDF.Config.Expr "balance.ironSpeed >= 2 && features.enableBonus" KDFSample After /kdf config apply , the chat shows what was saved, whether a reload ran, and the keys that need a restart or advise one.

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: The host decides. Standalone and the listen-server host edit their own files. A dedicated server has its values file; edit it and run /kdf reload , or apply changes as an administrator from a settings screen. Values are synchronized, files are not. While a client is connected, the host’s effective values are sent to it and held in memory. A client’s own values file is never written from them, and leaving the session restores the local values. Hot differences just work. If the host’s hot value differs from the client’s, the client uses the host’s value and reloads so its content matches. Cold differences warn. A client keeps the content it loaded with. The field reports IsHostMismatch , and the subsystem fires On Config Host Mismatch once per key and join. A UI can offer Adopt host values , which writes the host’s values to the local file; cold ones then need a restart. Who may change values. In a listen-server game only the host. On a dedicated server only administrators, through the settings UI or /kdf config . Everyone else sees the host’s values as read-only. Invalid values. An administrator request with a bad single value reports that error in the result. The valid values in the same request are still applied. The packs themselves are still not synchronized. Install the same packs and versions on the server and every client; only the configuration values travel.

sections.heading: Limits worth knowing
sections.text: session: and ags: values do not exist without a world (main menu). A document that uses one as a value is deferred and applied automatically once a save is loaded. In a config: condition, a setting that is not available yet is not an error either. An element-level hasClass condition cannot see classes that KDataForge generates. Operands of where: filters resolve cfg: references but not apply-time templates such as {item:...} . Definitions are read when KDataForge loads. Adding or removing fields needs /kdf reload ; a field that disappears is no longer listed, but its object stays alive (marked stale) so a widget that still holds it does not crash. Values are capped at 64 elements of 1024 characters when they are synchronized to clients.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Symptom Likely cause The values file is not created The pack has no valid field, or another pack’s ref differs only in case and took the file name. A reference stays text It was quoted, or it is not the whole scalar. Use cfg:id unquoted, or {cfg:id} inside a string. Config value 'KDFSample:x' does not exist A typo in the id, or the field is declared in another pack. Use cfg:<pack>:<id> . A hot change needs a restart anyway The field also feeds a cold context or a cold property. See Restart-advised results . A value in the file is ignored Wrong type, out of range, or a syntax error. The log names the key and says the default is used. A category shows as FGCategory The category: class was not found or is not a UFGCategory . Check the id and that the class document is in the same pack. Run /kdf report for the full list of configuration diagnostics, and KDF.Config.Dump <pack> to see every value slot and the file and line of each field.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: Templates and Typed References Config Expressions Blueprint Config API Player-Configurable Balancing Conditions & Packs

pages.title: Patching (type: cdo)
pages.description: The property-patch document type. Covers how patches, target selectors, and modifiers fit together, plus where the deep-dive pages live.

sections.heading: Patching (type: cdo)
sections.text: This document type runs at the CDOChanges stage, after GameTags , Assets , and Localization , and before any content-generation stage. Its entries live under the patches key as a sequence. YAML changes are loaded on the next session start. This is the workhorse document type. It edits any reflected property on any class default object or object instance in the game: items, recipes, buildings, schematics, research trees, KAPI/RRDA data assets, your own generated content, anything. Everything else this framework does (content creation, data assets, sink points) either patches through this same mechanism internally or exists alongside it.

sections.heading: Shape of a patch entry
sections.text: A type: cdo document is just a patches: list. Each entry needs at least one target selector ( target: , allAssetsOfClass: , or an ofClass: scope with filters such as matchTag: , matchName: , producedIn: , where: ), optional modifiers, and a properties: list describing the actual edits. The example below halves mManufactoringDuration on the iron ingot recipe: type : cdo patches : - # ---- one or more selectors are accepted; prefer one clear selector ---- target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C # target: also accepts a sequence of paths, patching every entry with the same properties: # OR: allAssetsOfClass: ... # OR: ofClass: ... + filters (matchTag / matchName / producedIn / ingredient / product / where) # ---- modifiers (all optional) ---- applyToSubclasses : false applyToSpawnedActors : false # ---- the ops ---- properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.5 Each entry needs at least one selector and a non-empty properties: list. The current implementation accumulates matches when selectors are combined, but one selector per entry is easier to audit. One document can hold any number of patch entries.

sections.heading: Hard asset references in native defaults
sections.text: Use full asset object paths for hard-reference properties such as TArray<TObjectPtr<UStaticMesh>> . A YAML sequence replaces the array; string allowlists remain ordinary strings. For example, with Periodic Madness installed: type : cdo patches : - target : /Script/PeriodicMadness.PMCleanerSettings properties : - path : mStaticMeshesCleanlist value : - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Nodes/ResourceNode_OreIron_01.ResourceNode_OreIron_01 KDataForge keeps hard references added to permanent native defaults alive across garbage collection and session changes. These assets remain resident until the game exits, even if a later edit removes them from the array. No YAML opt-in or class declaration change is needed. After upgrading from a build where inspecting these arrays crashed, fully restart the game before loading the pack again.

sections.heading: Inline instances in property arrays
sections.text: An ordinary properties: entry can replace an array of instanced UObject references. Write each array entry as a map with class: and optional nested properties: . KDataForge creates the instance as a subobject of the patched target, then applies the nested property operations. This works for any compatible instanced object array, including schematic dependencies and unlocks. Because set is the default operation, the following patch replaces the complete mSchematicDependencies array on every target. It does not append to existing dependencies: type : cdo patches : - target : - /RSS/Schematics/Flat/Sink_RSS_Flat_Belt.Sink_RSS_Flat_Belt_C - /RSS/Schematics/Flat/Sink_RSS_Flat_Ceiling.Sink_RSS_Flat_Ceiling_C properties : - path : mSchematicDependencies value : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/AvailabilityDependencies/BP_SchematicPurchasedDependency.BP_SchematicPurchasedDependency_C properties : - path : mSchematics value : - /SatisfactoryPlus/Content/SchematicManager/Schematics/Milestones/T1/Schematic_SF+_T1_0.Schematic_SF+_T1_0_C - path : mRequireAllSchematicsToBePurchased value : true - path : mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess value : true class: must resolve to a concrete subclass compatible with the array element type. For example, mUnlocks accepts FGUnlock subclasses and mSchematicDependencies accepts FGAvailabilityDependency subclasses. The nested properties: use the same paths and operations as a top-level CDO patch.

sections.heading: The four things you need to know, and where they’re documented
sections.text: Writing a patch entry means answering four separate questions. Each one is covered by its own page rather than duplicated here: what to target, what operation to apply, how to write the value for the property’s type, and how to address nested/array/map properties in the path itself. Concern Page Selecting what to patch : class path, object path, allAssetsOfClass: , ofClass: scope filters ( matchTag: , matchName: , producedIn: / ingredient: / product: , where: ), applyToSubclasses: , applyToSpawnedActors: , the bare class-name shortcut Targeting What you can do to a value : all 22 operations and which property kinds accept them Operations How to write a value : every property kind’s YAML form (bool, numerics, enums, strings, FText, object/class/soft refs, structs, arrays/sets/maps, gameplay tags) Property Types The path grammar : array indices, map keys, struct/object dereference, authored-name matching YAML Schema → Property Paths Two curated example galleries put all of the above together for real FactoryGame classes: Balancing (recipes, items, resources, schematics, research, categories) and Power & Machines (buildables, power, extractors, pipelines, runtime actor patches).

sections.heading: Diagnostics, never failures
sections.text: An unsupported op×type combination, an unresolvable path, or a target that matches nothing all produce diagnostics. The specific patch entry is skipped, but the rest of the document, and every other document, still applies. Run /kdf report after any change to confirm exactly what was patched and see every warning/error in one place.

sections.heading: Vanilla snapshots
sections.text: Before the first write to a property path on an object, KDataForge records its original text value. The in-game editor uses it for diffing, undo, and changes-only export. The YAML pipeline runs once during initialization and exposes no general reload or document-revert operation. Runtime actor patches are a separate boundary. They apply operations directly to every matching instance and do not preserve player-modified or save-restored values through snapshot comparison.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: A patch “did nothing” and there’s no error : check matchTag / where / producedIn / allAssetsOfClass selectors first. A selector that matches zero objects only warns ( /kdf report ). It doesn’t fail the document, and it’s an easy typo to miss because nothing looks broken until you actually check. Not sure which of the three target selectors to reach for? Targeting → Choosing a selector has a quick lookup table.

pages.title: Property Types
pages.description: One working example for every supported property datatype, and the gotchas specific to each.

sections.heading: Property Types
sections.text: Every properties: entry inside a type: cdo patch (see Patching) targets one reflected UE property, and the value: you write has to match that property's kind. KDataForge's value codec recognizes each UE property class in turn: bool, enum, numeric, string, object/class reference, struct, container. It only falls through to raw UE text-import for anything it doesn't special-case. This page walks through every kind it handles, in the order the codec checks them, so you know exactly what YAML shape to reach for. Pair this with Operations for what you can _do_ to a value once you've written it, and Targeting for picking what object the patch applies to.

sections.heading: bool
sections.text: Booleans accept more than just true/false: yes/no and on/off (case-insensitive) and the bare digits 1/0 all parse too, so you can match whichever style reads best in context: - path: mCanBeDiscarded value: false # true/false, yes/no, on/off, 1/0

sections.heading: int32 / uint8 / int64 (all integer widths)
sections.text: Every plain integer property takes a decimal integer within its reflected type's range: - path: mResourceSinkPoints value: 500 - path: mMenuPriority value: 42 Signed integers accept an optional + or - sign. int64 accepts -9223372036854775808 through 9223372036854775807, inclusive. Values outside those bounds are rejected rather than clamped. Smaller signed types also enforce their own bounds; for example, int32 accepts -2147483648 through 2147483647. Unsigned types require nonnegative values: uint8 accepts 0 through 255, and uint64 accepts 0 through 18446744073709551615. Fractions and exponent notation are not accepted as integer values.

sections.heading: float / double
sections.text: Floating-point properties take a decimal number. Setting mManufactoringDuration to a fraction halves the crafting time, since it's read in seconds: - path: mManufactoringDuration value: 2.5 - path: mEnergyValue value: 300.0

sections.heading: enum (typed `enum class` and `TEnumAsByte`)
sections.text: Unreal exposes two enum styles: the typed enum class and the older TEnumAsByte (a numeric property with an attached enum). Both are handled the same way. Write the value's name, optionally qualified with the enum's own name, or its numeric ordinal: - path: mForm value: RF_LIQUID # plain value name - path: mForm value: EResourceForm::RF_GAS # qualified form - path: mForm value: 2 # numeric value (the enum's underlying ordinal) - path: mStackSize value: SS_HUGE # EStackSize always use the name, not a raw count :::caution A numeric value sets the underlying ordinal, not "the number". mStackSize: 500 is **rejected with a validation error** EStackSize only has 6 valid ordinals (SS_ONE=0 … SS_FLUID=5), and KDataForge refuses any number that isn't one of them, exactly to stop it from silently becoming garbage at every use site that reads mStackSize. Always use the value name unless you specifically know the ordinal you want. ::: Enums marked Bitflags also constrain enum-backed properties: a numeric value must contain only declared bits, and a named value must resolve to one enum entry accepted by that same check. This remains the enum import path: use one name or one numeric value. Pipe-joined names, name sequences, and bitmask append/prepend/remove operations apply to plain integer properties with BitmaskEnum metadata, not enum-backed properties. Reflection exports bitmaskMode for these records so editor validation can derive declared bits from exact enum option values. Without Bitflags metadata, enum-backed values must match a declared enum value, even if the enum carries Unreal's flags marker.

sections.heading: bitmask (integer properties with `BitmaskEnum` metadata)
sections.text: Bitmask properties store several enum flags in one integer. Use a scalar for one flag and a YAML sequence for several flags: - path: mParentTask value: Above - path: mParentTask value: - Above - Left For set, KDataForge also accepts an inline sequence, a |-joined string, or a raw pre-computed integer mask. append/prepend and remove accept named flags only. Names remain readable: - path: mParentTask value: - Above - Left - path: mParentTask value: "Above|Left" - path: mParentTask value: 3 # Above (1) | Left (2) :::caution Plain integer bitmask handling requires a build with WITH_METADATA, property Bitmask and BitmaskEnum metadata, and the referenced enum already loaded. For enums marked Bitflags, named flags support both declared mask values (UseEnumValuesAsMaskValuesInEditor=true) and bit indices. Bit indices 0 through 63 map to 1 << index and must fit the reflected property width. This applies to both signed and unsigned properties: 8-bit properties allow 0..7; 16-bit properties allow 0..15; 32-bit properties allow 0..31; 64-bit properties allow 0..63. set, export, append/prepend, and remove preserve the high bit, including bit 31 in int32 and bit 63 in int64. For set, raw integer masks are nonnegative unsigned decimal bit patterns bounded by the reflected property width, including signed properties. int32 accepts raw masks through 4294967295; int64 accepts raw masks through 18446744073709551615. For example, 2147483648 sets bit 31 in int32, and 9223372036854775808 sets bit 63 in int64. Masks must contain only declared bits for enums marked Bitflags; without that enum marker, the resulting value must match a valid enum value. Named flags must also fit the property width. These bitmask rules do not change the signed ranges of ordinary integer properties described above. For enums that use declared mask values (UseEnumValuesAsMaskValuesInEditor=true), export fails if the runtime value cannot be rebuilt losslessly by OR-ing declared flag values. KDataForge logs a LogKDataForge error naming the property, enum, and undeclared bits; add matching enum flags or correct the property value. A raw numeric set mask can import such a value when it fits the declared-bit and property-width rules, but it does not bypass the export failure. Negative enum values and values-as-masks using bit 63 are unsupported: Unreal represents UEnum values as signed int64. This restriction does not affect bit-index 63, whose enum value is the positive integer 63. If property metadata is stripped or the enum cannot be resolved, a plain integer property falls back to ordinary numeric conversion and its normal signed or unsigned range. Named bitmask forms and bitmask mutation operations are unavailable. Do not assume named integer bitmasks work in a Shipping build; check whether that build retains metadata. Enum-backed properties have their own conversion path; see Enums. See Operations for mutation ops and Delivery Task Trees for every EKAPIDeliveryTaskParent bit. :::

sections.heading: FString
sections.text: Plain reflected strings take a quoted scalar as-is, no escaping beyond normal YAML quoting rules: - path: mSomeString value: 'Hello Ficsit'

sections.heading: FName
sections.text: FName properties look identical to FString in YAML. The codec just wraps the text in an FName before writing it. This matters for fields UE compares by name identity, like the quick-switch group below, rather than by string content: - path: mQuickSwitchGroup value: 'ingots'

sections.heading: FText: plain (culture-invariant)
sections.text: A bare scalar for an FText property produces a culture-invariant literal text useful for internal/debug strings, but not localizable. For anything player-facing, prefer the keyed form below or route it through Localization: - path: mDisplayName value: 'Better Iron Ingot'

sections.heading: FText: localized (key/namespace/source)
sections.text: Passing a map instead of a scalar creates a properly keyed, localizable FText instead of an invariant literal. The key field is required, while ns and source are optional. A map containing only source is invalid; use a scalar for culture-invariant text. This uses the same runtime-safe construction path the localization system relies on: - path: mDisplayName value: key: BetterIronIngot_Name ns: MyPack source: Better Iron Ingot

sections.heading: FText: StringTable references
sections.text: Use stringTable and key to retain an existing Unreal StringTable entry, including its translations and table identity. Use the table's registered ID or its full asset object path: - path: mDisplayName value: stringTable: /SatisfactoryPlus/ST_SatisfactoryPlus.ST_SatisfactoryPlus key: CDOBuilding_MiniExtractior.PropertyContainer_0.mDisplayName Both fields must be non-empty strings. Do not combine stringTable with ns or source. The table belongs to its original mod and must remain available. A missing table or key uses Unreal's missing-text diagnostic/placeholder; this form does not create tables or entries. Exporting a StringTable text produces this same map; copying, reverting and re-exporting retain its table identity instead of the currently displayed language. The in-game inspector edits table ID and key separately from the resolved text. A raw scalar containing LOCTABLE(...) remains a literal; convert native exports to the map above. Use value: null to clear an FText.

sections.heading: Object reference (hard)
sections.text: Hard object references (UObject* properties) take a full asset or object path, resolved and loaded immediately. Use none (or an empty string) to null one out: - path: mCategory value: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/ItemCategories/Cat_Ingots.Cat_Ingots_C - path: mSmallIcon value: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/UI/IconDesc_IronIngot_64.IconDesc_IronIngot_64 - path: mConveyorMesh value: none # null out a reference with none or ""

sections.heading: Class reference (`TSubclassOf`)
sections.text: Class references also take a path, but the codec tries several forms in order before giving up: 1. The path as given. 2. The path with a _C suffix appended (Blueprint class paths are frequently written without it). 3. The asset-path-to-object-path expansion. 4. For a bare name with no / or . at all, a generated-content id from the current pack first, then from every loaded pack. 5. If no generated class matches, a search across every currently loaded class by short name (see Targeting for the same shortcut applied to target:). - path: mOverriddenCategory value: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/ItemCategories/Cat_Ingots.Cat_Ingots_C # BP class (`_C` auto-retried) - path: mClassToScanFor value: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableResourceExtractor # native class - path: mProducedIn value: Recipe_MyGeneratedRecipe # generated-content id from this pack, if present - path: mFluidClass value: Desc_Water # bare-name shortcut for Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C see Targeting

sections.heading: Soft references (`TSoftObjectPtr` / `TSoftClassPtr`)
sections.text: The value is stored as a path string and never force-loads the target. The referenced asset only loads if and when the game actually needs it: - path: mPersistentBigIcon value: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/UI/IconDesc_IronIngot_256.IconDesc_IronIngot_256 # stored as a path, not loaded until the game needs it

sections.heading: Struct: native text form
sections.text: For structs with a native text representation, like FLinearColor, FVector, FGuid, and FGameplayTag, a plain scalar is parsed through that format. This is the same round-trip form the editor's "Copy" action produces: - path: mFluidColor value: '(R=255,G=100,B=0,A=255)'

sections.heading: Struct: map form (member names, Blueprint-authored names work too)
sections.text: Any struct also accepts a YAML map keyed by member name. This is resolved through the same flexible member lookup used elsewhere, so Blueprint-authored display names work, not just the raw C++ field name. Each value is recursively converted through this same codec for that member's type: - path: mFluidColor value: R: 255 G: 100 B: 0 A: 255

sections.heading: Struct: positional sequence form (members in declaration order)
sections.text: A YAML sequence assigns struct members positionally, in C++ declaration order. This is handy for terse, well-known structs, like a color or vector, where the member order never changes: - path: mScannerLightColor value: - 1.0 - 0.5 - 0.0 - 1.0

sections.heading: Nested structs (any depth)
sections.text: Struct members that are themselves structs recurse through the same map/sequence/scalar rules to arbitrary depth. Deeply nested data, like a struct inside a struct inside an array, reads and writes exactly like the flat cases above, just indented: - path: mCustomScannableDetails value: ScannableType: STY_Default NewDetails: Range: 500

sections.heading: TArray
sections.text: Setting a TArray property, the default set operation, empties the array and rebuilds it from the given sequence element by element. The value you write always fully replaces whatever was there before, rather than merging into it: - path: mIngredients value: # `set` replaces the whole array - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C Amount: 2 - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Coal/Desc_Coal.Desc_Coal_C Amount: 1

sections.heading: Instanced UObject arrays
sections.text: Arrays whose elements are instanced UObject references also use a sequence, but each element can define a new instance with class: and nested properties:. KDataForge creates the instance as a subobject of the patched target. With the default set op, the array is replaced rather than merged: - path: mSchematicDependencies value: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/AvailabilityDependencies/BP_SchematicPurchasedDependency.BP_SchematicPurchasedDependency_C properties: - path: mSchematics value: - /SatisfactoryPlus/Content/SchematicManager/Schematics/Milestones/T1/Schematic_SF+_T1_0.Schematic_SF+_T1_0_C - path: mRequireAllSchematicsToBePurchased value: true The class: must be a concrete subclass accepted by the array. For example, mUnlocks accepts FGUnlock subclasses and mSchematicDependencies accepts FGAvailabilityDependency subclasses. Nested entries use the same property paths and operations as top-level patch entries. The same instanced-object entry shape also works with array append, prepend, and insert when you want to add entries without replacing the whole array: - path: mUnlocks op: append value: class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties: - path: mRecipes value: - Recipe_MyGeneratedRecipe

sections.heading: Array element access (index paths)
sections.text: Rather than replacing a whole array, a path can index straight into one element, and from there into that element's own members. This lets you tweak a single ingredient's amount without re-listing every other ingredient: - path: mIngredients[0].Amount value: 3

sections.heading: TSet
sections.text: TSet properties also take a plain YAML sequence. Entries collapse if the type's equality would make them duplicates, since a set has no concept of ordering or repeated elements: - path: mSubCategories # sets take sequences; duplicates collapse value: - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/ItemCategories/SC_Smelted.SC_Smelted_C

sections.heading: TMap
sections.text: A TMap property takes a YAML map. Each key is converted through the map's own key property type before insertion, not just kept as a raw string. A bracketed key path lets you update a single entry in place instead of replacing the whole map: - path: mSomeMap value: Iron: 10 # keys converted through the map's key property type Copper: 20 - path: mSomeMap["Iron"] # single-entry access via key path value: 15

sections.heading: FGameplayTag
sections.text: A single gameplay tag is a struct with a native text importer under the hood, so it takes a plain dotted scalar just like any other native-text struct: - path: mStatisticGameplayTag value: KMods.AlternateRecipe

sections.heading: FGameplayTagContainer
sections.text: A tag container takes a sequence of tags. As with arrays, the default set operation replaces the whole container rather than adding to it. See Operations for the append/prepend/remove/clear variants that mutate a container instead, and Game Tags for registering your own tags before you reference them: - path: mGameplayTags value: # `set` replaces all tags - KMods.WikiExclude - MyPack.Special

sections.heading: Anything else (fallback)
sections.text: Any reflected type not listed above still works. The codec falls back to UE's own generic text import, so it accepts whatever text form the editor's "Copy" action produces for that property. This holds even for exotic or third-party struct types this page doesn't know about by name: - path: mSomeExoticStruct value: '(InnerValue=3,Flags=(bEnabled=True))'

pages.title: Type: recipe
pages.description: Generating new recipes from YAML, registering existing recipe classes, and how registration into SML's content registry actually happens.

sections.heading: Type: recipe
sections.text: The recipe type runs in the Recipes stage, which comes after the whole Items stage. That means a recipe can freely reference anything item / resource / building / unlock you just generated. It loads changes only during session initialization, so a change here needs a restart. Its entries key is recipes , its default parent is /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe , and its required base class is /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe (or a subclass of it). It is also the first type to support register-only mode via class: . recipe is the first content-creation type you’ll meet that supports two modes : generate a brand-new recipe class ( id: ), or register an existing class you didn’t generate ( class: ). Both modes end with the recipe queued into SML’s UModContentRegistry (unless you turn that off).

sections.heading: Mode 1: generate a new recipe
sections.text: A generated recipe is just a subclass of FGRecipe whose CDO you set up entirely through properties: . mIngredients and mProduct describe the item/amount pairs consumed and produced, mManufactoringDuration is the craft time in seconds, and mProducedIn lists which buildable(s) can craft it. super-ingot.recipe.yml puts all of that together for a recipe that turns 2 iron ingots into 1 of a generated item, craftable in a Smelter Mk.1: super-ingot.recipe.yml type : recipe recipes : - id : Recipe_MySuperIngot properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Ingot - path : mIngredients value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount : 2 - path : mProduct value : - ItemClass : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot Amount : 1 - path : mManufactoringDuration value : 4.0 - path : mProducedIn value : - /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/SmelterMk1/Build_SmelterMk1.Build_SmelterMk1_C No parent: is needed here, since it defaults to FGRecipe . No include: is needed for the Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot product reference either, because Items has already fully run by the time Recipes starts.

sections.heading: Mode 2: register an existing class, no generation
sections.text: Sometimes you, or another mod, already has a compiled or Blueprint recipe class sitting unused. Maybe it’s a hidden recipe another mod ships but never registers, or one you built yourself in the editor as a Blueprint. Swap id: for class: and KDataForge registers it without generating anything: type : recipe recipes : - class : /Game/SomeMod/Recipes/Recipe_Hidden.Recipe_Hidden_C # register, don't generate properties: still works in this mode if you want to tweak the existing class’s CDO at the same time you register it.

sections.heading: Removing recipes
sections.text: A type: recipe document can also declare a top-level remove: sequence. Each entry is either a bare class reference (a full Unreal class path, a bare loaded class name, or a generated content id from this or another loaded KDataForge pack) or a filter map that removes every recipe passing the scope filters ( producedIn: , ingredient: , product: , matchName: , matchTag: , where: ; the scope defaults to FGRecipe ). Removal-only documents are valid, and remove: can also be mixed with normal recipes: entries in the same document: type : recipe remove : - /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronPlate.Recipe_IronPlate_C - Recipe_IronPlateReinforced_C - Recipe_MyGeneratedRecipe - producedIn : Build_HadronCollider_C # every Particle Accelerator recipe - matchName : Recipe_Alternate_* # every alternate recipe A bare reference names the exact recipe class to suppress; it does not remove subclasses. If a generated id is ambiguous across packs, KDataForge logs the same ambiguity diagnostic used for other short-id class references. Filter maps are stored as rules and re-checked on every recipe grant, so recipes that load later in the session are covered. Removals are applied after queued registrations, so an explicit remove: wins over a register: for the same class. The consolidated guide, including how recipe removal interacts with schematics and saves, is Removing Content . Recipe removal is the one content removal kind that writes back into the save. SML has no RemoveRecipe API, and the authoritative list is the save-backed recipe manager list. KDataForge therefore blocks future recipe grants with native hooks and sweeps recipes restored from an existing save during world initialization. Uninstalling the pack self-heals on the next load because purchased schematics re-apply their recipe unlocks without the removal hook. Packaged runtime builds install both singular and batch recipe-add prevention hooks. Unreal Editor PIE still runs the initialization sweep, but those native hooks are compiled out there; a recipe granted again later in the same PIE session can therefore reappear. Verify prevention behavior in a packaged game session. Removal never revokes schematic purchases. If a schematic was already purchased, that purchase stays in the save; only the named recipe is kept out of the available recipe list while the pack is installed. To hide the unlock source as well, pair this with schematic remove: .

sections.heading: register: and auto-propagation
sections.text: Every recipe entry, generated or register-only, accepts a register: flag. It decides whether the class actually gets queued for UModContentRegistry registration at all, as opposed to merely existing so other YAML can point at it: type : recipe recipes : - id : Recipe_MySuperIngot register : true # default omit unless you specifically want to skip registration properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration value : 4 register: true is the default, so the recipe is queued unless you set it to false explicitly. SML’s own auto-propagation then takes over: registering a schematic that unlocks this recipe also registers the recipe, and the recipe’s ingredient and product items, automatically. You don’t have to register every layer by hand, just the top of the chain you actually care about, which is usually the schematic. Set register: false if you want the class to exist, so other YAML can reference it, but not be independently discoverable. This is useful for an internal helper recipe that only ever appears nested inside something else.

sections.heading: Editing existing recipes in bulk
sections.text: Changing recipes that already exist is a type: cdo job, and recipes have three selectors of their own: producedIn: (crafted in a building, or any building deriving from a base class), ingredient: and product: (consume / produce an item, or any item deriving from a base class). They default their scope to FGRecipe , accept a single class or a list, and combine with each other and with where: : type : cdo patches : - producedIn : /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer # every machine recipe … ingredient : Desc_IronIngot_C # … that consumes Iron Ingot properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.8 Every form is covered on Targeting , and Balancing has copyable examples.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: “My new item has no recipe in a fresh save” : check that something registers the recipe. Either register: true here (the default), or a schematic that unlocks it, whose own registration auto-propagates down to this recipe, will do it. A recipe that’s generated but never registered anywhere simply never reaches UModContentRegistry , and the game won’t know it exists. “class: gave me an error about register-only mode” : class: (register-only) is only valid for recipe , schematic , and research documents. item / resource / building / unlock can only generate ( id: ). See Type: item for why. A full pack tying a generated item + this recipe + a schematic + translations together lives in End-to-End Pack .

pages.title: Removing Content
pages.description: Taking recipes, schematics, and research trees out of the game with `remove:`, by exact class or by filter, what each removal does to an existing save, and how it combines with resource-node purges and sublevel blocking.

sections.heading: Removing Content
sections.text: KDataForge can take existing content out of the game as well as patch or generate it. Three document types accept a top-level remove: sequence, and each entry is either one exact class or a filter rule that removes every class of that type matching the same selectors type: cdo patches use : Document type Removes Default filter scope Save impact type: recipe craftable recipes (incl. build-gun recipes) /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe writes the save (recipe list is saved); self-heals after uninstall type: schematic milestones, MAM schematics, shop entries, … /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic save-clean; purchases stay type: research / mam M.A.M. research trees /Script/FactoryGame.FGResearchTree save-clean; research progress stays Two neighbouring features remove world content rather than registered classes and have their own pages: type: resourcenode destroys placed resource nodes, and type: sublevel stops optional sublevels from streaming in. Both accept the same filter rules; the differences are summarised below . Nothing else has a removal path. item , resource , building , unlock , and class documents do not accept remove: : there is no live registry to take an item out of. To make an item disappear in practice, remove the recipes that produce it and the schematics that unlock those recipes.

sections.heading: The two entry forms
sections.text: A bare class reference removes exactly that class. Full Unreal paths, bare loaded class names, and generated-content short ids from this or another loaded pack all resolve; subclasses are never implied: type : recipe remove : - /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronPlate.Recipe_IronPlate_C - Recipe_IronPlateReinforced_C # bare class name - Recipe_MyGeneratedRecipe # generated-content id A filter rule is a map with any of the scope-filter keys, matchTag: , matchName: , producedIn: , ingredient: , product: , where: , optionally narrowed by an explicit ofClass: . It removes every class of the document’s type in the scope that passes all the filters on the entry: type : recipe remove : # every alternate recipe, by naming convention - matchName : Recipe_Alternate_* # every recipe crafted in the Particle Accelerator - producedIn : /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/HadronCollider/Build_HadronCollider.Build_HadronCollider_C # every recipe that consumes Uranium, in any building - ingredient : Desc_OreUranium_C # every recipe of a mod, by content folder, that takes longer than a minute - ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe matchName : /Game/SomeMod/Recipes/* where : path : mManufactoringDuration greaterThan : 60 The scope defaults to the document type’s base class, so ofClass: is only needed to narrow it, for example to a mod’s own recipe base class. Bare references and filter rules can be mixed in one remove: sequence, and remove: can sit beside the normal generation entries ( recipes: , schematics: , research: ) in the same document. Filter rules are predicates, not lists . They are stored as rules and evaluated against every class the game presents, so a Blueprint recipe that loads later in the session is still tested and removed. The load report ( /kdf report ) prints an Info line per rule with how many loaded classes it matched at apply time ( Removal rule '… where matchName=Recipe_Alternate_*' currently matches 92 loaded class(es) ), which is the fastest way to check a filter before shipping it.

sections.heading: Recipes
sections.text: Removing a recipe keeps it out of the list of craftable recipes: it disappears from machines, the Craft Bench, and, for build recipes, the build gun (the buildable itself stays in the world). The game has no “remove recipe” API and its authoritative list is saved , so KDataForge does two things: Prevention : every grant of a removed recipe is cancelled the moment the game tries it, which also covers the unlocks purchased schematics re-apply on every load. Cleanup : recipes an existing save already restored are swept out during world initialization, before the recipe manager and its replication component read the list. Because the sweep writes the save, it runs on the server only; a client’s list is server-authoritative and arrives already filtered. The write is not permanent: uninstalling the pack removes the prevention hook, and the next load re-applies every purchased schematic’s unlocks, so the recipes come back. type : recipe remove : # take a vanilla recipe away - Recipe_IronPlateReinforced_C # …and every recipe that produced its ingredient in an Assembler - product : Desc_IronScrew_C producedIn : Build_AssemblerMk1_C Note Packaged builds install both the single and the batch recipe-grant prevention hooks. In the Unreal Editor (PIE) only the initialization sweep runs; a recipe granted again later in the same PIE session can reappear. Verify prevention in a packaged game. Removal never revokes schematic purchases. To also hide the unlock source, remove the schematic too (below).

sections.heading: Schematics
sections.text: Schematic removal goes through SML’s content registry filter before the schematic manager builds its per-session list. Nothing is written to the save, so uninstalling the pack brings the schematic back on the next load. Bare references and filter rules both work; ofClass: defaults to FGSchematic : type : schematic remove : - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C # every tier 8+ milestone - ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic where : - path : mTechTier greaterOrEqual : 8 - path : mType equals : EST_Milestone # every schematic that unlocks a Quantum Encoder recipe - where : path : mUnlocks[*].mRecipes[*].mProducedIn contains : Build_QuantumEncoder_C Removal does not revoke purchases. An already-purchased schematic stays in the save and keeps re-applying its unlocks on load, including the recipes it granted. Pair schematic removal with recipe removal when the content itself must become unavailable: no-nuclear.schematic.yml type : schematic remove : - Schematic_8-1_C # Nuclear Power milestone no-nuclear.recipe.yml type : recipe remove : - product : Desc_NuclearFuelRod_C - ingredient : Desc_OreUranium_C

sections.heading: Research trees
sections.text: Research-tree removal works exactly like schematic removal: the tree is filtered out of SML’s content registry before the M.A.M. builds its list, nothing is saved, and uninstalling the pack brings the tree back. type: mam is an alias for research and accepts the same grammar; ofClass: defaults to FGResearchTree : type : research remove : - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/BPD_ResearchTree_Caterium.BPD_ResearchTree_Caterium_C # every research tree another mod ships, by folder - matchName : /Game/SomeMod/Research/* Removal does not revoke progress: already-unlocked or completed research state stays in the save, and unlocks it granted stay granted. To remove recipes granted through that progression, add a type: recipe remove: too.

sections.heading: Ordering and conflicts
sections.text: Removals apply after registrations, whichever pack each came from. An explicit remove: therefore always beats a register: (or generation) of the same class. A removal rule from one pack can name a class another pack generated (the generated-content id resolves across loaded packs; an ambiguous id logs the usual ambiguity diagnostic). Removing a parent class never removes its subclasses. Use a filter rule when you mean a family. Schematic and research-tree removal filters every peer’s own list from the same YAML. A client without the pack keeps the schematic in its local list, so ship removal packs to every process in a multiplayer session. Recipe removal is server-authoritative and needs the pack on the server.

sections.heading: Resource nodes and sublevels
sections.text: type: resourcenode purges placed nodes by their effective resource descriptor, and type: sublevel blocks provider data assets before their levels stream in. Both accept the same filter keys instead of one exact reference: type : resourcenode remove : # every uranium descriptor (a vanilla one plus any modded variant deriving from it) - ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor matchName : Desc_OreUranium* nodeTypes : [ Node ] type : sublevel conditions : hasMod : RefinedRDLib block : - ofClass : /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset # required: sublevel assets have no default scope matchName : DA_Optional_* Unlike recipe rules, these two expand their filters once , when the document applies, against the descriptor classes and assets loaded at that moment; the load report says how many matched. Resource-node destruction can outlive the pack (the game saves destruction tombstones), so read the persistence warnings on the Resources page before shipping one.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: “ remove map entries need a filter” : a map entry must carry at least one of matchTag , matchName , producedIn , ingredient , product , where . ofClass: alone selects nothing; to remove one class, write it as a bare reference instead. A filter rule reports “currently matches 0 loaded class(es)” : the scope or the filter is too strict, or the classes are not loaded yet. Recipe rules still catch later-loading classes; for schematic and research rules, check the count on the next session once the game has loaded them, or name the classes explicitly. The recipe is gone but the item still shows in the codex / build menu : removal only affects the recipe list. Items and buildings are not registry-removable; hide them via a type: cdo patch ( mCanBeDiscarded , categories, …) or remove the schematics that reference them. Everything came back after uninstalling the pack : that is the design. All three removal kinds are non-destructive to the save’s purchase and progress state and restore themselves. The full grammar, including where remove: may appear, lives in the YAML schema .

pages.title: Type: research
pages.description: Generating new M.A.M. research trees from YAML, registering existing ones, and how this fits alongside schematics and recipes.

sections.heading: Type: research
sections.text: This entry type runs at the Research stage, after Schematics . It does not support live-reload, so changes require a restart. Its entries key is research , and the default parent is /Script/FactoryGame.FGResearchTree . The required base class is the same, /Script/FactoryGame.FGResearchTree (or a subclass). Register-only mode via class: is supported here too, with the same duality as recipe / schematic . research (or its filename-convention alias mam , for example my-tree.mam.yml ) generates or registers UFGResearchTree -derived classes: the individual M.A.M. (Molecular Analysis Machine) research trees themselves, not the schematics nested inside them. Like Recipes , it supports two modes. You can generate a brand-new tree with id: , or register an existing one untouched except for a property tweak with class: . The mode-selection mechanics are identical to recipe , so see that page’s “register an existing class” section if you need the general rules. This page only covers what’s specific to trees.

sections.heading: Editing an existing research tree
sections.text: Most of the time you don’t need to generate a research tree. The base game’s trees already exist, and you just want to rename or retune one. That’s register-only mode, or honestly, just a plain cdo patch: both work identically for editing something that already exists. Here’s an example renaming the Mycelia tree’s display text: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C properties : - path : mDisplayName value : ' Mycelia (Rebalanced) '

sections.heading: Generating a new research tree
sections.text: Use type: research with id: when you actually want a new tree. This applies when your pack adds a whole new content line that deserves its own M.A.M. entry, rather than living inside an existing tree. mDisplayName is the tree’s name in the menu, and mMenuPriority controls where it sorts relative to other trees: my-content-line.research.yml type : research research : - id : MyContentLineTree properties : - path : mDisplayName value : My Content Line - path : mMenuPriority value : 50 register: true (default) queues it into SML’s UModContentRegistry per-world before the freeze, same mechanism as recipes and schematics.

sections.heading: Gating tree unlock and visibility
sections.text: Research entries accept two instanced FGAvailabilityDependency lists: unlockDependencies: appends to mUnlockDependencies ; visibilityDependencies: appends to mVisibilityDependencies . type : research research : - id : MyContentLineTree unlockDependencies : - class : /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties : - path : mSchematics value : - Schematic_MyPrerequisite visibilityDependencies : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/AvailabilityDependencies/BP_GamePhaseReachedDependency.BP_GamePhaseReachedDependency_C properties : - path : mGamePhase value : EGP_EarlyGame Native and Blueprint paths both work. Known native classes automatically remap to concrete Blueprint implementations. Full inventory: Availability Dependency Classes . ⚠️ A schematic does not “point at” a tree. Unlike mProducedIn / mProduct on a recipe, there is no field on UFGSchematic that associates it with a research tree. The relationship works the other way around: the tree’s mNodes array visually places schematics inside it.

sections.heading: Adding and removing visual nodes
sections.text: Node mutation lives directly on each research: entry. addNodes: is additive: it appends real BPD_ResearchTreeNode instances and does not replace an existing node implicitly. Each useful node names a schematic: and a coordinate: ; it can also define parents: , nodesToUnhide: , unhiddenBy: , and optional properties: . A graph reference may be a literal coordinate or another node’s schematic class. References work both for nodes in the same list, regardless of their order, and for nodes that are already present in the tree. This example adds one node to the vanilla Mycelia tree without re-registering that existing tree: research : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C register : false autoPath : true addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_MyExtension coordinate : X : 4 Y : 2 parents : - schematic : Schematic_ExistingParent nodesToUnhide : - X : 5 Y : 2 For a concrete base-game example, this adds the Pure Super Ingot schematic after the Mycelia Gas Mask research node: type : research research : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/BPD_ResearchTree_Mycelia.BPD_ResearchTree_Mycelia_C register : false autoPath : true addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_PureSuperIngot coordinate : X : 4 Y : 6 parents : - schematic : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/Research_Mycelia_GasMask.Research_Mycelia_GasMask_C With autoPath: true , KDataForge turns every resolved parents: edge from addNodes: into a matching straight road on the parent. For custom or bent roads, use autoPath: false with childrenAndRoads: ; a parent can provide one block map with key and points fields or a sequence of them for multiple children. Set class: on a node only when a custom UFGResearchTreeNode subclass is required. Its ordinary properties: list remains available, but convenience fields that the subclass does not expose are reported and skipped rather than failing the whole document. To remove a node, select it by schematic class with tree-entry-level removeNodes: . It accepts a scalar class reference or a block map with schematic: . KDataForge applies removals before addNodes: additions in the same tree entry, then removes the node and all surviving Parents , NodesToUnhide , UnhiddenBy , and ChildrenAndRoads references to its coordinate. addNodes: then appends replacements or unrelated new nodes. autoPath: true applies to those additions and writes straight roads from every resolved parent: research : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C autoPath : true removeNodes : - Schematic_ObsoleteExtension addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_NewExtension coordinate : X : 6 Y : 3 parents : - schematic : Schematic_ExistingParent For a move or replacement, use the same schematic in removeNodes: and addNodes: with its new coordinate. Removal still happens first, so duplicate nodes and stale roads are not retained. nodes: remains a legacy alias. When both keys are present, addNodes: wins and KDataForge warns that nodes: was ignored. autoPath: works with addNodes: and legacy nodes: .

sections.heading: Removing research trees
sections.text: A type: research document accepts a top-level remove: sequence. type: mam is an alias for research , so it accepts the same removal grammar. Each entry is either a bare class reference (a full Unreal class path, a bare loaded class name, or a generated content id from this or another loaded KDataForge pack) or a filter map that removes every tree passing the scope filters ( matchName: , matchTag: , where: ; the scope defaults to FGResearchTree ). Removal-only documents are valid, and remove: can also be mixed with normal research: entries: type : research remove : - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/BPD_ResearchTree_Caterium.BPD_ResearchTree_Caterium_C - MyGeneratedResearchTree - matchName : /Game/SomeMod/Research/* # every tree another mod ships, by folder A bare reference names the exact research-tree class to remove; it does not remove subclasses. If a generated id is ambiguous across packs, KDataForge logs the same ambiguity diagnostic used for other short-id class references. Removals run after registrations, so an explicit remove: wins over a register: for the same class. The consolidated guide is Removing Content . Research-tree removal is save-clean. KDataForge removes the class from SML’s content registry before the M.A.M. builds its per-session tree list, so uninstalling the pack brings the tree back on the next load. Removal does not revoke progress. Already-unlocked or completed research state stays in the save, and any unlocks already granted by that progress stay granted. This only removes the tree from the current available research-tree list while the pack is installed. To remove recipes granted through that progression, also use recipe remove: .

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: New tree doesn’t appear in the M.A.M. menu : confirm registration succeeded ( /kdf report ). An empty tree with no nodes may also simply not render meaningfully in the M.A.M. UI, so see the callout above and the linked tutorial for what’s currently achievable. Just want to rename or reprioritise a vanilla tree : don’t generate anything. Use a plain cdo patch as shown above. It’s simpler and doesn’t touch the content registry at all. Want a schematic unlocked through research instead of the HUB : that’s just mType: EST_MAM on an ordinary Type: schematic entry. Nothing tree-specific about it.

pages.title: Resource node placement and replacement
pages.description: Add ordinary resource nodes or safely reuse nearby nodes with range and overlap checks.

sections.heading: Resource node placement and replacement
sections.text: type: resourcenode supports add, replace, and the existing remove rules. Positions and distances use Unreal centimetres. Coordinates are world coordinates; rotation order is pitch, yaw, roll in degrees. type: resourcenode add: - id: northern-iron resource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C position: [10000, 20000, 1200] purity: Pure checkRange: 500 reuseExisting: true allowToMove: true preventOverlap: true overlapClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceNodeBase replace: - id: nearby-copper resource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreCopper/Desc_OreCopper.Desc_OreCopper_C fromResource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C position: [30000, 20000, 1200] checkRange: 500 allowToMove: false purity: Normal Use stable, unique id values across all add and replace entries in a pack. Identity combines pack reference and entry ID. Changing either creates a different placement.

sections.heading: Adding nodes
sections.text: add first looks for a nearby ordinary node when reuseExisting: true. A matching node is updated in place. Otherwise KDataForge creates an infinite ordinary node with replicated resource and purity, using the game's resource mesh/decal data. Every added node owns a separate actual AFGNodeMeshActor; each peer creates its local mesh actor and links it to the resource node. Use descriptors with suitable node visuals. Existing extractor restrictions still apply; adding a node does not automatically grant scanner unlocks or permit new resources in an extractor. | Field | Default | Meaning | | id | Required | Stable identity, unique within pack. | | resource | Required | Resource descriptor class. | | position | Required | Three finite coordinates [x, y, z]. | | rotation | [0, 0, 0] | Finite [pitch, yaw, roll]. | | purity | Normal for additions | Impure, Normal, or Pure. Replacement/reuse preserves existing purity when omitted from replace. | | checkRange | 500 | Search and optional overlap radius. Greater than zero, at most 100000 cm. | | reuseExisting | true | For add, reuse nearest ordinary node instead of creating a duplicate. | | allowToMove | true | Move a reused/replaced node and its linked mesh to requested transform. | | preventOverlap | false | For newly created nodes, reject location when an actor of overlapClass is in range. | | overlapClass | /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceNodeBase | Actor class for overlap prevention. | | fromResource | Any | Restrict replacement/reuse selection to an existing resource descriptor. | | mesh | Resource default | Optional cooked UStaticMesh asset path. | | material | Resource default | Optional material/material-instance asset path overriding slot 0. Mutually exclusive with materials. | | materials | Resource defaults | Optional list of up to 64 material asset paths or null, indexed by material slot. null clears that slot override. | Range checks follow the KBFL spawner pattern: reuse an existing node first, then optionally check whether the new spawn area is free. Overlap prevention uses collision overlaps plus a distance fallback for actors without suitable collision. KDataForge chooses nearest ordinary node deterministically; equal distances use actor path order. It does not remove unrelated nodes outside configured locations.

sections.heading: Replacing nodes
sections.text: replace requires an existing ordinary node within checkRange. It updates that node in place; it never deletes the node or transfers an extractor to another actor. Linked mesh/materials update on every peer. If no mesh actor exists, KDataForge creates and links an AFGNodeMeshActor. No match means no node is created. Streamed-in nodes are checked when their level or actor becomes available. radius is accepted as a replacement-only alias for checkRange. Do not provide both. reuseExisting, preventOverlap, and overlapClass control additions; they do not change explicit replacement selection. Occupied nodes and nodes with unresolved extractor links are preserved. Nodes with saved resource or purity overrides are also preserved: these include nodes modified by the game's resource randomization. Such targets produce a warning. Configure placement on a world without randomized overrides, or use add with an unoccupied location and reuseExisting: false. Fracking cores, satellites, geysers, and resource deposits cannot be created or replaced by these fields. The existing remove syntax retains its own node-type filters and occupancy options.

sections.heading: Reload, saves, and multiplayer
sections.text: Newly created nodes are saved with their pack/entry identity and are reused on later loads. Repeated loading does not intentionally create duplicate nodes. Removing an addition retains its occupied node. Unoccupied obsolete additions are removed at the next world load before the game's node manager initializes; hot reload retains them until then. For an unoccupied reused/replaced node, hot reload restores its previous descriptor, purity, transform, and linked mesh before applying new rules. If an extractor occupies that node, restoration is deferred; a warning explains why it remains unchanged. Replacement ownership and original descriptor, purity, transform, mesh, and materials are stored in a server-side save record. Resource/purity overrides persist and replicate. Reloading the same rule can restore its owned replacement even when an extractor was installed afterwards; that extractor is never moved. Removing or changing the rule restores original values when the node is unoccupied. Keep KDataForge installed while removing a replacement pack so its saved restoration record can be processed. New actors spawn only on authority and replicate their initialization to clients. Every peer must load the same pack for replacement of existing level nodes and local mesh/scanner updates. This feature does not distribute pack files or provide a pack checksum handshake. Scanner caches and radar scans refresh after placement processing; standard research controls whether a resource can be selected in the scanner. Avoid combining contradictory purge and placement rules for the same resource. Review warnings after changing IDs, moving occupied locations, or editing packs used by an existing save.

pages.title: Resource node appearance
pages.description: Maintain material slots and hidden mesh actors on existing resource nodes, including streamed nodes and local client meshes.

sections.heading: Resource node appearance
sections.text: Use type: resourcenode with visuals to override existing nodes' mesh materials, or hideMeshes to hide selected static mesh assets and disable collision on their mesh actors. These rules run independently on server and clients. They also handle nodes and mesh actors that appear later or stream into the world. They do not create or destroy resource nodes. Save the configuration as node_appearance.resourcenode.yml in your pack. Replace the example material with an asset shipped by your mod: type: resourcenode visuals: - resource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C materials: - slot: 0 material: /MyMod/Materials/MI_Node.MI_Node meshActorsPerTick: 1 resource names an exact resource descriptor class. Its subclasses are not included. Material mappings skip resource deposit actors. materials is a non-empty list of slot/material records. Slots are zero-based integers from 0 through 63; each slot may occur only once per resource. Unlisted slots remain unchanged. Write numbers as numbers, not quoted strings. Material paths name material or material-instance objects, without _C. Descriptors and assets must be cooked and available in installed mods on every peer. Invalid visual entries or unresolved material/mesh references reject that resource-node document. Keep independent placement and appearance edits in separate files.

sections.heading: Hide meshes
sections.text: type: resourcenode hideMeshes: - /MyMod/ResourceNodes/SM_OldNode.SM_OldNode Every entry must resolve to a static mesh asset. Matching uses exact mesh identity. The matching mesh actor and its static mesh component become hidden; actor collision is disabled. Hiding takes precedence over material assignments, works without a linked node, and also applies to matching meshes linked to deposits. The resource node itself remains.

sections.heading: Timing, overrides and reload
sections.text: meshActorsPerTick defaults to 1 and accepts integers from 1 through 1024. It limits pending mesh resolutions and round-robin maintenance separately; one pending node lookup is also processed each tick. Larger budgets catch up faster at higher per-frame cost. The field requires visuals or hideMeshes in the same document. Mesh actors whose node link is not ready are retried. Rules continue enforcing configured appearance afterwards. Later applied documents replace earlier material mappings for the same resource descriptor. Repeated resources in a single document are rejected. Hide lists from active documents are combined. The last explicitly configured maintenance budget wins. Reloading or disabling a pack restores saved instance materials, visibility and collision before the remaining rules are applied again. Restoring does not replace a current value that another system changed away from the last value applied by these rules. The editor's Affected Elements preview reports these rules as requiring live world state. A descriptor export cannot identify paired mesh actors or streamed instances.

pages.title: Type: resource and Resource Nodes
pages.description: Generate resource descriptors, remove matching world Resource Nodes, unlock scanner visibility, and patch node actor classes.

sections.heading: Type: resource and Resource Nodes
sections.text: The resource type runs in the Items stage at priority 25 , after item ( 30 ) and before building ( 20 ). Its entries key is resources . The default and required base class is /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor . Register-only mode ( class: ) is not supported, so entries use id: . YAML files are scanned during GameInstance initialization and again through /kdf reload . Existing generated resource classes keep their runtime identity, so restart the session when removing or structurally replacing a generated resource definition. The similar names hide four separate systems: Concept FactoryGame type What KDataForge does Resource definition UFGResourceDescriptor type: resource generates a new descriptor class Resource Node removal AFGResourceNodeBase and subclasses type: resourcenode destroys matches by descriptor and optional node type Resource Node property patch AFGResourceNodeBase and subclasses A cdo actor patch modifies a node class and all matching instances Scanner visibility UFGUnlockScannableResource A schematic unlocks: entry registers descriptor and node-type pairs AWESOME Sink value AFGResourceSinkSubsystem data type: sinkpoints sets item scores and has no node-placement behavior type: resource does not spawn, place, move, or remove Resource Node actors. A generated descriptor becomes mineable only when a map or another mod assigns it to a compatible node. Removal is a separate, destructive capability under type: resourcenode .

sections.heading: Generate a resource descriptor
sections.text: resource uses the same class-generation mechanism as Items , but defaults to FGResourceDescriptor and rejects parents outside that hierarchy. super-coolant.resource.yml type : resource resources : - id : MySuperCoolant parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Coolant - path : mForm value : RF_LIQUID - path : mFluidColor value : R : 40 G : 200 B : 255 A : 255 Parenting from Desc_Water inherits its fluid-oriented defaults. The generated class has the canonical path /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> with no _C suffix. You can also reference it by the short id MySuperCoolant when resolution is unambiguous. FGResourceDescriptor adds these reflected defaults on top of FGItemDescriptor : Property Purpose mDepositMesh , mDepositMaterial Loose resource-deposit visuals mDecalMaterial , mDecalSize Ground decal and collision footprint mPingColor , mCompassTexture Scanner and map presentation mCollectSpeedMultiplier Manual collection speed multiplier mManualMiningParticle , mFactoryMiningParticle , mDestroyedParticle Mining effects mManualMiningAudioName Manual-mining audio event name mFrackingHighlightParticleSystemTemplate Resource-well highlight effect Inherited item fields such as mForm , display texts, icons, category, stack size, and gameplay tags remain available through the same properties: grammar.

sections.heading: Make mForm match the use case
sections.text: mForm controls whether belts, pipes, extractors, and recipes accept the resource. Generating a liquid descriptor does not create a pipe-compatible producer or a world node. KDataForge validates the enum and property types, but it cannot validate the rest of your gameplay chain.

sections.heading: Removing Resource Nodes ( type: resourcenode )
sections.text: resourcenode runs in the SubsystemMods stage, after generated resource descriptors exist. Its remove: sequence registers world-purge rules. A scalar entry removes every node whose effective resource descriptor matches. A map adds filters and safety controls: type : resourcenode remove : # Scalar shorthand: all node types, occupied nodes protected, scanner entries removed. - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Uranium/Desc_OreUranium.Desc_OreUranium_C - resource : MyCustomOre # generated-content short ids work nodeTypes : - Node - Deposit allowOccupied : false removeFromScanner : true Field Default Meaning resource required¹ UFGResourceDescriptor class path or generated-content short id nodeTypes all Sequence of Node , FrackingSatellite , FrackingCore , Geyser , or Deposit allowOccupied false When false, skips a node group used by an extractor removeFromScanner true Also removes scanner pairs and matching KAPI extractor allow-list data ¹ Instead of resource: , an entry may carry an ofClass: scope (default FGResourceDescriptor ) plus the scope filters ( matchName: , matchTag: , where: , …); the entry’s options then apply to every loaded descriptor class that passes, and the load report says how many matched: type : resourcenode remove : - ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor matchName : Desc_OreUranium* # vanilla uranium plus any modded variant named like it nodeTypes : [ Node ] Qualified node-type names such as EResourceNodeType::Geyser also work. An omitted or empty nodeTypes sequence matches every type. Matching uses each node’s effective resource class, including a runtime resource override; it is exact by descriptor class and does not match descriptor subclasses implicitly. There is no filter for transform, purity, amount, or level name. Purge rules run before world BeginPlay , for later actor spawns and streamed levels, and once more on the next tick to catch nodes retargeted by the vanilla randomizer or KBFL. Destruction is server-authoritative. Clients remove the separate local mesh actor and rebuild scanner clusters; radar-tower resource caches are rebuilt on the server. Removing a fracking core also removes its satellites so no satellite keeps a dead core reference. With allowOccupied: false , KDataForge checks the whole fracking group and skips it when an extractor is attached. allowOccupied: true overrides that protection and can leave the extractor holding an invalid node reference. Use it only after removing affected extractors. When removeFromScanner is true, KDataForge removes every vanilla scanner pair for the descriptor, updates KAPI allow/deny data when KAPI is installed, and reapplies the exclusion after schematic purchases repopulate unlock data. Set it to false only when a scanner entry with no matching node is intentional. Danger Resource Node destruction can outlive the pack. Vanilla saves a destruction tombstone for each level-placed node, so deleting this YAML or uninstalling the pack does not reliably restore the node. SatisfactoryPlus strips most such tombstones, but resource deposits remain protected and can stay destroyed. Back up the save before testing. Treat resourcenode as a world migration, not a reversible balance patch. Caution Current source cannot remove raw pointers already cached by AFGResourceNodeManager . A node first matched only in the deferred post- BeginPlay pass, such as one retargeted by a randomizer or KBFL, can leave a dangling manager entry for the rest of that session. Test these integrations in a real world and on a dedicated server before shipping.

sections.heading: Patching Resource Node actor classes ( type: cdo )
sections.text: The built-in cdo handler selects classes, standalone asset objects, asset families, or gameplay tags. Runtime actor patches then match actors by class. Unlike resourcenode , property patches have no selector for actor transform, current resource, purity, node type, or level-instance name. Goal Current support Patch the CDO of one custom Resource Node actor class Yes, with type: cdo Apply properties to every instance of that class Yes, with applyToSpawnedActors: true Include every derived node class Yes, with applyToSubclasses: true ; this is very broad Patch one pre-placed node by map location or object path No; world actors do not exist during initial target resolution Select nodes by descriptor for property writes No; descriptor selection is available only for resourcenode removal Place, move, or clone world nodes No Remove nodes by descriptor and optional node type Yes, with type: resourcenode Create or wire fracking cores and satellites No For a custom mod where every desired node has its own actor class, a class-scoped patch is useful: type : cdo conditions : hasMod : YourNodeMod patches : - target : /YourNodeMod/World/BP_MyOreNode.BP_MyOreNode_C applyToSpawnedActors : true applyToSubclasses : false properties : - path : mExtractMultiplier value : 2 - path : mCanPlaceResourceExtractor value : true The patch first writes the class default. At world begin play, it also writes the same properties to every matching pre-existing actor. Every later matching spawn receives them as well. These instance writes do not preserve player-modified or save-restored values. Targeting /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceNode with applyToSubclasses: true would affect nearly every ordinary node, including nodes added by other mods. Use that only when the global scope is intentional.

sections.heading: Reflectable fields and runtime caveats
sections.text: FactoryGame exposes relevant UPROPERTY fields including mResourceClass , mResourceClassOverride , mResourceNodeType , mPurity , mPurityOverride , mAmount , mResourcesLeft , mCanPlaceResourceExtractor , and mExtractMultiplier . Fracking satellites also carry an instance-only mCore link. Caution Reflection access does not make every write behaviorally safe. KDataForge writes property storage directly. It does not call SetResourceClassOverride , InitResource , replication notifies, mesh refresh functions, or Resource Node Manager rebuilds. Several fields are saved, replicated, cached, or initialized during BeginPlay . Prefer stable configuration fields on a dedicated custom node class, then test descriptor, purity, and amount changes on a server and across save/load.

sections.heading: Scanner visibility and removal
sections.text: Use an instanced FGUnlockScannableResource on a schematic to add a descriptor and node-type pair to the scanner: type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_MyCustomOre unlocks : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockScannableResource.BP_UnlockScannableResource_C properties : - path : mResourcePairsToAddToScanner value : - ResourceDescriptor : MyCustomOre ResourceNodeType : Node ResourceNodeType accepts Node , FrackingSatellite , FrackingCore , Geyser , or Deposit . This only makes matching existing nodes scannable. It does not place them. See Schematics and the Base-Game Unlock Classes . This unlock is additive. To remove a descriptor from scanner data while purging its nodes, keep removeFromScanner: true on the corresponding type: resourcenode rule.

sections.heading: Advanced Resource Node visual metadata
sections.text: FactoryGame stores randomized-node mesh overrides in UFGResourceNodeData . This UPrimaryDataAsset contains mResourceDescriptor and an mNodeMeshOverrides map keyed by ENodeMeshType : MT_Node , MT_Core , MT_Crack , MT_Satellite , and the desert variants. Existing assets can be edited through cdo , and KDataForge can create a dataasset instance of that class. Override values reference cooked meshes and materials. type: asset only creates 2D textures. This metadata changes visuals, not world placement, and its startup timing must be tested against the Resource Node Manager in the target game build.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: The descriptor exists but there is nothing to mine: A descriptor is not a world actor. Place or spawn a compatible node in a map or dedicated mod. The Object Scanner cannot find it: Add FGUnlockScannableResource with the correct ResourceNodeType , and make sure matching nodes exist. An actor patch changed too many nodes: Narrow target: to a dedicated custom node class and keep applyToSubclasses: false . A removed node did not come back after deleting the pack: Vanilla persisted its destruction. Restore a backup or use a purpose-built save repair workflow; KDataForge cannot recreate the original level actor from YAML. An occupied node was skipped: Remove its extractor first. Avoid allowOccupied: true unless invalidating the extractor’s saved node reference is intentional.
