The scanner still lists a removed resource: Use removeFromScanner: true and confirm the same pack is installed on every process. Purchased schematic unlocks are filtered again at runtime. Descriptor or purity changed but visuals or extraction did not: The game may already have initialized or cached related state. Direct reflection does not invoke setters or notifications. Sink points did not help: Sink Points only control AWESOME Sink scoring. They have no Resource Node or scanner behavior. Need the resource in a recipe? Items completes before Recipes , so reference the short id or /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> directly. No include: is needed across stages.

pages.title: Type: schematic
pages.description: Generating new schematics/milestones, registering existing ones, the instanced unlocks list that's the normal way to hook up a recipe, and gating a schematic on prerequisites.

sections.heading: Type: schematic
sections.text: A type: schematic document generates new schematic classes (milestones, MAM research, alt recipes’ tech-tree entries, HUB upgrades) or registers an existing one. It works exactly like Type: recipe does for recipes. What makes schematics different is two sublists only they support: an inline unlocks: list and an inline dependencies: list. unlocks: instances real FGUnlock subobjects directly onto the schematic, and it’s how you actually wire a generated recipe to something the player can unlock. dependencies: does the same for FGAvailabilityDependency subobjects, gating the schematic on prerequisites. This type runs in the Schematics stage, after Recipes , so a schematic can reference recipes generated in the same pack. It does not support live-reload: changing it needs a restart. Its entries key is schematics , its default parent is /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic , and its required base is /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic or a subclass of it. Register-only mode ( class: ) is supported, the same as for recipe . The unlocks: and dependencies: sublists are supported only by schematic .

sections.heading: Worked example: generate + unlock a recipe
sections.text: A schematic entry uses the same generate-or-register duality as recipes: id: generates a brand new class, and class: registers an existing one. properties: configures it with the usual op grammar. Here a new milestone is generated with a display name, tech tier, cost, and a build time, and its unlocks: list immediately hooks up the recipe generated elsewhere in the pack: super-ingot.schematic.yml type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_MySuperIngot properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Ingot Smelting - path : mTechTier value : 2 - path : mTimeToComplete value : 60 - path : mCost value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount : 50 unlocks : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties : - path : mRecipes value : - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Recipe_MySuperIngot register: true (the default) queues this into SML’s UModContentRegistry per-world before the freeze. Importantly, it auto-propagates : registering the schematic also registers Recipe_MySuperIngot and every item that recipe touches. You almost never need to register a recipe or item separately once its owning schematic is registered.

sections.heading: Instanced unlocks: , the normal way to wire up a recipe
sections.text: Under the hood, each entry in unlocks: resolves the schematic CDO’s mUnlocks array by reflection. It instantiates the given class: as a subobject of that CDO, then applies properties: to that new instance before appending it. This is the exact same mechanism vanilla schematics use to hold their unlocks, just driven from YAML instead of a Blueprint graph. A schematic can carry more than one unlock, for example a recipe unlock alongside an inventory-slot unlock: unlocks : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C # any concrete FGUnlock subclass properties : - path : mRecipes value : - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Recipe_MySuperIngot - class : /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlockInventorySlot properties : - path : mNumInventorySlotsToUnlock value : 1 class: here must resolve to an FGUnlock subclass, either native, Blueprint, or a class you generated with Unlocks . Known native FactoryGame/KMods paths automatically remap to their Blueprint implementation before instancing, so /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlockRecipe and BP_UnlockRecipe_C are equivalent. properties: then configures that specific instance. This is what you want for a one-off unlock tied to a single schematic. Reach for a standalone type: unlock document only if you want to reuse the exact same preconfigured unlock class across several schematics: see Unlocks for that narrower case. Only FGUnlockRecipe and FGUnlockInventorySlot are shown above, but the mechanism works with any concrete FGUnlock subclass the base game ships (scanner unlocks, emotes, customizer options, Central Storage upgrades, …). See the Base-Game Unlock Classes for the full list with every class’s settable properties. For a repeatable schematic with a purchase cap, level-dependent rewards and costs, and generated cost/reward curves, see the complete UKLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases example .

sections.heading: Shortcut unlocks
sections.text: For the common unlocks, schematic also accepts compact fields alongside (not instead of) the fully generic unlocks: list. They still create normal engine FGUnlock instances in mUnlocks , so they work with generated content, vanilla classes, and other mods exactly as a hand-written unlock does: schematics : - id : Schematic_Convenience recipes : - Recipe_MySuperIngot - /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C schematics : - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_2-3.Schematic_2-3_C handSlots : 1 inventorySlots : 3 scannableResources : - resource : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Bauxite/Desc_OreBauxite.Desc_OreBauxite_C nodeType : Node # optional; Node is the default recipes: accepts only UFGRecipe classes and produces one FGUnlockRecipe ; schematics: accepts only UFGSchematic classes and produces one FGUnlockSchematic . handSlots: and inventorySlots: are positive integers and produce the matching arm-equipment/inventory unlock. Each scannableResources: entry takes a resource descriptor class and optional nodeType: ( Node , FrackingSatellite , FrackingCore , Geyser , or Deposit ) and produces an FGUnlockScannableResource . Use unlocks: whenever a shortcut does not cover the unlock type or when you need custom properties.

sections.heading: Unlocking resource scanner visibility
sections.text: FGUnlockScannableResource adds a resource descriptor and node-type pair to the Object Scanner. It does not create or place a Resource Node: unlocks : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockScannableResource.BP_UnlockScannableResource_C properties : - path : mResourcePairsToAddToScanner value : - ResourceDescriptor : MyCustomOre ResourceNodeType : Node ResourceNodeType accepts Node , FrackingSatellite , FrackingCore , Geyser , or Deposit . See Resources and Resource Nodes for descriptor generation, node actor patches, and placement limits.

sections.heading: Gating a schematic on prerequisites
sections.text: dependencies: is the mirror image of unlocks: , using the exact same instanced-object mechanism. Each entry creates a real instanced FGAvailabilityDependency subobject directly on the schematic’s CDO, appended to mSchematicDependencies : type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_AdvancedSuperIngot properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Advanced Super Ingot dependencies : - class : /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties : - path : mSchematics value : - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Schematic_MySuperIngot - path : mRequireAllSchematicsToBePurchased value : true That schematic won’t be purchasable until Schematic_MySuperIngot is. Dependency entries use the same native-to-Blueprint remapping as unlock entries. See Availability Dependency Classes for every native and Blueprint class, abstract state, path, and field. Common choices: FGSchematicNotPurchasedDependency : inverse of FGSchematicPurchasedDependency FGItemPickedUpDependency : requires specific items to have been picked up FGResearchTreeProgressionDependency : requires progress in a M.A.M. research tree FGGamePhaseReachedDependency : requires a minimum Space Elevator game phase Two flags on the schematic itself control what happens while dependencies aren’t met: mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess (block purchase, but don’t hide the entry) and mHiddenUntilDependenciesMet (hide the schematic entirely until then). Set them via ordinary properties: alongside dependencies: .

sections.heading: Making a milestone (schematic) free
sections.text: Because properties: is ordinary op grammar, the usual tricks apply to an existing, registered schematic too. clear wipes an array, and a plain numeric value: overrides a duration without having to compute a relative offset: type : schematic schematics : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C # register-only: editing a vanilla milestone properties : - path : mCost op : clear # no item cost - path : mTimeToComplete value : 1 # 1-second freighter turnaround (This particular example edits an existing vanilla schematic. For a genuinely simpler one-off tweak like this, a plain cdo patch with target: works identically and doesn’t need the register-only framing at all. See Balancing → Making a milestone free . Using class: here is only meaningful when you also want SML registration semantics applied, which a vanilla schematic that’s already registered doesn’t need.)

sections.heading: Removing schematics
sections.text: A type: schematic document accepts a top-level remove: sequence. Each entry is either a bare class reference (a full Unreal class path, a bare loaded class name, or a generated content id from this or another loaded KDataForge pack) or a filter map that removes every schematic passing the scope filters ( matchName: , matchTag: , where: ; the scope defaults to FGSchematic ). Removal-only documents are valid, and remove: can also be mixed with normal schematics: entries: type : schematic remove : - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C - Schematic_MyGeneratedMilestone - where : # every tier 8+ schematic path : mTechTier greaterOrEqual : 8 schematics : - id : Schematic_ReplacementMilestone properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Replacement Milestone A bare reference names the exact schematic class to remove; it does not remove subclasses. If a generated id is ambiguous across packs, KDataForge logs the same ambiguity diagnostic used for other short-id class references. Removals run after registrations, so an explicit remove: wins over a register: for the same class. The consolidated guide is Removing Content . Schematic removal is save-clean. KDataForge removes the class from SML’s content registry before the schematic manager builds its per-session list, so uninstalling the pack brings the schematic back on the next load. Removal does not revoke purchases. An already-purchased schematic stays in the save and keeps re-applying its unlocks on load, including recipes it granted. To actually take away craftable content, pair schematic removal with recipe remove: .

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: The schematic shows up but the recipe never unlocks : check that the unlocks: entry’s class: actually resolves ( /kdf report will show a failed patch if it doesn’t) and that mRecipes points at the exact generated class path, with no _C suffix. Two mods both try to unlock the same recipe : that’s fine. FGUnlockRecipe instances are additive, and duplicate unlocks of an already-unlocked recipe are a no-op in the base game. Want to unlock a recipe from a schematic you didn’t generate (vanilla, another mod’s, or your own from an earlier pack): unlocks: works in register-only ( class: ) mode too, it’s just easy to miss. See Adding a Recipe to an Existing Schematic . A schematic with dependencies: is purchasable even though its prerequisite isn’t met : dependencies: alone only registers the check; you also need mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess: true (block purchase until met) and/or mHiddenUntilDependenciesMet: true (hide the entry entirely) as ordinary properties: on the same schematic. Full worked pack: End-to-End Pack ties an item + recipe + this schematic + sink points + localization together in one folder.

pages.title: Type: sinkpoints
pages.description: Set AWESOME Sink point values for items, understand registration timing, and keep sink scoring separate from Resource Nodes.

sections.heading: Type: sinkpoints
sections.text: This document type runs in the SubsystemMods stage, after all content-generation stages. Its entries key is entries , and the track: field accepts Default or Exploration , defaulting to Default . This one’s simple in shape but strict about timing: it sets how many AWESOME Sink points an item is worth. type : sinkpoints track : Default # or Exploration entries : - item : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot points : 8 - item : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C points : 100 overridden : 50 # optional a separate "overridden" point value some UI paths read item: must resolve to an UFGItemDescriptor subclass. Both the bare generated-content id shortcut (e.g. item: MySuperIngot instead of the full /KDataForge/Gen/... path, see Generated Content Short Ids ) and the bare class-name shortcut work here too (see Targeting → bare class name ), though sticking to full paths in a published pack is still the safer habit. points: is a plain integer. overridden: is optional, and it’s only needed if you specifically want a distinct “overridden” points value separate from the base one. One sinkpoints document builds one UDataTable and registers it against whichever track: you picked. Multiple documents, even across packs, just add more rows to the sink subsystem: they don’t need to be merged into one file.

sections.heading: Many items at once: filter entries
sections.text: An entry may replace item: with an ofClass: scope (default /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor ) plus the scope filters ( matchName: , matchTag: , where: , …). Every loaded item descriptor class that passes the filters gets the entry’s points: (and overridden: ): type : sinkpoints entries : - ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor where : path : mForm in : [ RF_LIQUID , RF_GAS ] # every fluid and gas: not sinkable points : 0 - ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor matchName : Desc_Nuclear* # everything nuclear is worth a fixed 500 points : 500 Filter entries expand against the descriptor classes loaded when the document applies, and the load report warns when a filter matched nothing. A later explicit item: row for the same descriptor in the same document wins, because rows are keyed by class name.

sections.heading: Registration timing and Resource Node boundary
sections.text: KDataForge queues sink point tables during initialization and registers them per world before SML’s content registry freezes. /kdf reload re-reads and validates the document, but cannot replace a table inside that already-frozen registry. Restart the session or dedicated server before judging a sink-point change. Sink points only control item scoring in the AWESOME Sink. They do not place Resource Nodes, change purity, or grant scanner visibility. See Resources and Resource Nodes for those systems.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Changed points do not appear : restart the session or dedicated server. Points show as 0, or unchanged in-game : check that item: actually resolved ( /kdf report lists a failed patch if the class path was wrong), and make sure you’re looking at the right track: ( Default vs. Exploration are separate tables). Sink points for a freshly generated item are part of the combined pack in End-to-End Pack . A resource still has no mineable node or scanner entry: Sink scoring is unrelated. Follow the descriptor, world-node, and scanner steps on the Resources page.

pages.title: Sounds
pages.description: Import pack-relative PCM16 WAV or lossless FLAC files as Wwise audio events for ADA messages and other audio consumers.

sections.heading: Sounds
sections.text: type: sound imports WAV or FLAC files from your pack as generated UAkAudioEvent assets. Use it when an existing game or mod feature accepts an audio event, such as an ADA message's mAudioEvent. Importing an event does not play it or create a message trigger.

sections.heading: Declare sounds
sections.text: Place the audio file inside the directory containing your pack.yml: DataForge/ pack.yml # ref: MyPack welcome.sound.yml audio/ welcome.flac # file: welcome.sound.yml type: sound sounds: - id: AdaWelcome file: audio/welcome.flac name: Welcome voice line description: Volume of the ADA welcome message category: Voice subCategory: ADA sounds: must contain at least one entry. Every entry requires id and file; the four display fields are optional and must be non-empty strings when supplied. | Field | Meaning | | id | Stable event id. Start with an ASCII letter; remaining characters may be ASCII letters, digits, _, ., or -. | | file | WAV or FLAC path relative to the pack root, not the YAML file's directory. | | name | Sound setting label; defaults to <id> volume. | | description | Sound setting help text; defaults to an explanation of playback volume. | | category | Group label below the native Audio settings section. | | subCategory | Additional group label, combined with category into one Audio subcategory. | With both grouping fields above, the Audio subcategory is Voice / ADA. Without either field, it is KDataForge sound events. Each sound receives a volume setting with a default of 100%, where 0% mutes it. These controls appear only under Options → Audio, never in KDataForge pack configuration. Audio preferences are local to each player and are not synchronized by the host. There is no volume field in a sound entry. Existing local Audio preferences keep their values. Older __sounds.*.volume entries in pack configuration files no longer affect playback; they can be removed. To group all ADA sounds together, use the same category and subCategory on every sound entry.

sections.heading: Accepted audio
sections.text: - Little-endian RIFF/WAVE containing uncompressed 16-bit PCM, or native lossless FLAC containing 16-bit PCM. - Mono or stereo, with a sample rate from 8,000 through 192,000 Hz. - A non-empty audio payload containing complete PCM frames; maximum 64 MiB for both the encoded file and decoded PCM. - A .wav or .flac extension, matched without regard to case. - FLAC must declare its nonzero total frame count in STREAMINFO. Decoding verifies the declared frame count and PCM MD5 when supplied. MP3, OGG (including Ogg FLAC), 24-bit FLAC and floating-point WAV are unsupported. Export as PCM16 WAV or native 16-bit FLAC in your audio editor. Files and any symbolic links must resolve inside the pack directory; absolute paths and paths escaping the pack are rejected. Existing WAV packs continue to work. To reduce download size without changing audio, convert PCM16 WAV to FLAC without resampling, mixing channels or changing bit depth, then update only sounds[].file. Keep the sound ID and message references unchanged. FLAC is decoded to the same PCM for playback, so runtime audio memory does not shrink. FLAC packs require a KDataForge build with FLAC support; keep WAV when supporting older builds. The editor checks FLAC structure and format limits; the game importer also decodes frames and verifies the supplied PCM checksum. Generated events play once in 2D and route to the master bus. This document type does not author loops or spatial attenuation.

sections.heading: Reference an event
sections.text: Inside the same pack, use the bare event id in an audio event property: type: dataasset assets: - id: WelcomeMessage class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGMessage properties: - path: mAudioEvent value: AdaWelcome This creates a message asset with an audio reference. A separate game or mod workflow must trigger that message. The full event object path for ref: MyPack is: /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_AdaWelcome Use the full path when referring to the event from another pack. Audio events are assets, so their paths have no _C suffix. Sound ids share the generated asset namespace with images, curves and data assets; choose distinct ids across those types. See Generated Content Short Ids for reference resolution.

sections.heading: Load stage and multiplayer
sections.text: Sounds run in the Assets stage, before dataasset documents resolve properties such as FGMessage.mAudioEvent, and before later CDO changes. File ordering does not require placing a sound YAML before a data asset YAML. Install the same pack definitions on every multiplayer client and the server. Every client, including a listen-server host, also needs the referenced audio files. Dedicated servers do not need WAV or FLAC files: they validate the relative path syntax and create placeholder events at the same generated asset paths, without opening audio files, creating bank caches or loading Wwise banks. Messages, subtitles and server-side triggers remain available. Audio contents and symbolic-link containment are checked on clients, where the audio files exist. Importing on the server does not transfer audio files to clients. The workspace's Alpakit PackagePlugin automatically excludes raw .wav and .flac files from dedicated-server staging for WindowsServer and LinuxServer. This also applies to the server directories inside merged bundles and direct server deployments; the Windows client directory retains its audio. No YAML conditions or extra pack settings are needed. Keep the sound YAML and its message references in server packages. When packaging with an older Alpakit, audio files can remain in server packages harmlessly; older KDataForge versions still require them during import. An Alpakit filter that excludes only .wav keeps .flac files in dedicated-server packages. Extend that filter to both formats to obtain the same server size savings; keep client audio and server YAML definitions.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - File cannot resolve: Check the path relative to pack.yml, filename case on Linux, and whether a symbolic link points outside the pack. - WAV rejected: Re-export as uncompressed PCM16 mono/stereo WAV within the rate and size limits above. Renaming an MP3 to .wav does not convert it. - FLAC rejected: Export native 16-bit FLAC with a known frame count, within both size limits. Re-export files with checksum failures; renaming another format does not convert it. - Generated event missing: Check for duplicate ids, including collisions with other generated assets, and confirm the sound document's conditions pass. - Bank cache cannot be written: The client must be able to write generated banks under FactoryGame/Content/KDataForgeRuntimeSounds/. - Wwise rejects the bank: Inspect LogAkAudio and LogWwiseFileHandler alongside KDataForge diagnostics. - Import succeeds but nothing plays: Confirm a consumer triggers the event and check the sound's volume setting and the game's master volume.

pages.title: Type: sublevel
pages.description: Block RefinedRDLib or KBFL sublevel assets before they stream into a game world.

sections.heading: Type: sublevel
sections.text: Use type: sublevel when another mod declares optional world sublevels through RefinedRDLib or KBFL and a compatibility pack must stop selected sublevels from loading. The document runs in the CDOChanges stage during session initialization. It changes the provider’s data assets in memory; it does not unload a level that has already streamed in. Restart the session after changing it. This handler is deliberately narrow. It supports these two asset families: Provider Asset class Blocking action RefinedRDLib /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset Makes the asset’s map selector match no normal map KBFL /Script/KBFL.KBFLSubLevelSpawning Clears its sublevel list and disables the asset Use an ordinary type: cdo document for any other asset class.

sections.heading: Block explicit assets
sections.text: block: must be a non-empty sequence. A scalar entry is an exact asset object path. Map entries accept target: as either one path or a sequence of paths: type : sublevel block : - /SomeMod/World/DA_OptionalSublevel.DA_OptionalSublevel - target : - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_A.DA_Nodes_A - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_B.DA_Nodes_B Exact targets use direct object loading, so they still work when the Asset Registry is not fully populated during early startup. A path that does not resolve produces a warning: the owning mod may be absent, or the object path may be wrong.

sections.heading: Block every asset of a provider class
sections.text: Use allAssetsOfClass: for a bulk compatibility rule: type : sublevel conditions : hasMod : RefinedRDLib block : - allAssetsOfClass : /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset The scan includes derived asset classes. A map may combine target: and allAssetsOfClass: ; all matches accumulate. The provider is an optional dependency: an unresolved bulk class produces an Info diagnostic instead of a hard dependency failure.

sections.heading: Block assets by filter
sections.text: To block only some of a provider’s assets, give a map entry an ofClass: scope plus the scope filters ( matchName: , matchTag: , where: ). ofClass: is required here, sublevel assets have no default scope, and only asset instances are matched, never class defaults: type : sublevel conditions : hasMod : RefinedRDLib block : - ofClass : /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset matchName : DA_Optional_* # by asset name - ofClass : /Script/KBFL.KBFLSubLevelSpawning where : path : mSubLevelArray isEmpty : false Filter entries expand against the asset registry when the document applies (same Asset Registry caveat as allAssetsOfClass: ); the load report states how many assets a filter matched. Note Bulk discovery depends on the Asset Registry. If an installed provider class resolves but the scan finds no assets during early startup, KDataForge reports that condition. List exact target: paths instead when the assets must always be blocked.

sections.heading: Boundaries
sections.text: sublevel blocks only RefinedRDLib and KBFL descriptor assets. It does not target arbitrary Unreal streaming levels, persistent-map content, world-partition cells, or already loaded levels. Missing or invalid entries do not discard valid entries in the same document. Each target reports its own diagnostic. Changes are in-memory and session-scoped. Removing the YAML restores normal provider behavior on the next session; no save data or source asset is rewritten. Every multiplayer process loads its own sublevels. Install the same pack on server and clients.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Nothing was blocked: use the asset object’s path, not the generated class path. Check /kdf report for an unresolved target or an empty Asset Registry scan. Target is rejected as the wrong kind: only RRDLSublevelAsset and KBFLSubLevelSpawning instances are supported. Patch other asset types with type: cdo . Level was already present: KDataForge loads once during GameInstance initialization. Restart instead of expecting an in-session unload.

pages.title: Targeting
pages.description: Every way to select targets, including class CDOs, asset instances, all assets of a class, tag / name / property filters, recipe shortcuts (producedIn, ingredient, product), subclasses, spawned actors, and the same filters in remove:, block:, and sinkpoints entries.

sections.heading: Targeting
sections.text: Every type: cdo patch needs at least one target selector. The current validator accepts multiple selectors and GatherTargets accumulates their matches, but one clear selector per patch is easier to reason about. This page shows all selectors and the modifiers that widen a selection.

sections.heading: Class identity filters
sections.text: Filtered scopes accept classType: any (default), blueprint, or native. This tests Unreal's CLASS_CompiledFromBlueprint flag; it does not guess from class names. excludeClasses accepts one class reference or a non-empty list. Exact references exclude those classes while their subclasses remain eligible. Full class-path patterns starting with / also accept * and ? wildcards, matched case-insensitively against each candidate's own class path. For example, excludeClasses: ['/KLib/*', '/SatisfactoryPlus/*'] leaves those namespaces untouched while selecting other mods' recipes. A subclass outside an excluded namespace remains eligible; patterns do not expand through ancestry. Both filters also run for classes loaded later. type: cdo patches: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor classType: blueprint matchAssets: false excludeClasses: - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/SpaceElevatorParts/Desc_SpaceElevatorPart_1.Desc_SpaceElevatorPart_1_C where: path: mForm equals: RF_LIQUID properties: - path: mForm value: RF_GAS Combine with ofClass, or a recipe shortcut that supplies a scope. These scope filters do not narrow separately listed target or allAssetsOfClass selections. Other filters are AND-combined. For data-asset candidates they test the asset's class. Set matchAssets: false for CDOs only. Consequently, exclusion patterns match a data asset's class path, not its individual object path. Wildcard exclusions must start with /; a short pattern such as Recipe_* is rejected. Quote patterns in YAML, especially patterns containing * or ?. Explicit classType: any selects every class in an ofClass scope without another predicate.

sections.heading: `target:` class path: the class default object (CDO)
sections.text: The most common form. Blueprint asset classes use the _C suffix (auto-retried if forgotten); native classes use /Script/Module.Class: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.5

sections.heading: `target:` bare class name: shortcut for the full class path
sections.text: Anywhere a class path is accepted, a bare class name (no / or .) resolves against every class currently loaded in memory, so you don't have to spell out the full asset path: type: cdo patches: - target: Desc_Water # same class as # /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C properties: - path: mResourceSinkPoints value: 0 If the short name matches more than one loaded class, KDataForge logs an Error to LogKDataForge listing every match. It still applies the patch, using the first match sorted by full class path, so the result stays deterministic. Prefer the full class path in published packs to avoid relying on load order. This shortcut is meant for quick local tweaks.

sections.heading: `target:` generated-content id: shortcut for `/KDataForge/Gen/...`
sections.text: A bare id also resolves to a class your own pack generated, so you can target your own item/recipe/schematic/... content without spelling out /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_...: type: cdo debug: true patches: - target: MySuperIngot # same as /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot properties: - path: mResourceSinkPoints value: 50 This is checked before the bare class-name shortcut above, and works the same way everywhere a class or object reference is accepted, not just target:. See Generated Content Short Ids for the full write-up (resolution order, cross-pack matches, and which reference kinds support it).

sections.heading: `target:` object path: one asset instance
sections.text: The same key also accepts an object path (PrimaryDataAsset instances etc.) and patches that object directly. Instances have no _C suffix: they are objects, not classes. type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - target: /KLib/Assets/MinerDescriptions/DA_MinerDesc_Iron.DA_MinerDesc_Iron properties: - path: mIsDisabled value: true

sections.heading: `target:` a sequence of paths: patch several targets in one entry
sections.text: target: also accepts a list of paths instead of a single scalar. Every entry is resolved the same way a scalar target: would be (class path, bare class name, generated-content id, or object path), and the same properties:/applyToSubclasses:/applyToSpawnedActors: apply to each one: type: cdo debug: true patches: - target: - MySuperIngot # generated-content id - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C properties: - path: mResourceSinkPoints value: 50 This is purely a convenience for "these unrelated targets happen to want the exact same properties: block", it does not widen a single class the way applyToSubclasses: does, and mixing target kinds (a class path alongside an object path) in one list is fine, each entry is resolved independently. Prefer applyToSubclasses: or matchTag: instead when the targets share a common base class or tag; reach for a target: list when they don't. An explicit target: must contain one non-empty scalar reference or a non-empty list of them. An empty string, null, mapping, nested list or empty target list produces a source-line error and skips the entire patch entry, including its other selectors. Valid entries in other patches still apply. KDF.ApplyToAssets uses the same check before changing editor assets. A well-formed reference that cannot resolve keeps the normal warning and runtime class-watch behavior.

sections.heading: `allAssetsOfClass:` every asset of a class
sections.text: Patches every asset of that class (and its subclasses) found in the asset registry. This is ideal for data-asset families: type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties: - path: mProductionTime op: multiply value: 0.75

sections.heading: `ofClass:` scope + filters: select by tag, name, recipe shape, or property values
sections.text: The remaining selectors all work the same way: ofClass: names a scope (that class and every subclass of it, plus data-asset instances of it unless matchAssets: false), and one or more filters on the same patch entry pick the members of that scope to patch. Every filter present on an entry must pass, so the filters are AND-combined: | Filter | Matches when … | | matchTag: (+ tagProperty:) | the object carries every listed gameplay tag | | matchName: | the class name (or full path) matches any listed wildcard pattern | | producedIn: | a recipe's mProducedIn references any listed building class or a subclass of it | | ingredient: | a recipe's mIngredients[*].ItemClass references any listed item class or a subclass of it | | product: | a recipe's mProduct[*].ItemClass references any listed item class or a subclass of it | | where: | every listed path / operator clause holds | The three recipe shortcuts (producedIn:, ingredient:, product:) default the scope to /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe when ofClass: is omitted, and any matchTag:, matchName: or where: on the same entry shares that default. Without a recipe shortcut those three require an explicit ofClass:. Set ofClass: anyway to narrow the scope to a mod's own recipe base class. Filters never narrow a target: or allAssetsOfClass: selector on the same entry, those still match everything they name. When no object in the scope passes, KDataForge logs one warning that repeats the filters it evaluated, so you can see which one was too strict.

sections.heading: `matchTag:` select by gameplay tag
sections.text: Selects everything in the scope that carries the tag(s). matchTag: accepts a scalar or a sequence, and when it's a sequence, all tags must match. Two optional keys are available: tagProperty: names the tag container property explicitly, and matchAssets: also matches data-asset instances (default true): type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - matchTag: KMods.AlternateRecipe # scalar; use a block sequence for multiple tags ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe # required scope tagProperty: mGameplayTags # optional explicit tag container property matchAssets: true # also match data-asset instances (default true) properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.8 Register your own tags first using type: gametag. The GameTags stage always runs before everything else. Then match on them in the same pack: see Game Tags.

sections.heading: `matchName:` select by class name pattern
sections.text: Matches the class name against a wildcard pattern (* any run of characters, ? one character, case-insensitive). The trailing _C of Blueprint classes is optional in the pattern. When the pattern contains a /, it is matched against the full class path instead, which lets you select by content folder. A sequence matches when any pattern matches: type: cdo patches: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe matchName: Recipe_Alternate_* # every vanilla alternate recipe, no tags needed properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.8 - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic matchName: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/* # by folder: the milestones properties: - path: mTimeToComplete op: multiply value: 0.5 For data-asset instances the pattern is matched against the asset's own name and path, not its class.

sections.heading: `producedIn:` / `ingredient:` / `product:` recipe shortcuts
sections.text: The three shortcuts answer the questions pack authors ask most often about recipes, without spelling out a where: clause. Each accepts a class path (any form that target: accepts: full path, bare class name, or generated-content id) or a sequence of them, and a recipe matches when any entry is referenced or one of its subclasses is: type: cdo patches: # every recipe crafted in a Constructor is 25% faster - producedIn: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/ConstructorMk1/Build_ConstructorMk1.Build_ConstructorMk1_C properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.75 # every recipe crafted in ANY manufacturing building (Constructor, Assembler, Manufacturer, # Refinery, Blender, Particle Accelerator, modded machines deriving from the same base, …) - producedIn: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer properties: - path: mVariablePowerConsumptionFactor op: multiply value: 0.9 # every recipe that consumes Plastic OR Rubber - ingredient: [Desc_Plastic_C, Desc_Rubber_C] properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.9 # every recipe that produces a Screw, but only when it is crafted in an Assembler - product: Desc_IronScrew_C producedIn: Build_AssemblerMk1_C properties: - path: mProduct[0].Amount op: multiply value: 2 The subclass rule is what makes the native base classes useful as values: FGBuildableManufacturer covers every machine that derives from it, /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildGun covers every build-gun (buildable) recipe, and /Script/FactoryGame.FGWorkBench covers every hand-craftable recipe (the vanilla Craft Bench is BP_WorkBenchComponent_C, a subclass). A class that is not loaded yet when the patch runs is matched by exact path only (a warning tells you), the subclass rule needs the class resolved.

sections.heading: `where:` filter by property values
sections.text: where: compares reflected properties of every candidate in the scope. It takes one map, or a sequence of maps that must all hold. Each map names a path: (the same property path grammar as properties:, plus [*] for "any element") and exactly one operator: | Operator | Applies to | Matches when … | | equals, notEquals | everything | the value equals the given YAML value (class references: the class or a subclass) | | lessThan, lessOrEqual, greaterThan, greaterOrEqual | numbers, enums (ordinal), booleans | numeric comparison | | contains, notContains | arrays, sets, tag containers, strings/names/text | an element equals the value (same rules as equals), the container has the tag, or the text contains the substring | | in, notIn | everything | any listed value matches: equals for a scalar leaf, contains for an array/set/tag container leaf | | matches | everything | the display text matches a wildcard pattern (*Alternate*); references use their path | | isEmpty: true/false | containers, text, references | the container/text is empty, or the reference is null | A candidate that does not have the property at all simply does not match. A comparison that cannot apply to the property's type (greaterThan on an array, [*] on a float, …) is reported once per patch entry as a warning naming the path. Remember that the scope class's own CDO is a candidate as well, and it only holds default values: isEmpty: true on mProducedIn matches FGRecipe itself, not just the orphaned Blueprint recipes you were thinking of. /kdf report lists every object a patch touched. type: cdo patches: # long recipes (more than 8 seconds) that use Iron Ingot get a bit faster - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe where: - path: mManufactoringDuration greaterThan: 8 - path: mIngredients[*].ItemClass # [*] = any element equals: Desc_IronIngot_C properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.8 # every schematic up to tier 3 completes instantly - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic where: path: mTechTier # a single clause can be written as one map lessOrEqual: 3 properties: - path: mTimeToComplete value: 0 # liquids and gases never earn sink points (`in` = any of the listed values) - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor where: path: mForm in: [RF_LIQUID, RF_GAS] properties: - path: mResourceSinkPoints value: 0 # recipes crafted in a Constructor OR an Assembler (`in` on an array = contains any) - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe where: path: mProducedIn in: [Build_ConstructorMk1_C, Build_AssemblerMk1_C] properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration op: multiply value: 0.9 # recipes nobody can craft anywhere (empty mProducedIn) get the Craft Bench - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe where: path: mProducedIn isEmpty: true properties: - path: mProducedIn op: append value: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/-Shared/WorkBench/BP_WorkBenchComponent.BP_WorkBenchComponent_C [*] may appear more than once in a path (mUnlocks[*].mRecipes[*]) and descends through struct members and object references alike; a where: clause with [*] matches when any element path satisfies the operator. [*] is read-only: a properties: op still has to address one concrete element (mIngredients[0].Amount). Inside a where: path a class reference reads through to its defaults: mProduct[0].ItemClass.mForm compares the produced item's form, and mUnlocks[*].mRecipes[*].mProducedIn on a schematic walks into every unlocked recipe's producer list (soft references are loaded on demand). This is a filter convenience only; properties: ops never write through a class reference. Filters and the lazy class watch: like applyToSubclasses:, every scope-filter patch keeps watching the session. A Blueprint recipe or item class that loads later (common for content the game only references on demand), or a native-parent class generated by KDF, is tested against the same filters once its class and CDO are initialized, and patched when it passes. A not-yet-resolved explicit class target is also watched by its exact path, including a generated class created in a later content stage. KDF does not force CDO creation during class allocation.

sections.heading: The same filters in `remove:`, `block:`, and `sinkpoints` entries
sections.text: The scope filters are not a cdo feature. Every document type that selects existing content takes the same keys in place of one exact reference, with a default scope that fits the type: | Document / key | Filter entry selects | Default ofClass: | Details | | type: recipe → remove: | recipes to take out of the game | FGRecipe | Removing Content | | type: schematic → remove: | schematics to take out of the game | FGSchematic | Removing Content | | type: research / mam → remove: | research trees to take out of the game | FGResearchTree | Removing Content | | type: resourcenode → remove: | resource descriptors whose placed nodes are purged | FGResourceDescriptor | Resources | | type: sublevel → block: | provider data assets to block | none, ofClass: required | Sublevels | | type: sinkpoints → entries: | item descriptors that receive the entry's points: | FGItemDescriptor | Sink Points | type: recipe remove: - producedIn: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/HadronCollider/Build_HadronCollider.Build_HadronCollider_C type: sinkpoints entries: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor where: path: mForm in: [RF_LIQUID, RF_GAS] points: 0 Recipe, schematic, and research removal rules are stored as predicates and re-checked against every class the game presents, so late-loading Blueprint content is covered. Resource-node, sublevel, and sink-point filters expand once, when the document applies, against what is loaded at that moment; the load report tells you how many matched.

sections.heading: `applyToSubclasses:` widen a class target to every derived class
sections.text: With a class target, applyToSubclasses: true also patches every derived class's CDO: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableResourceExtractor applyToSubclasses: true # every miner, oil extractor, water pump, … properties: - path: mExtractMultiplier op: min value: 2 > ⚠️ Wide blast radius. Subclass expansion covers _every_ derived class, including ones added > by other mods you may never have heard of. Prefer the most-derived class that still covers what > you mean. Use min/max/clamp/multiply rather than absolute set where possible, and check > /kdf report to see exactly which classes were patched.

sections.heading: `applyToSpawnedActors:` runtime actor patches
sections.text: For actor classes, saves and archetypes override CDO values on already-placed instances. Setting applyToSpawnedActors: true re-applies the ops to every instance the moment it spawns (world begin play and every later spawn): type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/StorageContainerMk1/Build_StorageContainerMk1.Build_StorageContainerMk1_C applyToSpawnedActors: true # re-applied to every instance the moment it spawns applyToSubclasses: false # exact class only properties: - path: mInventorySizeX value: 12 - path: mInventorySizeY value: 8 These instance writes are unconditional. They do not compare a value against the vanilla snapshot or preserve a value changed by a player or save. Resource Nodes are an important consequence of class-only actor matching. KDataForge cannot select one placed node by location, descriptor, purity, amount, or node type. See Resources and Resource Nodes.

sections.heading: Actor lifecycle actions
sections.text: Use actorAction to remove live actors rather than edit their class defaults: type: cdo patches: - target: /MyMod/Retired/Build_Prototype.Build_Prototype_C applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true actorAction: dismantle target must name actor classes; a target list is supported. applyToSpawnedActors: true is required: actions cover existing actors and future spawns. applyToSubclasses defaults to false. Omit properties; an action and property operations require separate entries. CDO scope filters such as ofClass, allAssetsOfClass and where are not supported here. Optional actorSelector predicates use the existing server-only instance selection. Generated actor IDs are created after the CDOChanges stage. Add deferOneGameTick: true when targeting these IDs so registration runs after generation and BeginPlay. The action then uses its normal subsequent world timer tick; existing native or cooked actor classes do not need this extra registration delay. - destroy calls the actor's normal destruction function. - dismantle calls the game's dismantle interface on child dismantle actors, then the parent. Actors without that interface use normal destruction instead. Actions wait until the actor has begun play, then run on a subsequent world timer tick. Replicated actors are changed by their authority. Local, non-replicated client actors can also be removed locally; a client never removes a remote replicated actor through this action. Reload and world shutdown cancel pending callbacks. Removing or reloading the pack does not recreate actors already removed; destruction of saved or level-placed actors may persist in the save. Use a disposable save when first validating a removal pack. The visual CDO editor exposes Instance operation with property operations, destroy and dismantle choices. Remove existing property operations before choosing an action. Class reflection alone cannot preview live actor matches; Affected elements reports this selection as limited.

sections.heading: Player inventory remapping
sections.text: Use inventoryRemap to replace existing player inventory items and convert items added later: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGCharacterPlayer applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true inventoryRemap: - from: /MyMod/Items/Desc_Old.Desc_Old_C to: /MyMod/Items/Desc_New.Desc_New_C multiplier: 10 Targets must be FGCharacterPlayer classes or subclasses. The explicit target and applyToSpawnedActors: true are required. applyToSubclasses defaults to false. Each entry names concrete item descriptor classes. multiplier defaults to 1 and must be an unquoted integer from 1 to 2147483647. Use a separate patch for property writes or actorAction; asset and class scope filters are unavailable for inventory remapping. Generated item IDs require deferOneGameTick: true so registration follows item generation. Conversions run on the server after the player and inventory are ready. They handle existing players and later spawns, then listen for item additions, removals and inventory expansion. The complete output must fit while original stacks still occupy their slots. Otherwise originals remain and conversion retries on later inventory changes. A quantity above the 32-bit item-count limit also leaves originals unchanged. Partial conversions are not allowed. Sources must be unique. A destination cannot also be a source: chained and cyclic conversions are unsupported. Runtime validation also rejects conflicting or chained rules from separate entries whose player target classes overlap. Conversions replace descriptor and count; per-item dynamic state is not transferred. Optional actorSelector predicates keep their normal server-only behavior. Reload unbinds previous callbacks and applies current rules; it does not turn already converted items back into their originals. In the visual CDO editor, choose Instance operation → Remap player inventory. Add conversions, choose source and output descriptors, then enter numeric multipliers. Existing conversion rows must be removed before switching operation modes. Affected elements reports live inventory selection as limited; exported class defaults do not describe player inventory contents.

sections.heading: Choosing a selector
sections.text: The selector keys cover targets from a single class to every actor in a class family. Use the table below to choose the narrowest useful selector: | I want to patch… | Selector | | One recipe / item / building class | target: class path | | One data-asset instance | target: object path (no _C) | | A handful of unrelated targets, same properties: | target: sequence of paths | | A whole data-asset family | allAssetsOfClass: | | Everything carrying a tag | matchTag: + ofClass: | | Every class whose name / folder matches a pattern | matchName: + ofClass: | | Every recipe crafted in a building (or building family) | producedIn: | | Every recipe consuming / producing an item (or item family) | ingredient: / product: | | Everything whose property values meet a condition | where: + ofClass: | | A base class and everything derived | class target: + applyToSubclasses: true | | Values on placed/spawning actors | + applyToSpawnedActors: true | Filters combine: producedIn: + ingredient: + where: on one entry select recipes that satisfy all three. Prefer the narrowest combination that still describes what you mean, and check /kdf report to see exactly which classes were patched.

pages.title: Templates and Typed References
pages.description: Read pack configuration, game settings and reflected game data from YAML. Typed references, {prefix:body} templates, function calls, nesting, escaping and quoting.

sections.heading: Templates and Typed References
sections.text: YAML values do not have to be literals. KDataForge can fill them with the value of a pack configuration field, a game setting, or any property or function result of a game class. There are two mechanisms: Mechanism Looks like Where it works Result Typed reference cfg:balance.ironSpeed (a whole, unquoted scalar) Any value of any document The typed value: a number, a boolean, a list. Template {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} inside a string Any string value of any document (pre-pass providers); operation arguments (apply-time providers) The value inserted as text, or, when the string is exactly one token, the typed value. A template is {prefix:body} . The prefix names a provider and the body tells it what to read. Providers come in two groups that run at different times: Pre-pass providers ( cfg , session , ags , option ) run once the pack files are read and before anything is applied. They work in every string of every document. Apply-time providers ( class , item , resource , building , recipe , schematic , research , category , dataasset , asset ) read reflected game data at the moment an operation is applied. They work in the operation arguments value , min and max , including nested maps and lists inside them. All examples on this page use the pack of the Player-Configurable Balancing tutorial.

sections.heading: Typed references
sections.text: A scalar that is unquoted and matches cfg: , session: , ags: or option: followed by a name is replaced by the typed value before the stages run: Form Reads cfg:<id> A configuration field of the own pack. cfg:<pack>:<id> A field of another pack. session:<id> A session setting (SML session setting, falling back to an advanced game setting of the same id). ags:<id> An advanced game setting. option:<id> A local game option of the player. typed-refs.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : # float field -> the number 2.0 - path : mManufactoringDuration op : divide value : cfg:balance.ironSpeed # list field -> a list of tags - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : cfg:tags.extra - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : # select field with int32 values -> the number 1, 2 or 3 - path : mResourceSinkPoints value : cfg:features.tier # QUOTED -> stays the literal text cfg:balance.ironSpeed - path : mDescription value : ' cfg:balance.ironSpeed ' How the value is inserted: Field value type Inserted as number, boolean An unquoted scalar in canonical form ( 2.0 , true ). string, text, name, tag A quoted scalar. a list ( multiple: true ) A list of scalars. This works for arrays, sets and gameplay tag containers. Rules: Whole scalar only. cfg:balance.ironSpeed x has a space and stays literal text. To embed a value in text, use the template form {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} . Unquoted only. A quoted 'cfg:...' or "cfg:..." is always literal. Names are letters, digits, _ , . and - . The pack part of cfg:<pack>:<id> is the pack ref . References are not replaced in the values of the keys id , type , include and ref , in map keys, or anywhere inside a conditions: block. Use a config: expression there. The editor reports a reference in such a place as config.ref-not-resolved . An unknown id leaves the scalar as written and logs a warning with file and line. The type has to fit the property. A number field into a text property is an error at apply time; the editor checks the combination while you type ( config.type-mismatch ).

sections.heading: Game settings
sections.text: session: , ags: and option: read the live game settings. The ids come from the settings index of a reflection export ( indexes/settings.json ); the ids below are only examples. settings.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mCanBeDiscarded value : ags:FG.GameRules.NoPower Session and advanced settings do not exist without a world. On the main menu a document that uses one of them is deferred and applied automatically once a save is loaded. It is applied again when the setting changes. In a config: condition, an unavailable setting is not an error either. option: values exist at any time.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.text: {prefix:body} can sit anywhere inside a string, next to normal text or other tokens: super-ingot.item.yml type : item items : - id : SuperIngot parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mDescription value : ' {cfg:texts.motto} Smelts like {item:/Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C:GetItemName} at {cfg:balance.ironSpeed}x speed. ' With the sample defaults this reads: Forged from YAML. Stacks high, sinks well. Smelts like Iron Ingot at 2.0x speed. {cfg:...} was replaced before the stages ran. {item:...:GetItemName} was read from the game when the property was written, in the player’s language. Pre-pass templates follow the same exclusions as typed references: they are not replaced in the values of id , type , include and ref , in map keys, or inside conditions: blocks.

sections.heading: Providers
sections.text: Prefix Phase Target Must derive from Example cfg pre-pass A config field none {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} , {cfg:Other:shared.level} session pre-pass A session setting none {session:FG.Example} ags pre-pass An advanced game setting none {ags:FG.GameRules.NoPower} option pre-pass A local game option none {option:FG.Example} class apply Any class (its default object) none, function libraries allowed {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:Round(2.6)} item apply An item descriptor class UFGItemDescriptor {item:/Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C:GetItemName} resource apply A resource descriptor class UFGResourceDescriptor {resource:/Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C:GetItemName} building apply A buildable class AFGBuildable {building:/Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/SmelterMk1/Build_SmelterMk1.Build_SmelterMk1_C:mPowerConsumption} recipe apply A recipe class UFGRecipe {recipe:/Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C:mManufactoringDuration} schematic apply A schematic class UFGSchematic {schematic:/Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C:GetTechTier} research apply A research tree class UFGResearchTree {research:/Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/BPD_ResearchTree_Mycelia.BPD_ResearchTree_Mycelia_C:GetDisplayName} category apply A category class UFGCategory {category:SampleBalanceCategory:mDisplayName} dataasset apply A data asset instance (asset path or KDataForge dataasset id) UDataAsset {dataasset:CleanerItem_SuperIngot:mProductionTime} asset apply Any asset object by path none {asset:/Game/Path/To/Asset.Asset:SomeProperty} Class targets accept the same forms as any class reference: a full path, /Script/Module.Class , a Blueprint class path ( _C is retried when missing), a bare id of content generated in the same pack ( SampleBalanceCategory ), or a generated class path. A target that is not of the provider’s base class is an error: {item:...Recipe_IngotIron_C:...} fails. A third-party mod can add more prefixes, see Writing a provider .

sections.heading: The body: <target>:<member>
sections.text: The target never contains a colon, so the first : after it starts the member. A member is either a property or a function : {item:<class>:mDisplayName} a property of the class default object {item:<class>:mStruct.Field} a path through structs {item:<class>:mIngredients[0].Amount} an array element {item:<class>:GetItemName} a function, no parentheses {item:<class>:GetItemName()} the same, with parentheses {class:<class>:FClamp(3.5, 0, 3)} a function with arguments Property paths use the same syntax as path: in patches and read through class defaults. A bare name is read as a property when the class has one with that name, otherwise it is called as a function. Blueprint-authored property names work as well. What you get back: Reflected type Result bool true or false , typed boolean integers a whole number float , double fixed-point text with at least one decimal ( 2.0 , 0.125 ) enum the value name, for example SS_BIG FString , FName the string FText the text; keeps its localization when it is the only piece class or object reference the object path FGameplayTag the tag name TArray , TSet , gameplay tag container a list Other types (for example a struct that is not a gameplay tag) cannot be inserted as text. The token fails with an error that names the type.

sections.heading: Calling functions
sections.text: A function can be called when it is safe to run while content loads: it is Native and either BlueprintPure , or a non-static const member; it returns a value; it is not a network function ( Net* ), Exec , delegate, or Blueprint event; all its parameters are inputs. Output parameters are not supported; a const reference input is fine; parameter and return types are limited to bool , integers, floats, enums, FString , FName , FText , class and soft class references, gameplay tags, and structs made of those (up to three levels deep). An object reference is allowed as a parameter only, never as the return value; a non-static member of an AActor , UActorComponent or USubsystem is not callable. Static functions are allowed on any class, which is what makes function libraries usable. Property reads are always fine. Non-static members run on the class default object (class targets) or on the asset (object targets). Every call is logged at verbose level.

sections.heading: Implicit and explicit arguments
sections.text: Class targets. If the function has exactly one input and it is a class reference that fits the target class, KDataForge passes the target class for you. That is why GetItemName needs no argument although the engine function is GetItemName(inClass) . Object targets ( dataasset , asset ). A static function with exactly one input that accepts the object gets the object implicitly. Every other input must be written inside the parentheses, separated by commas. The count has to match exactly.

sections.heading: Argument literals
sections.text: Literal Examples number 3 , -1 , 2.5 string 'text' , "text" (escapes \\ , \' , \" , \n , \t ) boolean true , false enum value or name SS_BIG , EStackSize::SS_BIG , Tag.Name as a string class, object or tag a string: '/Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor' , 'KDF.Sample.Test' struct, in field order Vector{3, 4, 0} , {3, 4, 0} struct, by field name Vector{X=3, Y=4, Z=0} , {X=3, Y=4, Z=0} Struct literals can be nested up to 64 levels. Commas inside quotes, brackets, parentheses and braces do not split arguments. The struct type name is optional and a leading F is ignored. Each literal is converted with the same rules as a value: in a patch, so everything on Property Types applies. function-calls.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : # No arguments, implicit class: the stack size of the Iron Ingot as an integer. - path : mResourceSinkPoints value : ' {item:/Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C:GetStackSize} ' # Three explicit arguments, one of them a nested config token. - path : mEnergyValue value : ' {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:FClamp({cfg:balance.ironSpeed}, 0.5, 3)} ' # A struct literal, positional and by field name. Both give 5.0. - path : mRadioactiveDecay value : ' {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:VSize(Vector{3, 4, 0})} ' - path : mRadioactiveDecay value : ' {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:VSize({X=3, Y=4, Z=0})} ' Failed calls are reported with the reason: Message Meaning only native functions can be called A Blueprint function. the function must be BlueprintPure or a const member It can change state. output parameter X is not supported It has an out parameter. non-static members of actors, components and subsystems are not callable Use a property read or a static function. X expects N argument(s) but M were given Argument count mismatch. The editor checks all of this against the reflection data of a bound .kdfdata archive ( template.member-not-callable , template.argument-count , template.argument-type ).

sections.heading: Nesting
sections.text: A token can contain other tokens. The inner ones resolve first, up to four levels: nested.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mDescription value : ' Clamped speed {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:FClamp({cfg:balance.ironSpeed}, 0.5, {cfg:balance.ironSpeed})} ' Pre-pass tokens are replaced everywhere, including inside the body of an apply-time token, so the config value is already in place when the function is called. Substituted values are never scanned again, which means a text value that happens to contain braces is safe. This includes text that looks like an apply-time token: a string a player types into a setting, or one sent by a multiplayer host, is inserted as plain text and never calls a function.

sections.heading: Whole-token typed values
sections.text: An apply-time token that is the entire value of value , min or max keeps its type instead of becoming text. Numbers stay numbers, lists stay lists, class and object results become paths, and an FText becomes the text itself (with its localization). copy-values.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronPlate.Recipe_IronPlate_C properties : # The Iron Plate recipe takes exactly as long as the Iron Ingot recipe. - path : mManufactoringDuration value : ' {recipe:/Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C:mManufactoringDuration} ' # A rounded, typed integer. - path : mProduct[0].Amount value : ' {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:Round({cfg:balance.ironSpeed})} ' The same is true for list elements and members of a struct value: each one that is exactly one token is replaced by its typed result. If one token cannot be resolved, that operation fails with an error that names the token and the reason. Nothing is written for it, and the other operations still run. A pre-pass token that cannot be resolved stays in the text as written and logs a warning. Prefixes are case-sensitive . {Item:...} and {CFG:...} are not tokens, and a prefix that is one letter off ( {itm:...} ) is not either. They stay in the text as written, and the load report and KDF.Template log a warning that names the text and suggests the registered spelling. Any other {...} is left alone without a warning.

sections.heading: Escaping
sections.text: A backslash directly before { and a registered prefix turns the token into literal text: escape.item.yml type : item items : - id : EscapeDemo parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mDescription value : ' Use \{cfg:balance.ironSpeed} to read the speed, it is {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} now. ' This produces Use {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} to read the speed, it is 2.0 now. Each phase removes only its own escapes, so \{item:...} survives the pre-pass and is un-escaped when the operation is applied. In a YAML double-quoted string a backslash is itself an escape, so write \\{cfg:...} . Single-quoted, plain and block scalars take \{ as written. The backslash only counts directly before { and a registered prefix. Any other {...} is left alone, so {0} and similar text-format arguments pass through untouched.

sections.heading: Formatting of inserted values
sections.text: Numbers are written in a fixed, culture-independent form so that saves and multiplayer peers agree: integers as whole numbers; floats and doubles in fixed point with the field’s decimals (or the digits of its step , otherwise 4 for float and 6 for double ), trailing zeros removed, at least one decimal: 2.0 , 0.25 , 1.5 ; booleans as true or false ; lists joined with , when they end up inside text: KDF.Sample.Test, KDF.Sample.Plain . When the destination is an FText property, literal text and token results are joined as text. A string that consists of a single FText token keeps that text unchanged, including its key and namespace, so a translated name stays translated.

sections.heading: Quoting pitfalls
sections.text: YAML decides what a plain scalar means before KDataForge sees it: You write What happens Write instead value: {cfg:texts.motto} text A plain scalar starting with { is a flow mapping. The editor reports template.unquoted-start and the YAML does not parse. value: "{cfg:texts.motto} text" or single quotes value: Speed: {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} : inside a plain scalar starts a mapping. Quote the whole value value: "cfg:balance.ironSpeed" Quoted, so the text cfg:balance.ironSpeed . value: cfg:balance.ironSpeed value: cfg:balance.ironSpeed x Not a whole reference; plain text. value: "{cfg:balance.ironSpeed} x" value: "\{cfg:x}" \{ is not a valid escape in a double-quoted YAML string. '\{cfg:x}' or "\\{cfg:x}" config: !features.enableBonus A leading ! starts a YAML tag. The editor reports config.expression-quote . config: '!features.enableBonus' a token with a trailing # ... Starts a YAML comment inside a plain scalar. Quote it Use single quotes when the text contains " , double quotes when it contains ' . Inside a double-quoted YAML string, use single-quoted literals in expressions and function arguments, and the other way round.

sections.heading: Writing a provider
sections.text: Mods can add their own prefixes through KDataForgeApi . A provider is a class that implements IKDFTemplateProvider : class FMyProvider final : public IKDFTemplateProvider { public: virtual FName GetPrefix () const override { return FName ( TEXT ( " my " )); } virtual EKDFTemplatePhase GetPhase () const override { return EKDFTemplatePhase::ApplyTime; } virtual FKDFTemplateResult Resolve ( const FKDFTemplateRequest & Request ) override { FKDFTemplateResult Result; Result . mStatus = EKDFTemplateStatus::Resolved; Result . mValue = FKDFConfigValue:: MakeScalar (EKDFConfigValueType::String, Request . mBody ); return Result; } }; // During CONSTRUCTION, next to handler registration: FKDFTemplateProviderRegistry:: RegisterWithSpelling ( MakeShared <FMyProvider>(), TEXT ( " my " )); The prefix must match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]* . The first registration wins and the built-in prefixes are reserved. Documents match the prefix case-sensitively against the spelling you pass to RegisterWithSpelling . Plain Register uses GetPrefix().ToString() instead, and Unreal keeps the letter case of whichever spelling of a name it saw first ( item may read back as Item ), so use RegisterWithSpelling to get exactly the prefix you wrote. Resolve runs on the game thread. Return Resolved with a typed mValue (and mText with bHasText for an FText ), Unavailable when the source does not exist yet (the document is deferred), NotFound , or Error with mError . Set bWorldBound when the answer depends on the world or session so that it is re-read when those change. See API Design for the rest of the public API.

sections.heading: Testing templates
sections.text: KDF.Template "Speed {cfg:balance.ironSpeed}x, stack {item:/Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C:GetStackSize}" KDFSample KDF.Template "<text>" [pack] expands the text with both phases and prints the result and any warnings to the log. The optional pack scopes cfg: and bare generated ids. In Blueprint, Resolve Template String and Resolve Template Text do the same, see the Blueprint Config API . Quote text containing spaces. Inside the quoted text, use \" for a literal double quote and \\ for a literal backslash; other backslashes stay literal. The optional pack must be one unquoted word. Missing closing quotes or extra arguments produce a usage error. The console normalizes whitespace runs to a single space before the command receives the text. KDF.Template "Status: \"{cfg:texts.motto}\"" KDFSample

sections.heading: Editor diagnostics
sections.text: Code Severity Meaning template.unquoted-start error A plain scalar starts with { . template.unbalanced error {prefix: without a closing } . template.malformed error Empty id, bad id, a missing member, or a malformed reference. template.unknown-provider warning A near miss of a registered prefix such as cfgg . Other unknown braces stay literal and silent. template.unknown-member warning The member is neither a property nor a function of the target. template.member-not-callable error The function violates the call rules above. template.argument-count , template.argument-type error Wrong number or type of arguments. template.class-family error The target is not of the provider’s base class. template.nesting-depth error Tokens nested deeper than four levels. config.unknown-id , config.case-mismatch error, warning The config id does not exist, or differs only in letter case. config.ref-not-resolved warning A reference sits where KDataForge never resolves it. config.type-mismatch error or warning The value type does not fit the destination property. The member checks need a bound reflection archive, see KDataForge Tools .

pages.title: Type: unlock
pages.description: Generating a standalone, reusable FGUnlock subclass from YAML, and why most people actually want the schematic-level unlocks list instead.

sections.heading: Type: unlock
sections.text: This document type sits in the Items stage at priority 40 , after generic class ( 50 ) and ahead of item , resource , and building . That ordering lets later content reference generated unlock classes. It loads during session initialization, so a restart is needed after changes. Its entries key is unlocks . There is no default parent ; provide a concrete FGUnlock subclass that derives from /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlock . Register-only entries ( class: ) are not supported, so use id: . Read this carefully before reaching for it: most packs never need this document type. If you just want a schematic to unlock a recipe, which is the overwhelmingly common case, use the schematic’s own inline unlocks: list instead. See Schematics → Instanced unlocks . That creates an unlock instance directly on the schematic’s CDO with no separate class needed. type: unlock exists for a narrower case. You want one preconfigured unlock class, with baked-in default properties, that you intend to reference by class from multiple schematics, or hand off to another mod, without repeating the same property block every time. parent: can be any concrete FGUnlock subclass the base game ships. See the Base-Game Unlock Classes for the full list and their settable properties.

sections.heading: Worked example, a reusable “give starter items” unlock
sections.text: The pattern below generates a single FGUnlockInventorySlot subclass with its slot count baked in. Any schematic can then grant the exact same reward just by pointing at the generated class, instead of re-declaring the property every time: starter-kit.unlock.yml type : unlock unlocks : - id : MyStarterKitUnlock parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockInventorySlot.BP_UnlockInventorySlot_C # any concrete FGUnlock subclass properties : - path : mNumInventorySlotsToUnlock value : 3 This generates /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_MyStarterKitUnlock , a class, not an instance. Reference it from a schematic exactly like any other unlock class: some.schematic.yml type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_UsesStarterKit properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Starter Kit Schematic unlocks : - class : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MyStarterKitUnlock

sections.heading: Why it has to run first
sections.text: Unlocks generate at priority 40 , after generic class ( 50 ) and ahead of item ( 30 ), resource ( 25 ), and building ( 20 ). All five sit within the Items stage. This ordering exists specifically so that a schematic generated later in the same pack can reference the unlock class the moment it’s created, with no include: gymnastics needed.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: “Why didn’t my item unlock show up on the schematic?” Nine times out of ten this means you meant the schematic’s inline unlocks: list (a FGUnlockRecipe / FGUnlockSchematic /etc. instance configured right where it’s used), not a standalone generated class. See Type: schematic first. Reusing one unlock class across many schematics and want to change a default later? Edit the type: unlock document’s properties: . Every schematic referencing that generated class picks up the new CDO default the next time a fresh instance is created from it. Existing save data that already holds an old instance is unaffected, same as any other CDO-default change.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.description: Build the smallest possible pack, confirm it loads, and learn the report, logging, and restart workflow.

sections.heading: Getting Started
sections.text: Start here if you have never written a KDataForge pack before. It walks through the smallest useful pack: one folder with two files . Along the way you’ll touch every piece of tooling you need on day one, including where files go, the /kdf chat commands, how to read the load report, debug logging, multiplayer, and the most common ways a fresh pack silently does nothing. The Task Guides build on this shape to accomplish specific goals. Examples contains complete packs that combine several capabilities, while Features explains each capability.

sections.heading: Where files go
sections.text: Author packs under your mod’s canonical root: <your-mod>/DataForge/ pack.yml faster-smelting.cdo.yml KDataForge starts its recursive scan at the Unreal project directory, which is FactoryGame/ in a packaged game. Up to six levels below that project root, it recognizes any directory named DataForge , the legacy name data-editor , or any directory that directly contains pack.yml . Names are case-insensitive. Every *.yml or *.yaml file below a detected root is a document, or several documents when separated with --- . See Multiple Documents Per File . Detected roots may nest. A YAML file belongs only to its deepest enclosing root, so a nested pack is not also loaded by its parent. Heavy engine directories such as Content , Saved , Plugins , and Source are pruned during root discovery.

sections.heading: pack.yml
sections.text: A pack.yml manifest is how a set of documents becomes a named, versioned unit instead of a pile of loose files. It is optional. Without a manifest, the implicit pack ref and name come from the parent directory of the detected root. That fallback can change when a folder moves, so declare an explicit stable ref from day one. The ref is the save-persistence contract: ref : MyFirstPack name : My First Pack version : 1.0.0

sections.heading: The first patch: half smelting time
