sections.text: A type: cdo document patches properties directly on a class’s default object. Setting mManufactoringDuration to a fraction of its original value halves the crafting time. It’s a good first patch to try because the result is immediately visible in-game: faster-smelting.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.5 Start the game and iron ingots now smelt twice as fast. The type: key is optional here. The .cdo.yml filename suffix would set the root type via the filename convention ( <name>.<type>.yml ), but an explicit type: always wins.

sections.heading: /kdf report and loading changes
sections.text: /kdf report : prints the load report, showing which packs and documents were found, what was applied, and every diagnostic (see below). /kdf reload : restores KDataForge-touched reflected properties to their original session baseline, rescans every pack file (including edited configuration values files : hot values apply, cold values report “restart required”), then runs the normal deterministic stage pipeline again. KDF.Reload : runs the same smart reload from a host or dedicated-server console. /kdf sound PackRef Id : previews an imported Wwise sound on the local client. Console equivalent: KDF.Sound PackRef Id . See Wwise Sounds . After editing a file, run /kdf reload , then use /kdf report to inspect the replacement load. Only the listen host, a dedicated-server administrator, or the server console may reload.

sections.heading: Smart reload
sections.text: Reload does not blindly apply an add , append , or multiply operation on top of its previous result. Before re-applying files, KDataForge restores every touched top-level reflected property to the value captured before KDataForge first changed it this session. This also removes property changes from files deleted since the previous load. Invalid documents are skipped under normal diagnostic rules, so their old property effects are not retained. Reload clears and rebuilds actor patches, lazy-class watches, content-removal rules, resource-node rules, registration queues, diagnostics, and patch history. Any open /kdf editor window closes because its undo history refers to the pre-reload state.

sections.heading: Restart boundaries
sections.text: Some engine state cannot be reversed safely after world startup: SML freezes recipe, schematic, research-tree, and sink-point registrations before BeginPlay. New, deleted, or re-registered entries need a session restart to change those live registries. Content already removed by a remove: rule is not re-added when that rule disappears. Reload updates the rule set for later checks; restart the session to rebuild availability from startup. Generated UObject identities, gameplay tags, and localization entries are process-lifetime state. Current files can update existing objects or strings, but deleting their definitions does not unload them. Restart to prove removal. resourcenode reload rules apply immediately. Node destruction is server-authoritative and may create vanilla save tombstones; removing the rule cannot resurrect already destroyed nodes. Reload is process-local. Multiplayer clients do not receive the host’s reload. Restart every process with the same pack set when changes must be multiplayer-consistent. Prefer clicking over typing? /kdf editor opens the in-game editor. Runtime browses reflected objects, applies supported property operations live, and exports YAML. Packs browses files grouped by their owning pack.yml , creates packs below <ProjectDir>/Mods/DataForge/<pack-name>/ , and edits every YAML node through Form or Raw YAML mode. Form mode includes schema-aware field/entry templates, filtered class selectors, reflected property paths, supported-operation choices, and enum/boolean presets. Save validates and writes atomically; /kdf reload applies live-safe file changes.

sections.heading: Reading the report
sections.text: Diagnostics are never fatal . A broken file is skipped and the load continues. Each one carries a severity that tells you how much attention it deserves: Severity Meaning Example Info Expected skips, not printed by /kdf report A document’s conditions: failed (mod not installed, version mismatch) Warning Tolerated problems Unknown root type, duplicate pack ref Error A file, document, or single patch was skipped Malformed YAML, target class not found, unsupported op×type combination

sections.heading: Debugging
sections.text: Every applied op can be traced with debug logging, and you get to choose how wide the net is cast: per document, per pack, or globally across every pack loaded. Per document : add debug: true at the top level of any document type. Every applied op from that file logs: faster-smelting.cdo.yml type : cdo debug : true patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.5 Per pack : add debug: true to pack.yml . Every document of the pack logs: ref : MyFirstPack name : My First Pack version : 1.0.0 debug : true Global : set the console variable KDF.Debug 1 (open the console with ~ ) or launch the game with -KDFDebug . Everything logs then, including ops originating from the in-game editor. Each applied op produces one line at Log verbosity: [KDF DEBUG] faster-smelting.cdo.yml: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C.mManufactoringDuration multiply : 2.000000 -> 1.000000 The format is <file>: <target path>.<property path> <op> : <pre value> -> <post value> . The pre/post pair is what makes it useful: you see exactly what a multiply or append actually did. Where the log lives : in a packaged game the log file is %LOCALAPPDATA%\FactoryGame\Saved\Logs\FactoryGame.log . Search it for [KDF DEBUG] .

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: KDataForge loads YAML independently in every game process. It does not negotiate pack checksums, reject mismatches, or stream applied operations from the server. Install the same pack set and versions on the dedicated server or host and on every client. The one thing the host does send to clients is the value of each pack configuration field, held in memory only. The in-game editor’s live property changes are local to the process where they are made. Export those changes to YAML and distribute the resulting pack when they must be consistent for all players.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Most “nothing happened” reports trace back to one of a small handful of causes. Check these before assuming something is broken: Symptom Likely cause / fix File is ignored entirely Missing type: key and the filename doesn’t follow the <name>.<type>.yml convention. Add one of the two One document of a multi-document file is ignored Every document in a --- -separated file needs its own type: key. The filename convention only works for single-document files, see Multiple Documents Per File “class not found” Check the path form: cooked Blueprint asset classes use _C ( /Game/....Asset.Asset_C , auto-retried if omitted), native classes use /Script/Module.Class , and KDataForge-generated classes use /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> with no _C . The short id: also works when unambiguous; see Generated Content Short Ids Op rejected at load time Unsupported op×type combination. Check the op table in the YAML Schema and the per-op examples in Operations Data-asset instance not found Instances (not classes) have no _C suffix, see Targeting Change applied but not visible on placed buildings Saves/archetypes override CDO values. Use a runtime actor patch ( applyToSpawnedActors ), see Buildings

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.text: KDataForge Tools : edit YAML and catch malformed documents or schema mistakes before launching the game Lint Your Pack : reproduce existing KPatchwork pull-request policy checks Targeting : every way to select what a patch applies to Balancing : recipes, items, schematics, research Items , Recipes , Schematics : new content from YAML, or the tied-together End-to-End Pack Item + Icon + Recipe + Tier-1 Unlock : this tutorial series’ natural next step, walking through exactly that trio Pack Configuration : let players change numbers, toggles and texts of your pack without editing YAML

pages.title: Lint Your Pack
pages.description: Validate packs in KDataForge Pack Manager or with the kdf lint command, including pack configuration, templates and cold properties; reproduce existing KPatchwork CI checks with the standalone linter.

sections.heading: Recommended: KDataForge Pack Manager
sections.text: For local pack authoring, use KDataForge Pack Manager instead of installing the standalone Python linter. Open your project, edit YAML in the Code or Visual editor, and review live diagnostics in Problems . For a full project check, choose Lint pack under Settings → Language server . An optional .kdfdata reflection archive adds class and property information. After validation, test the pack in game with /kdf report . KPatchwork’s pull-request CI still uses the pinned Python linter and repository-specific policy schemas. Use the commands below when reproducing that existing CI result. The desktop app validates KDataForge runtime grammar, so a passing desktop check does not replace KPatchwork’s policy check.

sections.heading: Command line: kdf lint
sections.text: The checks of the desktop app also run without the window. kdf lint <path> is the command-line front end of the same validation core: it reads the same schemas and applies the same rules as the Problems panel, including everything in Configuration, template and cold-property checks below. kdf lint <your-mod> kdf lint <your-mod> --format github kdf lint <your-mod> --datapack C:\Path\2026-10-12.kdfdata kdf lint <your-mod> --warnings-as-errors Option Meaning --format text , json , github , sarif Output format. github produces workflow annotations, sarif code-scanning reports. --datapack <file.kdfdata> A reflection export archive. It enables the class, property, function and setting checks. Without it those checks are skipped instead of guessed. --warnings-as-errors Exit with a failure status on warnings too. --allow-unknown-types Do not report root types that no schema knows (third-party handlers). --schema-dir <dir> , --allow-schema-override Extra schemas, and permission for them to replace bundled ones. --user-settings <file> A settings file with the lint policy (see .kdf-editor.toml in Projects and Packs ). --profile runtime , legacy runtime (default) validates the current runtime grammar. legacy adds the KPatchwork policy rules, for example the required contributer field. --no-color Plain output. <path> follows the same root rules as the Python linter below: pass the folder that contains the DataForge folder (or a folder of several nested packs). The command exits with status 1 when it reports an error.

sections.heading: Configuration, template and cold-property checks
sections.text: These rules were added with pack configuration . They run in the desktop app, in kdf lint , and in the language server. Area Codes What is checked Config definitions config.filename , config.filename-type , config.duplicate-id , config.prefix-clash , config.id-reserved , config.default-invalid , config.range-invalid , config.option-invalid , config.category-missing , config.category-invalid , config.reserved-key , plus schema errors such as a missing name or description File naming, unique and well-formed ids, defaults that satisfy their type, ranges, options, categories that are UFGCategory classes References config.unknown-id , config.unknown-pack , config.pack-disabled , config.case-mismatch , config.type-mismatch , config.ref-not-resolved Every cfg: and {cfg:} reference points at an existing field, the field type fits the destination, nothing sits where it is never resolved Expressions config.expression-syntax , config.expression-type , config.expression-quote , config.condition-invalid , config.condition-in-config config: conditions parse, type-check and are quoted safely Templates template.unquoted-start , template.unbalanced , template.malformed , template.unknown-provider , template.nesting-depth , and with a reflection export template.unknown-member , template.member-not-callable , template.argument-count , template.argument-type , template.class-family Token syntax, nesting depth, known providers, and for apply-time providers whether the member exists and is callable with those arguments Hot and cold config.hot-in-cold-stage , config.hot-in-condition , config.hot-into-cold-property , property.cold Hot values used where only load-time values apply, and operations that target cold or newActors properties (needs a reflection export) Game settings setting.unknown-id , setting.type-mismatch session: , ags: and option: ids against the settings index of a reflection export (only when it contains one) Pack icon pack.icon-missing , pack.icon-escape , pack.icon-format , pack.icon-symlink , pack.icon-path The icon file exists, stays inside the pack, has a supported format, and is not a symlink out of the pack property.cold is information by default. Set coldProperties under [lint] in .kdf-editor.toml to "info" , "hint" or "off" to change it. Severities of the other codes follow the table on the templates and expressions pages.

sections.heading: Standalone Python linter for existing CI
sections.text: Standalone KDataForge Linter validates packs with bundled schemas. Its CLI uses a lint subcommand plus a path: kdataforge-linter lint DataForge kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --format github kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --format json kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --allow-unknown-types Useful options include --schema-dir <dir> for extra schemas, --allow-schema-override when a custom schema intentionally replaces a bundled one, --allow-unknown-types for handler types that the linter does not know yet, --warnings-as-errors , and --format text|json|github . It also checks instanced FGUnlock and FGAvailabilityDependency references in schematics, research trees, and delivery-task data assets. Native classes with known Blueprint implementations, abstract classes without Blueprint variants, wrong-family references, and unknown class paths emit warnings only. They do not turn an otherwise valid pack into exit code 1 unless you enable --warnings-as-errors . Base-Game Unlock Classes , Mod Unlock Classes , and Availability Dependency Classes document bundled inventory.

sections.heading: KPatchwork policy schemas
sections.text: KPatchwork repository runs this same kdataforge-linter executable, pinned through its pyproject.toml and uv.lock . Repository-local schemas under ci/schemas override selected bundled schemas with KPatchwork policy, such as its required player-facing pack description. The linter is also the validation step used by KPatchwork’s pull-request CI. It reports every issue it finds in one run: warnings are printed but do not fail the command, while errors produce exit code 1 . Run KPatchwork’s exact CI-equivalent command from its repository root: Terminal window uv run --locked kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --schema-dir ci/schemas --allow-schema-override --format github

sections.heading: Get the linter
sections.text: Install uv and Git, then clone KPatchwork: Terminal window git clone https://github.com/Satisfactory-KMods/KPatchwork.git cd KPatchwork KPatchwork currently requires Python 3.11 or newer. uv run --locked creates the required Python environment from the repository’s lockfile, so you do not need to install PyYAML manually.

sections.heading: Choose the correct root
sections.text: The positional <path> after lint is the directory searched recursively for pack.yml files and YAML documents. Every manifest must be at least one directory below that path. For the standard standalone layout from Getting Started , pass <your-mod> , not its DataForge child: <your-mod>/ DataForge/ pack.yml faster-smelting.cdo.yml From the cloned KPatchwork directory, its pinned executable can also lint an external mod without the repository policy override: Terminal window uv run --locked kdataforge-linter lint " <your-mod> " For a repository containing several nested packs, pass their common container instead: Pack layout <path> value <your-mod>/DataForge/pack.yml <your-mod> <your-mod>/DataForge/<pack-name>/pack.yml <your-mod>/DataForge KPatchwork/DataForge/<category>/<pack>/pack.yml DataForge The linter examines every .yml and .yaml below the selected root. Choose the narrowest root that still leaves at least one directory between the root and each pack.yml ; otherwise unrelated YAML files may be reported as being outside a pack.

sections.heading: KPatchwork policy fields
sections.text: Caution KPatchwork’s policy linter requires a contributer field spelled exactly this way. This is repository ownership metadata, not a required KDataForge runtime manifest field. A standalone pack can be valid at runtime and still fail this policy check when the field is absent. The current standalone KDataForge Linter schema also validates contributer , so it may report the same field. Treat that as current linter policy, not runtime grammar. Standalone schemas accept an optional string description in pack.yml . KPatchwork’s override requires it because CI uses the text on its generated mod page. The KDataForge runtime also reads it, as the pack description for settings screens, see Pack Configuration . When preparing a pack for KPatchwork, add your GitHub login or a non-empty list of co-maintainers: ref : MyTweaks name : My Tweaks version : 1.0.0 description : Explains player-facing compatibility changes supplied by this pack. contributer : - your-github-login KPatchwork CI uses this value for ownership checks as well as linting. Changing the field in that repository requires maintainer approval.

sections.heading: What current standalone linter checks
sections.text: The current linter checks: YAML syntax, empty documents, and explicit type values in multi-document files; pack manifests, semver-like versions, unique refs, dependencies, missing dependencies, and dependency cycles; known document types and the filename-based <name>.<type>.yml convention; conditions, patch selectors, property paths, operation names, and required operation arguments; inline instances and generated IDs, including duplicate IDs within a pack; generated classes, unlocks, items, resources, buildings, recipes, schematics, and research-tree mutations; top-level remove: for recipe/schematic/research documents, including remove-only documents; sublevel blocking documents and resourcenode removal documents; float/vector curve keys, modes, finite values, and duplicate key times; included files, image assets, data assets, localization entries, game tags, and sink-point entries; symlinks, YAML outside a pack, and files that escape the selected root or pack directory. Unknown condition keys are warnings. Unknown document root types are warnings only when you pass --allow-unknown-types ; otherwise the standalone linter reports them as errors because no schema was available. Structural problems, invalid values, missing files, and duplicate identities are errors.

sections.heading: Version notes
sections.text: The standalone Python linter does not know pack configuration: *.config.yml definitions, cfg: references, templates, config: conditions and the pack icon are checked by the desktop app and kdf lint only. It may report a config document as an unknown root type; validate such packs with the desktop app or kdf lint . Use a current standalone KDataForge Linter build when using newer runtime handlers. Current bundled schemas cover type: sublevel , type: resourcenode , and top-level remove: on type: recipe , type: schematic , and type: research , including remove-only documents. Older linter releases may report those documents as unknown root types or reject remove: as an unexpected field. In that case, update the linter before treating the diagnostic as authoritative. After linting, still verify in game with /kdf report ; static schemas cannot prove runtime class resolution or another mod’s installed content. KPatchwork may pin an older standalone release until its lockfile is updated. Its ci/schemas directory overrides only repository-policy schemas; it does not add every newer runtime handler. Use a current standalone build when checking new KDataForge grammar outside KPatchwork CI.

sections.heading: Read the result
sections.text: A successful run prints the number of packs and documents it checked: lint passed: 1 pack(s), 1 YAML document(s) Errors include the file and the failed rule. Fix every error: line, then run the same command again: error: /path/to/pack.yml: version '1.0' is not semver-like error: /path/to/faster-smelting.cdo.yml: cdo.patches[0] requires properties The linter has no automatic-fix mode. Show current CLI options with: Terminal window uv run --locked kdataforge-linter lint --help

sections.heading: What static linting cannot prove
sections.text: The linter parses files without loading Unreal Engine or Satisfactory. It cannot prove that an asset or class path exists, that a reflected property has the expected runtime type, that another mod is installed, or that two otherwise valid packs produce the intended result together. After linting, start the game and use /kdf report to check runtime resolution and application. Use debug logging when you need the before/after value for each applied operation.

pages.title: Reference
pages.description: Normative grammar, public API, handler implementation, and editor tooling. Lookup material for advanced KDataForge work, not a tutorial.

sections.heading: Reference
sections.text: This section is lookup material, not a walkthrough. Consult these pages when you already know roughly what you’re building and need the exhaustive, field-by-field detail rather than a guided example. Features explains what a capability does and why it’s shaped the way it is, and Examples gives you copy-pasteable YAML. The pages below cover what those sections deliberately leave out: normative grammar, the stable C++ surface, editor tooling, and catalogs. YAML Schema is the complete, normative grammar for packs, document types, pack configuration definitions, typed references and templates, property paths, all 22 operations, conditions, and includes. It’s for pack authors who need to check the exact shape or default of a field rather than read a worked example. API Design documents the public C++ API surface in the KDataForgeApi module. It’s for third-party mod developers who link against KDataForge from native code and need to know which symbols are stable to build against long-term. Handler Template is a reference C++ implementation of a document handler, built around a worked RecipeHandler example. It’s for developers extending KDataForge itself with support for a new YAML root type. UE Editor Integration covers KDF.ApplyToAssets , the console command that applies YAML cdo patches directly onto assets inside the Unreal Editor so the changes can be saved as permanent edits. It’s for mod developers working in editor builds, not the packaged game. Reflection Export documents runtime type export, Blueprint loading, functions, the game settings index, reload classification and the cold-property catalog, Pack Manager bundle import, metadata supplement, and validation commands. Blueprint Config API documents the Blueprint surface of pack configuration: the config description classes per field kind, the function library, apply results, multiplayer roles and events. It’s for anyone building a settings screen. Config Expressions is the grammar, type rules and error codes of the config: condition key. Base-Game Unlock Classes catalogs every base-game FGUnlock subclass, its properties, concrete examples, and instantiation caveats. Mod Unlock Classes does the same for the unlock classes installed mods add, including the Blueprint path to use for each. Availability Dependency Classes catalogs every FGAvailabilityDependency , abstract state, Blueprint/native path, and field.

pages.title: API Design
pages.description: Public C++ handler contract in KDataForgeApi and the KDataForge registration surface used by third-party mods.

sections.heading: API Design
sections.text: Third-party handler types derive against KDataForgeApi . Registering those handlers calls UKDFSubsystem , which lives in the main KDataForge module, so a registering mod links both modules. Other implementation details may change between versions.

sections.heading: Stability guarantees
sections.text: IKDFDataEditorHandler , UKDFHandlerBase , FKDFNode , EKDFStage , EKDFOp , the context structs, and FKDFPatchRecord form the public handler contract. Additive changes are preferred. The main module exposes the registration and integration methods described below. The YAML schema is versioned through the documentation rather than C++ compatibility rules. Breaking schema changes belong in the changelog.

sections.heading: The KDataForgeApi contract
sections.text: Implement IKDFDataEditorHandler , or normally derive from UKDFHandlerBase , for one YAML root type. The interface is C++ only because UKDFDataEditorHandler declares CannotImplementInterfaceInBlueprint . class IKDFDataEditorHandler { virtual FName GetRootType () const = 0 ; virtual EKDFStage GetStage () const = 0 ; virtual int32 GetPriority () const ; virtual bool ValidateDocument ( const FKDFNode & , FKDFValidationContext & ) = 0 ; virtual bool ApplyDocument ( const FKDFNode & , FKDFApplyContext & ) = 0 ; virtual bool ExportObject (UObject * , FKDFNode & , FKDFExportContext & ); // optional virtual UClass * GetEditorPanelClass () const ; // optional }; There is no RevertDocument virtual in the current interface. The framework parser handles raw YAML loading. ApplyDocument performs writes, ValidateDocument performs structural checks, ExportObject supports editor export, and GetEditorPanelClass can provide a custom panel.

sections.heading: FKDFNode , the document model
sections.text: Handlers receive an order-preserving map, sequence, and scalar tree rather than YAML text. Key helpers include Find , FindShared , GetString , GetBool , GetInt , GetFloat , their TryGet* variants, and the MakeMap , MakeSequence , and MakeScalar builders used by exporters.

sections.heading: Contexts
sections.text: Contexts carry mGameInstance , mSourceFile , and a diagnostic sink with AddInfo , AddWarning , and AddError . Diagnostics are non-fatal. FKDFApplyContext adds bDryRun , mPatchRecord , and mAppliedOpCount .

sections.heading: Template providers and config values
sections.text: KDataForgeApi also exports the extension point for {prefix:body} templates : IKDFTemplateProvider ( GetPrefix , GetPhase , Resolve ), the request and result structs, and the thread-safe FKDFTemplateProviderRegistry ( Register , RegisterWithSpelling , Unregister , Find , GetPrefixes , GetPrefixSpellings ). The typed value that providers return and that the Blueprint Config API exchanges is FKDFConfigValue (with EKDFConfigValueType and FKDFConfigKeyedValue ); both live in KDFConfigTypes.h . There is no bLiveReload flag in the handler API. KDataForge scans YAML during GameInstance initialization and again when an authorized host runs /kdf reload . Reload restores captured top-level property baselines before rebuilding and applying the handler pipeline. Frozen SML registrations and irreversible world changes still require a restart.

sections.heading: Registration
sections.text: Register during your game instance module’s CONSTRUCTION phase. Explicit subsystem initialization is required because SML can dispatch module lifecycle phases before custom GameInstance subsystems have been created. #include " Module/GameInstanceModuleManager.h " #include " Subsystems/KDFSubsystem.h " UGameInstanceModuleManager * Modules = GetGameInstance ()-> GetSubsystem < UGameInstanceModuleManager > (); if (Modules != nullptr ) { Modules -> EnsureSubsystemInitialized (UKDFSubsystem:: StaticClass ()); if (UKDFSubsystem * KDF = UKDFSubsystem:: Get ( GetGameInstance ())) { KDF -> RegisterHandler ( NewObject <UMyHandler>(KDF)); } } Add KDataForgeApi for handler types and KDataForge for registration to your module dependencies. The subsystem retains handler objects against garbage collection. Registration after the initial load logs a warning. The documents apply on the next session. Multiple handlers may claim the same root type. They all run in priority order.

sections.heading: Optional soft integration
sections.text: If you only want your mod’s content to be editable, you do not need a custom handler. Reflected properties are already reachable through built-in cdo documents using target , allAssetsOfClass , and matchTag . Recommend a mod-presence condition: conditions : hasMod : YourModRef

sections.heading: Main-module surface
sections.text: Handler registration already links the main module. Handlers that generate content or integrate with the editor can also use these stable, additive entry points: API Purpose GetDynamicContent().GetOrCreateClass / GetOrCreateAsset Create save-stable generated classes or UDataAsset instances QueueContentRegistration / QueueSinkTableRegistration Queue per-world SML content registration before the freeze RegisterActorPatch / GetActorPatches / ClearActorPatches Manage spawn-time FKDFActorPatch rules consumed by UKDFActorPatchSubsystem RegisterNodePurge / GetNodePurges / ClearNodePurges Manage FKDFNodePurge rules consumed by UKDFResourceNodeSubsystem RegisterContentRemoval / GetContentRemovals / ClearContentRemovals Manage exact-class FKDFContentRemoval rules for recipe, schematic, and research content MarkDataAssetsChanged Request optional KAPI or RefinedRDApi consumer rescans after initial load ApplyEditorOp / RestorePropertyText Apply editor writes and restore canonical property text for undo ExportObjectToYaml Export an object to full or changes-only cdo YAML OnToggleEditorRequested() Multicast hook used by the in-game editor UI FKDFPatchUtil::ApplyOpsToObject Apply a parsed properties: sequence with pipeline semantics UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem Apply recipe cleanup for one world and query exact removal rules/counts

sections.heading: Runtime rule lifecycle
sections.text: The three Register* rule families above are retained on UKDFSubsystem for the GameInstance. Registering a rule with the same target class and source file replaces the previous rule. Clearing a rule array only stops later consumers; it does not undo actor writes, restore destroyed resource nodes, or put removed content back into an already-initialized manager. RegisterActorPatch is normally driven by applyToSpawnedActors: true . At world begin play, UKDFActorPatchSubsystem applies matching rules to existing actors; its spawn delegate handles later actors. A rule registered after that initial sweep affects future spawns. Call ApplyPatchesToActor explicitly when a late integration also needs an existing actor updated. RegisterNodePurge is normally driven by type: resourcenode . World initialization, actor-spawn, streamed-level, and deferred sweeps consume the rules. There is no public on-demand whole-world sweep, and destroyed level nodes can already have persistent vanilla save tombstones. RegisterContentRemoval is normally driven by document-level remove: . Schematic and research filtering happens while RegisterQueuedContentForWorld drains the SML registry before its freeze. Recipe rules are different: native add hooks prevent later grants, and UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem::ApplyWorldRemovals can re-run its idempotent save-restored-recipe sweep when the rule set grows. Calling it late does not retroactively remove a schematic or research tree from a registry that already initialized. UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem::Get(WorldContext) exists only for Game and PIE worlds. Its IsRecipeRemoved and IsContentRemoved queries use exact class identity, not ancestry. GetAppliedRemovalCount reports resolvable rules seen by the last application pass, not the number of manager entries changed. WereRemovalsApplied becomes true after the first non-empty application pass and clearing the GameInstance rule list does not reset that per-world history flag. FKDFRecipeRemoval exposes lower-level HasAnyRemovalRules , IsRecipeRemoved , and the server-only SweepSaveRestoredRecipes helper. Normal integrations should use UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem so world timing and reporting stay centralized. Native recipe-add prevention is compiled for packaged runtime builds, not Unreal Editor PIE; PIE still exercises the initialization sweep. Treat unlisted implementation details in the main module as internal.

sections.heading: Versioning
sections.text: KDataForgeApi follows the mod’s CI version. Handler ABI additions should be backwards compatible. Breaking schema changes must update the YAML Schema and the changelog.

sections.heading: Availability Dependency Classes
sections.text: Availability dependencies gate content without granting rewards. sections.heading: Regenerate inventory
sections.text: Run Mods/GameFeatures/KDataForge/Tools/scan_instanced_class_catalog.py inside Unreal Python. It combines Asset Registry's transitive derived-class set and Blueprint ParentClass tags with native header metadata, then writes Saved/KDataForge/instanced-class-catalog.json by default. Set KDF_CLASS_CATALOG_OUTPUT to write a temp comparison file instead. The bundled KDataForge-Linter/src/kdataforge_linter/catalogs/instanced_classes.json snapshot already matches the current Unreal scan, so it does not need regeneration unless classes or Blueprint variants change.

sections.heading: Base-Game Unlock Classes
sections.text: Type: schematic → Instanced unlocks and Type: unlock both work with any concrete FGUnlock subclass. The mechanism is fully generic (resolve class: , NewObject it onto the schematic’s CDO, apply properties: , append to mUnlocks ). Only a couple of unlock types show up in most examples ( FGUnlockRecipe , FGUnlockInventorySlot ); this page catalogs every one the base game ships, so you don’t have to go spelunking through engine headers to find them. For the unlock classes installed mods add on top, see Mod Unlock Classes . ℹ️ Native /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlock… paths with shipped Blueprint variants are accepted. KDataForge remaps them to concrete generated classes; exact Blueprint paths remain accepted. Linter reports native mapped form as warning class.native-remapped , never error. Abstract classes with no Blueprint variant cannot be instanced. Every property name below comes from FactoryGame reflection data.

pages.title: Blueprint Config API
pages.description: Build a pack settings screen in Blueprint. The config description objects, the Blueprint function library, apply results, multiplayer roles and events.

sections.heading: Blueprint Config API
sections.text: Pack configuration is defined in YAML and shown by a UI that a mod or a Blueprint author builds. KDataForge does not ship a settings screen. It gives you one description object per configured field, grouped by category, with typed getters, validating setters, and events, so a widget for each field kind takes a few nodes. Everything below lives in the module KDataForge and is available in Blueprint under the category KDataForge | Config .

sections.heading: The pieces
sections.text: Piece What it is UKDFConfigBlueprintLibrary Blueprint function library: pack list, descriptions by category, apply, multiplayer permissions, templates. All nodes take a world context. UKDFConfigDescription One field. Abstract; each field kind has a subclass with typed getters and setters. FKDFConfigValue A typed value in canonical text form. What descriptions accept and return. FKDFConfigApplyResult What an apply did: saved, reloaded, restart required, errors. FKDFPackInfo One pack: name, description, icon, state, number of fields. UKDFSubsystem Get it with Get KDataForge Subsystem . Holds the delegates On Config Applied , On Config Host Mismatch and On Reload Completed . A description is addressed by its key <pack>:<id> , for example KDFSample:balance.ironSpeed . Descriptions keep their identity across reloads: editing a definition file and running /kdf reload updates the same object in place when the field kind is unchanged, so a widget that holds one stays valid. A field that disappears is kept alive but marked stale ( Is Stale ) and no longer listed.

sections.heading: Field kinds
sections.text: The YAML type , valueType , display and multiple keys select the class: YAML Description class Get Kind type: text , valueType string , text or name UKDFConfigTextDescription Text type: text , valueType: tag UKDFConfigTagDescription Tag type: number , no slider UKDFConfigNumberDescription Number type: number with display: slider (or both min and max ) UKDFConfigSliderDescription (extends Number) Slider type: boolean UKDFConfigBooleanDescription Boolean type: select UKDFConfigSelectDescription Select type: select with multiple: true UKDFConfigMultiSelectDescription (extends Select) MultiSelect type: text or number with multiple: true UKDFConfigListDescription List Get Kind returns EKDFConfigFieldKind ( Text , Tag , Number , Slider , Boolean , Select , MultiSelect , List ). Switch on it, then cast to the matching class to reach the typed functions.

sections.heading: Common functions (every description)
sections.text: Identity and metadata, all pure: Function Returns Get Pack Ref , Get Id , Get Key <pack> , <id> , <pack>:<id> Get Display Name , Get Description Text The name and description as Text Get Tooltip , Has Tooltip FKDFConfigTooltip ( Title , Text ) and whether one exists Get Category Class The UFGCategory subclass (plain UFGCategory while unresolved) Get Apply Mode EKDFConfigApplyMode : Cold or Hot Get Value Type , Is Array EKDFConfigValueType ; whether the field holds a list Get Kind , Get Order The field kind; the sort order inside a category Get Source File , Get Source Line Where the field is defined Is Pack Active False when the owning pack was skipped by its conditions or dependencies Values: Function Returns Get Value The pending value, else the host value, else the stored value. Use this in widgets. Get Effective Value The value the loaded content was built with Get Default Value The default from the definition Get Stored Value The value in the local values file Get Host Value The multiplayer host’s value; type None when there is no override Get Value As String , Get Value As Display Text Canonical text (elements joined with , ); display text with option labels Setters (they set the pending value; nothing is saved until you apply): Function Behavior Set Value (Value, Out Error) Validates and stores. Returns false with Out Error for an invalid value. A number outside min and max is clamped and accepted. Fails on read-only descriptions. Set Value From String (Text, Out Error) Parses canonical text for this field. For a list field it takes one element. Reset To Default Pending value = default. Discard Pending Change Drops the pending value. State: Function True when Is Dirty A pending value exists that differs from the stored value Is Default The current value equals the default Is Restart Required A cold field whose saved value differs from the one the running content uses Is Restart Advised A hot field that also feeds a cold context or cold property Is Read Only The local player may not edit (see Multiplayer ) Is Host Override The multiplayer host overrides this field Is Host Mismatch A cold field whose host value differs from what this client loaded Is Stale The definition vanished Events on every description (assign in the Event Graph): Event Fires On Value Changed The value changed: after an apply, a reload from disk, or when host values arrive. On State Changed A state flag changed (dirty, restart required, host mismatch, stale, active). Events are queued while KDataForge loads or applies and broadcast afterwards, never in the middle of a load. Both pass the description.

sections.heading: Per-kind functions
sections.text: Text ( UKDFConfigTextDescription ): Get Text Kind ( String , Text , Name ), Is Multiline , Get Max Length , Get String and Set String , Get Text and Set Text , Get Name Value . Tag ( UKDFConfigTagDescription ): Get Tag and Set Tag , Get Tag Root , Get Selectable Tags (every tag below the root, for a picker). Number ( UKDFConfigNumberDescription ): Get Number Kind ( Int8 , Int16 , Int32 , Int64 , UInt8 , Float , Double ), Is Integer , Get Int and Set Int , Get Float and Set Float , Has Min , Has Max , Get Min , Get Max , Get Step (0 when none), Get Decimals . Slider ( UKDFConfigSliderDescription ): everything of Number plus Get Normalized (the value as 0 to 1 inside min to max ) and Set Normalized (snapped to step and decimals ). Boolean ( UKDFConfigBooleanDescription ): Get Bool , Set Bool , Toggle . Select ( UKDFConfigSelectDescription ): Get Options (array of FKDFConfigOption with Value and Label ), Get Selected Index ( -1 when the value matches no option), Set Selected Index . Multi-select ( UKDFConfigMultiSelectDescription ): the select functions plus Is Option Selected , Set Option Selected , Get Selected Indices , Set Selected Indices , Get Min Selected (0 when unlimited), Get Max Selected ( -1 when unlimited). List ( UKDFConfigListDescription ): Get Count , Get Element , Set Element , Add Element , Remove Element At , Get Min Count , Get Max Count ( -1 when unlimited). Elements are canonical text of the field’s value type. Every setter returns a Boolean and fills Out Error with a message for the player when the new value is rejected (out of range, too long, not one of the options, too many or too few entries, a tag outside the root).

sections.heading: Values
sections.text: FKDFConfigValue carries a type, an array flag and the elements as canonical text: Member Meaning Type EKDFConfigValueType : None (unset), Bool , Int , Float , String , Text , Name , Tag Is Array True for multiple: true fields Elements Array of strings; exactly one element for a scalar Canonical text is true or false , whole numbers, fixed-point floats without an exponent, and all other types verbatim. Helper nodes avoid hand-building values: Make Config Value Bool , Int , Float , String , Text , Name , Tag and Make Config Value Array (Type, Elements) , and the readers Config Value To Bool , Int , Float , String , Text , Tag (the first element), plus Config Values Equal .

sections.heading: The function library
sections.text: All nodes below take a world context. An empty Pack Ref means all packs where noted.

sections.heading: Packs and descriptions
sections.text: Node Returns Get All Pack Infos Every pack, active or skipped, as FKDFPackInfo Get Pack Info (Pack Ref, Out Info) One pack; false if unknown Get Pack Config Descriptions (Pack Ref) A map Category class to FKDFConfigDescriptionList ( Descriptions ), each list sorted by order Get Sorted Config Categories (Pack Ref) The category classes ordered by their mMenuPriority Get Config Descriptions Flat (Pack Ref) All descriptions sorted by category priority, then order Get All Config Descriptions Every non-stale description of every pack, unsorted Find Config Description (Key) The description for <pack>:<id> , or none Find Config Description By Id (Pack Ref, Id) The same with separate arguments The category map exists because a Blueprint map cannot hold an array as its value; the struct FKDFConfigDescriptionList wraps it. Use Get Sorted Config Categories for the section order and look each category up in the map, or use Get Config Descriptions Flat and start a new section whenever Get Category Class changes.

sections.heading: Pending changes, apply and reload
sections.text: Node Behavior Has Pending Config Changes (Pack Ref) Any description with a pending value Discard Pending Config Changes (Pack Ref) Drops all pending values Apply Config Changes (Pack Ref) Saves pending values and returns an FKDFConfigApplyResult . A hot change triggers exactly one reload. Is Config Restart Required (Pack Ref) Any cold field with a saved change that is not live yet Reload Config From Disk (Pack Ref) Re-reads the values files and applies hot differences. Not available on clients of another game (the result carries an error). Adopt Host Values (Pack Ref) Client action: writes the host’s values into the local file; cold ones then need a restart The same actions exist on UKDFSubsystem as Apply Config Changes , Get Config Net Role and Can Local Player Edit Config .

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: Node Returns Get Config Net Role EKDFConfigNetRole , see below Can Local Player Edit Config False for plain remote clients; true standalone, for the host, on a dedicated server and for dedicated-server administrators

sections.heading: Templates and expressions
sections.text: Node Behavior Resolve Template String (Text, Pack Ref, Out Error) Expands {prefix:body} templates (both phases) and returns the text; Out Error is empty on success. Resolve Template Text (Text, Pack Ref, Out Error) The same, returning Text Evaluate Config Expression (Expression, Pack Ref, Out Result, Out Error) Evaluates a config: expression . Returns false with Out Error when it does not parse or evaluate. Use them for texts such as a settings screen’s own tooltips. See Templates and Typed References for the syntax.

sections.heading: Packs
sections.text: FKDFPackInfo : Member Meaning Ref , Name , Description , Version , Priority From pack.yml ( Name and Description as Text ) Icon A Texture 2D ; decoded the first time a pack info is requested, empty on dedicated servers and for packs without an icon State , State Reason EKDFPackState and a readable detail Config Field Count Number of listed fields Has Pending Config A field has a pending value Restart Required A saved change needs a restart EKDFPackState : Active , DisabledByManifest ( enabled: false ), DuplicateRef (a second pack with the same ref), MissingDependency , DependencyCycle , SkippedByConditions , SkippedByDependency . A pack skipped by its conditions still lists its fields; their Is Pack Active is false, so a screen can show them greyed out.

sections.heading: Applying changes
sections.text: Apply Config Changes returns FKDFConfigApplyResult : Member Meaning Saved At least one value was written to a values file Reloaded A KDataForge reload ran as part of this apply Reload Scheduled A reload is queued because one was already running Restart Required At least one saved change only takes effect after a restart Pending The change was sent to the server and the answer is still outstanding (dedicated-server admin) Request Id Correlates the asynchronous answer; 0 for local applies Changed Keys The <pack>:<id> keys that changed Restart Required Keys Cold fields that need a restart Restart Advised Keys Hot fields that also feed cold contexts or cold properties: applied, but a restart is advised Errors Messages for values that were rejected The flow: pending values become stored values and the values file is written (a write failure rolls that pack back and reports an error). If a hot field changed, KDataForge reloads once. Cold fields stay on their old effective value and appear in Restart Required Keys . Finally every changed description fires On Value Changed and the subsystem fires On Config Applied once with the result. On a dedicated-server administrator’s client there is no local file to write. The apply sends the changes to the server, returns immediately with Pending set, and the real result arrives through On Config Applied . Invalid single values are reported in Errors ; the valid ones in the same request are still applied.

sections.heading: Multiplayer roles
sections.text: Get Config Net Role returns: Role Meaning May edit Local Standalone game yes, files are local ListenHost Host of a listen-server game yes; values are synced to clients DedicatedServer A dedicated server process yes (file plus /kdf reload , or the admin RPC) RemoteClient A client of someone else’s game no, host values are read-only RemoteAdmin A client with dedicated-server administrator rights yes, through an RPC On a listen server only the host may change values; clients see the host’s values read-only. Is Read Only on a description follows the role. While connected, a field the host controls reports Is Host Override ; a cold field whose host value differs from what the client loaded reports Is Host Mismatch . Leaving the session restores the local values. Subsystem events (assign them on the result of Get KDataForge Subsystem ): Event Fires On Config Applied (Result) After a local apply, and when a dedicated-server administrator’s request is answered On Config Host Mismatch (Description) Once per key and join when a cold host value differs from the one this client loaded On Reload Completed A KDataForge reload finished

sections.heading: Building a settings screen
sections.text: This is the node flow of a typical screen. Names are the Blueprint display names. Pack list. Get All Pack Infos , then For Each . Show Name , Description and Icon . Skip packs whose Config Field Count is 0. Grey out entries whose State is not Active . Open a pack. Get Config Descriptions Flat (Pack Ref) gives the fields in display order. For a sectioned layout call Get Sorted Config Categories and, for each category, take the list from Get Pack Config Descriptions with Find . One widget per field. Get Kind , then Switch on EKDFConfigFieldKind : Slider : Cast To KDFConfigSliderDescription . Set the widget’s range from Get Min and Get Max , its step from Get Step , its position from Get Normalized . On change call Set Normalized . Number : a text box. Read with Get Float or Get Int , write with Set Float or Set Int . Boolean : a checkbox with Get Bool and Set Bool . Select : a dropdown filled from Get Options (use each Label ), select Get Selected Index , write Set Selected Index . MultiSelect : a checkbox per option, Is Option Selected and Set Option Selected . Text : Get String / Set String or Get Text / Set Text per Get Text Kind ; use Is Multiline and Get Max Length . Tag : a dropdown filled from Get Selectable Tags , Get Tag and Set Tag . List : rows from Get Count and Get Element ; Add Element , Remove Element At . Show the metadata. Get Display Name as the label, Get Description Text underneath, Get Tooltip for the hover card. A badge for Is Restart Required or Is Restart Advised . Handle rejected input. Every setter returns false with Out Error . Show that text next to the widget and revert the widget to Get Value . Stay in sync. On construction bind On Value Changed and On State Changed of each description to a refresh of its widget. They fire after applies, reloads, and when host values arrive. Respect permissions. Disable the widgets when Is Read Only is true (or Can Local Player Edit Config is false) and mark Is Host Override fields as set by the host. Apply and reset. Enable Apply while Has Pending Config Changes is true and call Apply Config Changes . Show Restart Required Keys or Restart Advised Keys from the result. If Pending is true, wait for On Config Applied . Reset calls Reset To Default on the fields; Cancel calls Discard Pending Config Changes . Host mismatch. Bind On Config Host Mismatch and offer Adopt host values ( Adopt Host Values ), or just inform the player that a restart is needed to match the host. Reading a value in gameplay Blueprint needs no widget: Find Config Description By Id , cast to the kind, and read Get Float , Get Bool , … or use Get Effective Value with Config Value To Float .

sections.heading: Commands
sections.text: Command Where Effect /kdf config dump [pack] chat Lists fields: key, hot or cold, value, default, effective, pending, restart required /kdf config set <pack>:<id> <value> chat (host or dedicated-server admin) Sets the pending value; lists take comma separated elements /kdf config apply [pack] chat (host or dedicated-server admin) Saves, reloads when needed, prints what changed, what needs a restart and what is advised KDF.Config.Dump [pack] console Every value slot (default, stored, pending, effective, host), net role, pack states, file and line KDF.Config.Set <key> <value> console Same as /kdf config set ; also works on a client so that permission errors are visible KDF.Config.Apply [pack] console Same as /kdf config apply KDF.Template "<text>" [pack] console Expands templates KDF.Config.Expr "<expression>" [pack] console Evaluates a config: expression /kdf reload also re-reads edited values files: hot values apply, cold values report restart required.

sections.heading: For C++ users
sections.text: The same objects are plain C++ in the module KDataForge : UKDFConfigRegistry ( UKDFSubsystem::GetConfigRegistry() ), the description classes, and the native delegate UKDFSubsystem::OnConfigAppliedNative() . Mods that only need values can read them through the template and expression engines or call the Blueprint library from C++. Third-party template providers are covered in Templates and Typed References .

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: Pack Configuration Player-Configurable Balancing API Design

pages.title: Config Expressions
pages.description: The grammar, types and error codes of the config key in conditions, which gates packs, documents and single list entries on pack configuration and game settings.

sections.heading: Config Expressions
sections.text: A config: condition decides from pack configuration or game settings whether a pack, a document, or one entry of a list applies. Its value is an expression written as a YAML string: conditions : config : features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed >= 2 config: takes one expression, or a list of expressions that must all be true: conditions : config : - features.enableBonus - balance.ironSpeed >= 2

sections.heading: Where it works
sections.text: Place Effect when false pack.yml conditions: The whole pack is skipped (its settings stay listed, marked not active). A document’s conditions: The document is skipped. conditions: on any entry of any list , at any depth: operations, patches, ingredients, unlocks, nodes, struct list members, … That entry is removed before the document is applied. A config definition ( *.config.yml ) Not allowed ( config.condition-in-config ). A definition cannot depend on its own values. All forms share the keys conditions , conditionBehavior and the older spelling conditionBehaivor . config: is one more key of a condition object, so it combines with hasMod , gameVersion , modVersion and hasClass , with ifNotMatch , and with condition lists exactly as described in Conditions & Packs . bonus-conditions.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : divide value : cfg:balance.ironSpeed # An element condition: this entry is dropped while the bonus is off. - path : mProduct[0].Amount op : multiply value : 2 conditions : config : features.enableBonus # Mixed with other condition keys and negated as a whole. - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.9 conditions : - hasMod : KAPI - config : features.tier == 1 ifNotMatch : true An element condition is evaluated once, before anything is applied, and the three condition keys are stripped from the surviving entries. A condition inside a conditions: block is not an element condition. Two limits: an element-level hasClass cannot see classes that KDataForge generates, and where: filter operands resolve cfg: references but not apply-time templates.

sections.heading: Grammar
sections.text: or := and ( '||' and )* and := cmp ( '&&' cmp )* cmp := unary [ cmp_op unary ] (not chainable) cmp_op := '==' | '!=' | '<' | '<=' | '>' | '>=' | 'contains' | 'in' unary := '!' unary | primary primary := '(' or ')' | '[' [ literal ( ',' literal )* ] ']' | literal | operand literal := number | 'text' | "text" | true | false number := [ '-' ] digits [ '.' digits ] (no exponent) operand := id | cfg:id | cfg:pack:id | session:id | ags:id | option:id id := name ( '.' name )* name = letter or _ followed by letters, digits, _ Precedence from tightest to loosest: ! , comparison, && , || . Use parentheses for anything else. A comparison cannot be chained: a < b < c is an error. Write a < b && b < c . Strings use '...' or "..." with the escapes \\ , \' , \" , \n and \t . A list literal contains literals only: [1, 2, 3] , ['hard', 'extreme'] . Keywords are read after a full dotted name, so in.x is an id and x in [1, 2] is a test. true , false , in and contains cannot be field ids. Keywords, the prefixes cfg: , session: , ags: , option: and string values are case-sensitive : True is an id, CFG:x is not a reference, and 'Hard' == 'hard' is false. ( and ! can be nested up to 64 levels; deeper input is the parse error too-deep .

sections.heading: Operands
sections.text: Operand Reads balance.ironSpeed A field of the own pack. cfg:balance.ironSpeed The same, with the explicit prefix. cfg:Other:shared.level A field of the pack Other . session:<id> , ags:<id> , option:<id> A game setting, see Game settings . The effective value is read, which is what the loaded content was built with: for a cold field the value from the start of the game, for a hot field the current value.

sections.heading: Types and rules
sections.text: Type Comes from boolean boolean fields, true , false number number fields, number literals, select fields with a numeric valueType string text fields (string, text, name, tag), string select fields, string literals list of T any multiple: true field, list literals == and != compare two values of the same type. Numbers compare by value ( 100 equals 100.0 ). Lists cannot be compared; use contains , in , or test emptiness with !list . < , <= , > and >= compare numbers only. list contains x needs a list on the left and an element of the list’s type on the right. x in list is the same test the other way round. && , || and ! work on truthiness: a boolean is itself, a number is true when not 0, a string or list is true when not empty. && and || short-circuit. false && missing is false and does not look at missing . An unknown id, or a type error that is reached, makes the condition false and logs an error. The editor finds these while you type. A setting that is not available yet ( session: and ags: on the main menu) is not an error: the pack or document is deferred and checked again once a save is loaded. ifNotMatch does not turn such an unknown value into a match: the pack or document simply waits.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.text: With the defaults of the sample pack ( balance.ironSpeed 2.0, features.enableBonus true, features.tier 1, tags.extra holding KDF.Sample.Test , a non-empty texts.motto ): Expression Result features.enableBonus true !features.enableBonus false balance.ironSpeed >= 2 true features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed > 3 false features.tier == 1 true features.tier in [2, 3] false tags.extra contains 'KDF.Sample.Test' true !tags.extra false (the list is not empty) texts.motto != '' true (features.tier == 1 || features.tier == 2) && features.enableBonus true features.enableBonus || missing true ( missing is never read) missing || features.enableBonus error: unknown id, so the condition is false cfg:Other:shared.level >= 2 depends on the pack Other ags:FG.GameRules.NoPower == true the live setting (deferred on the main menu) expression-forms.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.9 conditions : config : features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed > 1 - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.95 conditions : config : features.tier in [2, 3] - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : [ KDF.Sample.Plain ] conditions : config : tags.extra contains 'KDF.Sample.Test' - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 1.05 conditions : config : ' !features.enableBonus ' - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 1.1 conditions : config : " texts.motto != '' " - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 1.2 conditions : config : - features.enableBonus - (features.tier == 1 || features.tier == 2)

sections.heading: Writing expressions in YAML
sections.text: The expression is an ordinary YAML scalar, so YAML rules come first: A plain scalar that starts with ! , [ , ' , " , & , * , % , @ or a backtick is not a plain string. Quote the whole expression: config: '!features.enableBonus' . The editor reports an unquoted start as config.expression-quote . The characters : (colon and space) and # also cannot appear in a plain scalar. Quote the expression if you need them. Inside a double-quoted YAML string use single-quoted literals, and the other way round: config: "texts.motto != ''" and config: 'texts.motto != "off"' . In a Markdown table or inline code the pipes of || must be escaped. That is a documentation matter only, the YAML needs no escaping.

sections.heading: Error codes
sections.text: Parse errors name a code and the position (counted in UTF-16 units from the start of the expression): Code Meaning empty The expression is empty or only spaces. unexpected-char A character that is not part of the grammar, for example # . expected-operand An operand is missing: a == , a == == b , ! . expected-close-paren ( without ) . expected-close-bracket [ without ] . unterminated-string A string without its closing quote. invalid-number A malformed number such as 1. (a dot needs digits after it). invalid-ref cfg: , session: , … without an id, or cfg:pack: without an id. reserved-id true , false , in or contains used as an id, for example cfg:true . chained-comparison a < b < c . list-element-not-literal A list literal that contains an id: x in [a, 1] . trailing-input Extra input after a complete expression: a b . too-deep ( and ! nested deeper than 64 levels. The editor adds type checks before the game ever runs: Code Meaning compare-mismatch == or != between different types or two lists. order-non-number < , <= , > or >= on something that is not a number. contains-non-list , in-non-list contains or in without a list on the correct side. list-element-mismatch An element whose type does not fit the list. unknown-id The id is not a field of the pack. They appear in the editor as config.expression-syntax (parse errors) and config.expression-type (type issues). A condition that is not a string or list of strings is config.condition-invalid .

sections.heading: Testing
sections.text: KDF.Config.Expr "features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed >= 2" KDFSample KDF.Config.Expr "<expression>" [pack] prints true , false , or the error. The optional pack decides what a bare id means. In Blueprint use Evaluate Config Expression . Quote expressions containing spaces. Escape double quotes inside the expression as \" , and literal backslashes as \\ ; other backslashes stay literal. The optional pack must be one unquoted word. Missing closing quotes or extra arguments produce a usage error. The console normalizes whitespace runs to a single space, including inside string literals. KDF.Config.Expr "texts.motto == \"Factory first\"" KDFSample

sections.text: Pack Configuration Conditions & Packs Templates and Typed References

pages.title: UE Editor Integration
pages.description: Applying YAML cdo patches directly onto assets inside the Unreal Editor with KDF.ApplyToAssets, turning runtime patches into permanent asset edits (WITH_EDITOR builds only).

sections.heading: UE Editor Integration
sections.text: Everything else in these docs happens at runtime : YAML is re-applied every session and never touches the assets on disk. This page covers the opposite workflow, for mod developers working inside the Unreal Editor . You apply your YAML packs directly onto the editor’s assets so the changes can be saved and become permanent. Editor builds only ( WITH_EDITOR ). None of this exists in the packaged game or on dedicated servers. Players keep the runtime pipeline.

sections.heading: KDF.ApplyToAssets [PathFilter]
sections.text: KDF.ApplyToAssets is a console command available only in editor builds. Run it with no arguments to sweep every scanned pack, or pass a path prefix to restrict the sweep to one branch of the content tree: KDF.ApplyToAssets KDF.ApplyToAssets /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes It only touches documents that explicitly set type: cdo . It uses the same property-path parser and reflection operation engine ( FKDFOpEngine::ApplyOp ) as runtime, pointed at editor objects. Other document types ( item , recipe , asset , …) are runtime concepts, and this command skips them. For each cdo patch, the optional PathFilter restricts application to targets whose path starts with the filter. For example, /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes applies only recipe patches and leaves everything else untouched. The target field resolves the same way it does elsewhere in cdo patches: a class path resolves to that class’s CDO, and anything else is loaded as an object path. Every modified package is marked dirty . For a Blueprint CDO, that is the generated class’s outer package, so the standard editor save flow (Save All or source-control checkout) persists the changes. Your YAML pack has effectively become a set of permanent asset edits. Afterwards, a summary line is logged with the number of ops applied, assets touched, and packages marked dirty. Caution This command is a narrow importer, not the runtime document dispatcher. It reads explicit target: paths and properties: only. It does not expand allAssetsOfClass or matchTag , and it does not reproduce applyToSubclasses , applyToSpawnedActors , or deferOneGameTick . Document conditions and include: ordering are also not evaluated here. Write editor-import patches with explicit targets and review the dirty packages before saving.

sections.heading: In-game editor property categories
sections.text: The in-game /kdf editor groups reflected fields by their Unreal Category metadata. Categories are collapsed by default so large CDOs remain navigable. Reflected fields without CPF_Edit are placed in a separate Non-UPROPERTY / Internal category. Despite that UI label, they are still reflected FProperty fields; they simply lack the normal edit flag or category metadata. They remain available for inspection and editing through the same reflection operation pipeline. CDO exports include these non-edit reflected fields as well.

sections.heading: Runtime-only defer flag
sections.text: Set deferOneGameTick: true on a type: cdo patch when the base game initializes the target during startup and the patch must run after that initialization: type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Some/Class.Some_C deferOneGameTick : true properties : - path : SomeProperty value : 123 KDataForge waits for the matching world to enter BeginPlay , then applies the patch on the following game tick. The flag is deliberately a one-tick startup delay, not a general timer. KDF.ApplyToAssets ignores this flag and applies explicit targets immediately.

sections.heading: When to use which pipeline
sections.text: Both pipelines share the same operation engine and property-path resolution. Target discovery, conditions, timing, and runtime modifiers differ as described above: Runtime (players, packs) Editor ( KDF.ApplyToAssets ) Changes live in YAML, re-applied every session The assets themselves, after saving Reversible Usually on next session. resourcenode destruction can persist in saves; recipe removal self-heals on a later load without the pack Via source control / not saving Audience Players, pack authors Mod developers cooking their own content Document types All ( item , recipe , asset , cdo , …) Explicitly typed cdo with explicit target: only Diagnostics debug: / KDF.Debug plus /kdf report Command warnings and one summary log; no runtime patch report See Resource Node removal before treating runtime YAML as reversible. Vanilla can retain destruction tombstones after that pack is removed.

sections.heading: Still open
sections.text: Asset/image import into the editor (bringing type: asset files in as real texture assets) and editor-side UI polish (search/filter/sort over patchable assets) are not implemented yet. Do not confuse this with the in-game editor ( /kdf editor , opened from chat while playing). That is a separate, runtime-only tool for browsing and editing content live in a running session.

pages.title: Handler Template
pages.description: Reference C++ implementation for creating a new document handler (worked RecipeHandler example).

sections.heading: Handler Template
sections.text: A handler owns one YAML root type and runs in one fixed EKDFStage . It receives parsed FKDFNode documents and never sees raw YAML text directly. Third-party mods write handlers when they want KDataForge’s validation, dry-run preview, diagnostics, and patch records applied to a new root type. Every handler normally derives from UKDFHandlerBase , which lives in the KDataForgeApi module. Registration uses UKDFSubsystem from the main KDataForge module, so the registering mod links both. See Module Structure for why that module boundary exists and what else lives on either side of it. See API Design for the rest of the public contract surface.

sections.heading: Minimal Skeleton
sections.text: A handler is normally two files: a header declaring the UCLASS and overrides, and a .cpp implementing them. The example below is a UMyRecipeHandler that owns a type: recipe document containing a recipes sequence. Start with the header: MyRecipeHandler.h #pragma once #include " CoreMinimal.h " #include " KDFHandlerBase.h " #include " MyRecipeHandler.generated.h " UCLASS () class MYMOD_API UMyRecipeHandler : public UKDFHandlerBase { GENERATED_BODY () public: UMyRecipeHandler (); virtual bool ValidateDocument ( const FKDFNode & Document , FKDFValidationContext & Context ) override ; virtual bool ApplyDocument ( const FKDFNode & Document , FKDFApplyContext & Context ) override ; }; The constructor sets the three identity fields that UKDFHandlerBase exposes: mRootType , mStage , and mPriority . ValidateDocument does cheap structural checks before anything is written, and ApplyDocument does the actual work. Only ApplyDocument is mandatory. UKDFHandlerBase ’s default ValidateDocument simply returns true : MyRecipeHandler.cpp #include " MyRecipeHandler.h " UMyRecipeHandler:: UMyRecipeHandler () { mRootType = TEXT ( " recipe " ); // matches `type: recipe` documents mStage = EKDFStage::Recipes; // fixed stage never reordered by priority mPriority = 0 ; // tie-break within (stage, root type); higher runs earlier } bool UMyRecipeHandler:: ValidateDocument ( const FKDFNode & Document , FKDFValidationContext & Context ) { if ( Document . Find ( TEXT ( " recipes " )) == nullptr ) { Context . AddError ( TEXT ( " recipe document requires a 'recipes' sequence " )); return false ; // skips ApplyDocument; never halts the load } return true ; } bool UMyRecipeHandler:: ApplyDocument ( const FKDFNode & Document , FKDFApplyContext & Context ) { const FKDFNode * Recipes = Document . Find ( TEXT ( " recipes " )); for ( const TSharedRef < FKDFNode >& Recipe : Recipes -> Sequence ) { const FString Id = Recipe -> GetString ( TEXT ( " id " ), FString ()); if ( Id . IsEmpty ()) { Context . AddError ( TEXT ( " recipe entry needs an 'id' " ), Recipe -> Line ); continue ; // per-entry problems are diagnostics, keep going } if ( Context . bDryRun ) { continue ; // resolve/validate only no writes } // … create/modify the recipe class, write properties via FKDFOpEngine/FKDFValueCodec … ++ Context . mAppliedOpCount ; if ( Context . mPatchRecord != nullptr ) { FKDFOpRecord & Op = Context . mPatchRecord -> mOps . AddDefaulted_GetRef (); Op . mTargetObjectPath = /* target path */ Id; Op . mOp = EKDFOp::Set; } } return Context . mAppliedOpCount > 0 ; } Stage order is fixed and shared across every handler, whether built-in or third-party. See Architecture for the full GameTags → Assets → Localization → CDOChanges → Items → Recipes → Buildings → … pipeline that your mStage slots into. mPriority only breaks ties between multiple handlers that share the same (stage, root type) pair. It never lets a handler jump into a different stage.

sections.heading: Registration (your mod’s game instance module)
sections.text: A handler object is useless until KDataForge knows about it. Registration has a hard timing requirement: it must happen during the CONSTRUCTION lifecycle phase, because KDataForge’s own RunInitialLoad() (scan, parse, validate, apply) runs at the later INITIALIZATION phase. Register too late and your handler simply never sees any documents. Do it from your own game instance module’s lifecycle dispatch: #include " Module/GameInstanceModuleManager.h " #include " Subsystems/KDFSubsystem.h " void UMyModGameInstanceModule:: DispatchLifecycleEvent (ELifecyclePhase Phase ) { Super:: DispatchLifecycleEvent (Phase); if (Phase == ELifecyclePhase::CONSTRUCTION) // MUST be CONSTRUCTION — { // KDataForge applies at INITIALIZATION UGameInstanceModuleManager * Modules = GetGameInstance ()-> GetSubsystem < UGameInstanceModuleManager > (); if (Modules != nullptr ) { Modules -> EnsureSubsystemInitialized (UKDFSubsystem:: StaticClass ()); if (UKDFSubsystem * KDF = UKDFSubsystem:: Get ( GetGameInstance ())) { KDF -> RegisterHandler ( NewObject <UMyRecipeHandler>(KDF)); } } } } Add KDataForgeApi and KDataForge to your module dependencies. The explicit initialization is required because SML may dispatch lifecycle phases before custom GameInstance subsystems exist.

sections.heading: Contract Checklist
sections.text: UKDFHandlerBase is forgiving about what you override, but diagnostics, dry-run preview, reports, and editor history depend on a few contracts. Run through these before shipping a handler: mRootType is lowercase and unique to your mod, or intentionally shared: all handlers for a type run, priority-ordered. Report diagnostics via Context.AddError/AddWarning/AddInfo . Never halt, and never call check() on user data. Honor Context.bDryRun : resolve and validate, but do not write. Record ops into Context.mPatchRecord . Reporting and editor history depend on it. If you write CDO properties yourself, snapshot originals first via UKDFSubsystem::GetVanillaCache().RecordSnapshot(...) and retain patched objects via RetainObject(...) . Optional overrides are ExportObject for editor export and GetEditorPanelClass for a custom editor panel. The current interface has no RevertDocument hook.

pages.title: Mod Unlock Classes
pages.description: Every mod FGUnlock subclass, with abstract state, Blueprint path, exact field types, accepted values, nested structs, examples, and caveats.

sections.heading: Mod Unlock Classes
sections.text: KDataForge uses mod unlocks in schematic and delivery-task unlocks: lists exactly like base-game classes. The mechanism is fully generic (resolve class: , NewObject it onto the schematic’s CDO, apply properties: , append to mUnlocks ), so mod-provided classes need no special handling. Known native paths with Blueprint variants automatically remap; exact Blueprint paths also work. Catalog reflects mods loaded during Unreal scan. Use these in a schematic’s instanced unlocks list or in a standalone type: unlock document. For base-game classes see Base-Game Unlock Classes . Caution These classes exist only when provider mod is installed. Gate optional integrations with a hasMod condition ; otherwise unresolved class is reported by /kdf report and skipped.
