sections.text: unlocks : - class : /KLib/Unlocks/BP_GiveToPlayersUnlock.BP_GiveToPlayersUnlock_C properties : - path : mAmounts value : - ItemClass : /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot Amount : 10 Class Fields and accepted types Purpose KLGiveItemToAllPlayerUnlock mAmounts: TArray<FItemAmount> , bCanRepeat: bool Gives listed items to every player KLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases mMaxPurchaseCount: int32 , mCostMultiplierCurve: TObjectPtr<UCurveFloat> , mRewardMultiplierCurve: TObjectPtr<UCurveFloat> , mRewardItemsByLevel: TArray<FKLRepeatPurchaseRewardLevel> , inherited mAmounts: TArray<FItemAmount> and bCanRepeat: bool Level-dependent repeat purchases and rewards, deposited once into Trading Post storage (overflow spawns in a crate beside it) UKLUnlockCleanerItem mItemDescriptor: TSubclassOf<UFGItemDescriptor> Info-only cleaner item entry; extends FGUnlockInfoOnly , so it grants nothing by itself KLNetworkLevelUnlock Deprecated Faxit tier recompute hook KLUnlockExtractorScanner inherited mResourcesToAddToScanner: TArray<TSubclassOf<UFGResourceDescriptor>> (legacy), mResourcePairsToAddToScanner: TArray<FScannableResourcePair> Deprecated; use FGUnlockScannableResource KLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases.mMaxPurchaseCount <= 0 means unlimited. Cost/reward curve X is number of completed purchases, so X=0 controls first purchase and X=1 the second. A null curve property uses multiplier 1, leaving the configured value unchanged. Full worked pack: Repeat-Purchase Schematic (KLIB) .

sections.heading: Mod struct value shapes
sections.text: Struct field Accepted type Constraint / meaning FKLRepeatPurchaseRewardLevel.mPurchaseLevel int32 Minimum 1. First purchase is level 1; highest configured level not above current purchase wins. FKLRepeatPurchaseRewardLevel.mItemsToGive TArray<FItemAmount> Reward items for this level. See base struct shapes . FKLRepeatPurchaseRewardLevel.bOverrideCosts bool When true, replaces normal costs with mCosts . FKLRepeatPurchaseRewardLevel.mCosts TArray<FItemAmount> Replacement costs when bOverrideCosts is true. FKLRepeatPurchaseRewardLevel.mAdditionalCosts TArray<FItemAmount> Costs added only at this exact level. mItemsToGive replaces the complete reward list from its level onward. bOverrideCosts: true replaces the complete raw cost list from that level onward; mAdditionalCosts applies only when mPurchaseLevel matches the current purchase exactly and does not carry forward. Both cost lists are raw values, combined before mCostMultiplierCurve is applied. Runtime-only mCached* and bHasCached* members are transient caches, not KDataForge configuration fields, so they are intentionally excluded.

sections.heading: Deprecated KLib unlocks
sections.text: KLNetworkLevelUnlock carries no data of its own and only forces a Faxit tier recompute; use the KPCLFaxit*Unlock classes below instead. KLUnlockExtractorScanner is superseded by the base-game FGUnlockScannableResource . Both still exist because shipped schematic assets instance them, so do not use either in a new pack.

sections.heading: KPrivateCodeLib fields
sections.text: unlocks : - class : /KPrivateCodeLib/Unlocks/BP_FaxitCapaUnlock.BP_FaxitCapaUnlock_C properties : - path : mCapacityType value : Drive - path : mAmount value : 1 - class : /KPrivateCodeLib/Unlocks/BP_FaxitSpeedUnlock.BP_FaxitSpeedUnlock_C properties : - path : mAmount value : 15000 # fluid units per minute, 1000 units = 1 m³ - path : bIsFluid value : true Class Fields and accepted types Purpose KPCLDeliveryTaskUnlock Enables delivery tasks, the research queue, and manual delivery KPCLDeliveryTaskInventorySlotUnlock mNumInventorySlotsToUnlock: int32 (min 1) Adds slots to the shared delivery-task manual-input inventory KPCLDeliveryTaskQueueSlotUnlock mAmount: int32 (min 1) Raises how many delivery tasks queue at once (limit starts at one) KPCLFaxitCapacityUnlock mCapacityType: EKPCLFaxitCapacityType , mAmount: int32 (min 1), bUseCapacityTypeDefaultAmount: bool Raises machine-network, network, drive, or network-building buffer inventory capacity KPCLFaxitFeatureUnlock mFeature: EKPCLFaxitFeature Enables RemoteAccess, Sink, or Depot KPCLFaxitSpeedUnlock mAmount: int32 (min 1, default 15), bIsFluid: bool Raises solid/fluid transfer rate KPCLDeliveryTaskSlotUnlockBase Abstract delivery-slot base; never instance directly KPCLFaxitUnlockBase Abstract Faxit base; never instance directly Slot/capacity amounts clamp to minimum 1. BufferInventory capacity uses an authored default helper: when bUseCapacityTypeDefaultAmount is true and raw mAmount is 1, the effective amount is 3 buffer slots; writing a custom mAmount disables that default in editor-authored assets. Faxit speed uses items/min for solids ( mAmount: 15 adds 15 items/min) and fluid units/min for fluids (1000 units = 1 m³, so mAmount: 15000 adds 15 m³/min). Faxit unlock values accumulate: every purchase recomputes from base values and reapplies each purchased unlock, so there are no tiers and no curves two capacity unlocks of 1 give the same result as one unlock of 2. pages.title: Reflection Export
pages.description: Export runtime Unreal classes, structs, enums, defaults, functions, game settings, reload classification, Blueprint mappings, and asset indexes for Pack Manager and validation use.

sections.heading: Reflection Export
sections.text: KDataForge can export every reflected type loaded by running game plus Blueprint-generated classes, user-defined structs, and user-defined enums found through Asset Registry. Exporter runs on game thread in bounded slices. JSON writing runs in background.

sections.heading: Run
sections.text: Wait until world begins play, then use console: KDF.DumpReflection Or chat: /kdf-reflection The two commands do not export the same amount: | Start | Options it uses | Result | | Console KDF.DumpReflection (bare) | none | Classes, structs, enums, defaults, Blueprint mappings, textures, the settings index and the cold-property catalog in the final ZIP. No functions, no data-asset or curve indexes and no flattened classes. | | Chat /kdf-reflection (bare) | --assets --functions --flattened --pack --image-max-dimension=1024 | The full profile: everything above plus functions, asset indexes and flattened classes. | | Launch argument -KDFReflectionAutoExport=<dir> | --assets --functions --flattened (and --image-max-dimension from -KDFReflectionAutoImageMaxDimension=<n> if given) | The same export, started automatically once a world has begun play. | For the data the VS Code extension needs (function completion in templates, asset-by-class indexes, inherited properties) use the bare chat command, the auto export, or give the console command the options yourself: KDF.DumpReflection --assets --functions --flattened. The chat defaults apply only when you give no option at all; as soon as you pass one, exactly the options you passed are used. Clients do nothing unless --force is supplied. Server or host is normal export location. Default directory is FactoryGame/KMods/ReflectionExport/. | Option | Meaning | | --out <dir> | Override output directory. | | --mounts /Game,/Plugin | Restrict Blueprint discovery to comma-separated mount points. | | --assets | Add asset-by-class indexes beyond textures; loading attempts still cover every selected registry asset. | | --asset-cap N | Limit assets recorded per class. | | --functions | Include reflected function signatures and flags (see Functions). | | --flattened | Write inherited-property view to classes.flat.ndjson. | | --image-max-dimension N | Largest exported texture side in pixels, 1 to 4096; default 1024. | | --used-textures[=true|false] | Select textures referenced by reflected non-widget class defaults; enabled by default. false selects all supported, portable texture candidates. | | --pack | Compatibility no-op; final ZIP is always written. | | --skip-widgets | Skip widget Blueprints; this is the default when omitted. | | --skip-widgets=true | Skip widget Blueprints, same as --skip-widgets. | | --skip-widgets=false | Include widget Blueprints, same as --widgets. | | --widgets | Shortcut that includes widget Blueprints. | | --budget-ms N | Game-thread budget per tick; default 8. | | --batch-size N | Blueprint load batch size; garbage collection runs between batches. | | --families name:path,... | Extend linter catalog families. | | --force | Allow local client export. | Progress appears in chat and LogKDFReflection. Run KDF.ValidateReflection [--out <dir>] after completion for runtime acceptance checks. Use the Python artifact validator for ZIP integrity, file parity, images, and schema validation; see Validation.

sections.heading: Output
sections.text: - manifest.json: runtime engine/build, platform, options, installed mods, counts, and failed loads. - classes.ndjson, structs.ndjson, enums.ndjson: path-sorted records with inline property data. - classes.flat.ndjson: optional inherited-property view. - indexes/subclasses.json, indexes/assets.json: class and registry lookup indexes. - indexes/settings.json: game settings that session:, ags: and option: references can read, see Settings index. - catalog/cold_properties.json: the cold-property catalog, see Reload classification. - indexes/textures.json: image path, format, dimensions, export method, or per-texture failure reason. - images/**: selected texture images as PNG, proportionally limited to the configured --image-max-dimension cap (default 1024 pixels per side). - nativeMapping.json: native-to-Blueprint and reverse mappings. - catalog/instanced_classes.json: linter family catalog. - schema/reflection.schema.json: draft 2020-12 schema. - <ISO-date>.kdfdata: mandatory ZIP bundle containing every output file. By default, texture selection recursively scans reflected non-widget class defaults. This retains descriptor, item, recipe, and schematic icons while excluding material-only maps, widget-only decoration, unreferenced helper textures, dynamic render/media textures, and transient runtime textures without a portable asset identity. Selected textures remain uncapped and appear in indexes/textures.json with Asset Registry tags, source and exported dimensions, resize state, image path, or explicit failure details. Every successful image is PNG. Cooked BC/BC7 data is decoded before writing; GPU readback supplies pixels when cooked CPU data is unavailable. Images exceeding the configured cap are proportionally downscaled or use a suitable cooked mip. The cap does not upscale images. Missing or unreadable higher mips can produce smaller output even when the source fits within the cap. Source/exported dimensions and resized record the result. Cooked-decode and GPU-readback fallbacks warn when using a lower mip than requested; the raw platformMipPng path does not. Unavailable textures remain indexed but produce no placeholder image. Each encoded PNG is limited to 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes). Larger previews are not written; their texture metadata remains indexed with status: error, errorCode: encodedImageTooLarge, and an increased image error count. Reduce --image-max-dimension and rerun the export to retry. With --used-textures=false, selection expands to all supported, portable texture candidates, including candidates not referenced by those defaults. The manifest's options.usedTexturesOnly records that choice: true pairs with options.textureSelection: reflectedNonWidgetClassDefaults, and false with options.textureSelection: allPortableTextures. options.imageMaxDimension records the actual image cap; consumers should read it instead of assuming every export uses 1024. Current exports containing options.imageMaxDimension must include both options.usedTexturesOnly and options.textureSelection with the consistent pairing above. If either selection field is present, its partner is required too. Legacy schemaVersion: 1 exports may omit all three fields. Exporter attempts to load every previously unloaded registry asset under configured mounts with quiet/no-warn flags and bounded batches. Failed loads remain in manifest. Garbage collection runs through engine safe points, never directly from ticker-time export code. --assets adds indexes for data assets, curves, and other classes referenced by object properties; --asset-cap applies only to non-texture index classes, not loading coverage. Native constructors sometimes generate a fresh GUID, current timestamp, seed, transient object name, or uninitialized byte sequence. Exporter detects volatile reflected types and values, emits reflected zero value, and writes defaultVolatile: true. Result stays valid ImportText input and deterministic. Stable constructor defaults remain unchanged. Blueprint-authored member names are emitted lowercase because Unreal's case-preserving FName display casing depends on asset load order. Lookup remains case-insensitive. To import, open VS Code extension Datapacks, choose Import game data, select generated .kdfdata, then bind imported datapack to project. Pack Manager validates manifest/schema, stores immutable archive copy, and exposes contents as datapack reflection section to editor and language server. See VS Code Extension & LSP for project binding, reflection requirements, and schema-only validation. Directory form is useful during editor/language-server development. Extension import finds reflection data by manifest.json at the archive root, under reflection/, or under kdf/reflection/. These prefixes are case-sensitive. Exactly one supported location may contain a manifest, and classes.ndjson must be a file under that same prefix; class records at another prefix cannot fill the gap. Multiple supported reflection manifests are rejected.

sections.heading: Runtime export publication and recovery
sections.text: The runtime exporter first writes loose files and the ZIP into a sibling directory named .<output-name>.kdf-export-<id>.stage. Preparation failures leave existing output files unchanged. Publication then replaces generated files individually, retiring obsolete generated files and publishing the new .kdfdata archive last. Do not read, import, edit, or start another export into that destination until completion. The whole directory is not replaced atomically. Before publication, the exporter preserves affected existing files under .<output-name>.kdf-export-<id>.stage.backup/previous/. Its recovery.json records the absolute destination, new archive filename, previousFiles, newFiles, and newDirectories. Paths in these three lists are relative to destination. A publication error attempts rollback and reports whether it completed; the recovery directory remains available even after a completed rollback. After every new file, including the archive, has been published, the exporter writes a sibling .<output-name>.kdf-export-<id>.stage.backup.committed file containing the same journal. It removes that marker only after removing the backup directory. A retained marker therefore records completed publication, possibly with interrupted cleanup; it does not prove artifact validity or that every backup file remains available. If writing the marker fails, publication can still succeed with a warning and retained recovery directory. An absent marker does not prove that publication failed. A process crash can interrupt publication or rollback. There is no automatic restart recovery. If output is incomplete or its state is uncertain: 1. Stop the exporting game process and any other writer to that destination. Copy the destination, matching staging directory, recovery directory, and commit marker, if present, to a safe location. Keep these copies unchanged until recovery is verified. 2. Inspect the journal and logs to identify the transaction and its exact destination. Confirm that every listed relative path stays inside that destination and that no affected path traverses a symlink, junction, reparse point, or nested mount. Do not combine journals from different exports. 3. If a commit marker exists, validate the published output first (see Validation). A valid completed export needs cleanup only. Without a marker, also check logs and validate before deciding to roll back: the marker write itself may have failed after successful publication. 4. To restore the previous files, first check that every previousFiles entry exists under backup/previous/. If any is missing, stop; interrupted cleanup may have removed part of the backup. Recover from the safe copies or another known-good export instead of using a partial backup. 5. Remove only the destination files listed in newFiles, if present. Remove only empty directories listed in newDirectories, deepest first; preserve directories containing other files. Copy each previousFiles entry from backup/previous/ back to the same relative destination path, creating parent directories as needed and overwriting the affected file. Restore any previous .kdfdata archive last. Copy, rather than move, so recovery sources stay intact. 6. Check restored files against the saved previous/ bytes and verify that newFiles are absent. Validate a restored complete export with both validators below. If no previous complete export existed, verify the restored prior state and generate a fresh export into a new empty directory. Retain the journals, staging files, backup, marker, and safe copies until these checks succeed. These names belong to runtime export. The metadata-merge commandlet uses separate .<output-name>.kdf-merge-<id>.stage and .backup sibling directories and directory-move recovery, explained under Editor Metadata Supplement. Do not apply runtime recovery.json steps to a metadata-merge backup.

sections.heading: Functions
sections.text: With --functions (included in the chat default and the auto export) each class record in classes.ndjson gets a functions array. The VS Code extension uses it to complete and check template function calls. | Field | Meaning | | name | The function name, lowercased so exports of different runs compare equal | | authoredName | The name with its authored letter case (GetItemName). Editors show this one. | | path | <ownerPath>:<name> | | ownerPath | The class that declares the function | | flags | The function flags, for example native, BlueprintPure, Const, Static, net and event flags | | params | Input parameters as property records, in declaration order | | return | The return value as a property record; absent when the function returns nothing | Property records use the same shape as class properties, including authoredName.

sections.heading: Integer bitmask metadata
sections.text: For integer properties with Bitmask and BitmaskEnum metadata, the exporter resolves only already-loaded enums. A full enum path must identify a loaded enum; a short name must uniquely match one. A resolved enum supplies its path, named options, and bitflags metadata. Plain integer bitmask properties also advertise bitmask operations and the named kdf.valueForm. A resolved enum with Bitflags metadata supplies bitmaskMode on both integer-bitmask and enum-backed property records: maskValues when UseEnumValuesAsMaskValuesInEditor metadata is present, and bitIndices otherwise. Consumers use that mode and exact option values to derive declared bits. Enum-backed properties keep enum import syntax; they do not get the pipe/sequence flag syntax or bitmask mutation operations used by plain integer BitmaskEnum properties. Without bitmaskMode, enum-backed properties use exact enum membership when complete option values are available. For plain integer bitmasks, an absent mode limits editor checks; runtime still requires a valid enum result and a value that fits the property. Missing metadata, an unloaded enum, or an ambiguous short name keeps the numeric fallback. Export does not load an enum merely to resolve this metadata. Runtime support requires WITH_METADATA and retained metadata; exported hints do not restore stripped runtime metadata. These hints describe available editor choices. Runtime value conversion still follows Property Types, including its mask-value, bit-index, and numeric forms.

sections.heading: Settings index
sections.text: indexes/settings.json lists the game settings that session:, ags: and option: references can read. It is written by every export. | Field | Meaning | | schemaVersion, engineVersion | Format and build | | counts | Number of settings per provider: session, ags, option, other | | settings | The records, sorted by provider, lowercase id and path | | unresolved | Setting assets that could not be indexed, with a reason (for example an empty id) | A record has: | Field | Meaning | | id | The setting id (StrId), exactly what follows the prefix in ags:<id> | | provider | session (SML session setting), ags (advanced game settings), option (local game options) or other (not readable by a prefix) | | path, class, source | The asset, its class, and which mod or the base game provides it | | displayName, tooltip | The texts shown in game | | valueType | bool, int, float, string, color or other | | default | The default value when it can be read | | range, displayRange | Slider or selection bounds; displayRange only when it differs | | options | {value, label} choices of an integer selector | | placements | Options-menu locations. Each entry contains category, optional subcategory and row priority; categories include class, display name and menu priority. | | sessionWide, dedicatedServerRelevant | Whether the setting is stored per session and whether a dedicated server uses it | | managerClass, mapWhitelist | The manager that owns the setting and, for session settings, the maps it is limited to | Active runtime-generated KDataForge sound sliders are included as option records with stable virtual paths and their Options → Audio placement. Dedicated servers do not create local Audio settings, so their exports omit these runtime-only records. The editor completes setting ids from this file and reports an unknown id as setting.unknown-id when the file exists.

sections.heading: Reload classification and cold-property catalog
sections.text: Every property declared directly by a class carries two extra fields under its kdf object: | Field | Meaning | | kdf.reload | hot, cold or newActors | | kdf.reloadReason | One sentence that says why, present when the classification comes from the catalog | - hot: a write applies live (an explicit allow-list entry). - cold: the game reads the property once or only when an object is created, so a live write does not change existing state. - newActors: the class default belongs to an actor or component, so only newly spawned actors see a write (the patch can set applyToSpawnedActors: true to include existing actors). Struct members, function parameters and container elements inherit the classification of the class property that contains them. The editor shows the classification next to path: completions and reports operations on cold or newActors properties as property.cold, see Reload classification. catalog/cold_properties.json is the catalog behind it: version, a description, and entries of {class, property, reload, reason, verified}. A class entry includes its subclasses and the property name is case-insensitive. verified: false marks an entry that is a reasonable assumption not yet checked in game.

sections.heading: Editor Metadata Supplement
sections.text: Packaged game may have WITH_METADATA disabled. Runtime records then contain metadataAvailable: false; export still succeeds. Generate metadata in modding editor: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe FactoryGame.uproject -run=KDFReflectionMetaExport -out=C:\Temp\KDFMeta Merge supplement into separate copy with same native commandlet: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe FactoryGame.uproject -run=KDFReflectionMetaExport ` -runtime=C:\Path\ReflectionExport ` -supplement=C:\Temp\KDFMeta\metadata.supplement.json ` -out=C:\Path\ReflectionMerged Merge records editor and game build per field and rebuilds mandatory ISO-named .kdfdata ZIP. The -runtime and -out directories must not overlap: they cannot be equal, and neither may contain the other. The -supplement file must be outside the -out directory, especially when using -force, which replaces an existing merge output directory. These path checks also apply without -force. On Windows and Linux, checks compare normalized paths and resolved physical paths, so symlink or junction aliases cannot bypass either restriction. Subsequent merge reads and writes use those resolved paths. The runtime directory and supplement file must exist. A new output path may have missing parent directories: the commandlet resolves its nearest existing directory ancestor and appends the missing components. Empty, inaccessible, dangling, or otherwise unresolvable paths are rejected before an existing output is replaced. Unsupported platforms reject the merge. The commandlet prepares a complete merged export and .kdfdata archive in a uniquely named sibling directory before replacing -out. Copy, metadata parsing, manifest, or archive errors during preparation leave an existing output untouched. The runtime manifest's generatedAt must be nonempty and contain no path separators because it supplies the archive filename. Keep the input and output directories unchanged until the commandlet finishes; do not run concurrent merges into the same output. With -force, the previous output moves to a uniquely named sibling backup before the prepared export moves into place. If publication fails, the commandlet tries to restore the backup. If restoration also fails, the error reports the backup path containing the previous output. Resolve any conflicting entry at -out, then move that backup directory back to -out. A successful merge removes its backup; a cleanup warning reports any backup retained for manual removal. Preparation failures also attempt to remove their staging directory and report its path if cleanup fails. These directory moves require same-filesystem rename support without replacing an existing entry. Linux requires renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE; unsupported kernels or filesystems reject publication. Replacement uses two directory moves, so an interrupted process can leave -out absent with the previous export in a sibling .<output-name>.kdf-merge-<id>.backup directory. Inspect any matching .stage and .backup directories before recovering or deleting them; staging directories may contain incomplete exports. Before -force replaces an existing output directory, the commandlet inspects its contents without following link targets. Any nested symlink or Windows reparse point blocks replacement, even if its target is unrelated to the inputs. On Linux, mount points also block replacement, including bind mounts on the same filesystem and an output directory that is itself a mount point. The resolved output target must share its parent's mount ID, and every nested entry must share that same mount ID. Mount IDs must be readable through /proc/self/fdinfo; if they cannot be verified, replacement is rejected. Unreadable entries, failed directory enumeration, or more than 1,000,000 entries also block replacement. Unmount mounted entries, remove other blocked entries, or choose a new output directory, then retry. No Python merge script is packaged into mod or archive.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.text: Run both validators after export completes: | Validator | Checks | | In-game KDF.ValidateReflection [--out <dir>] | Required live FactoryGame reflection shapes, authored user-struct member names, and sampled default ExportText/ImportText round trips (up to three per property kind). Checks required file presence, exactly one .kdfdata file, the FGUnlockRecipe Blueprint mapping, and basic settings, icon, and cold-property index structure when present. | | Python validate_reflection_export.py <directory> | Exported reflection contracts and records against the emitted draft 2020-12 schema; texture PNG integrity, dimensions, selection options, image/index consistency, and supported optional index/catalog checks. Requires exactly one ISO-named .kdfdata ZIP, sorted entries, valid ZIP CRCs, every generated file in the ZIP, and byte-for-byte agreement between each packed entry and its loose file. Unrelated regular custom files outside images/ may remain outside the archive. Also checks numeric integer schemaVersion: 1 and mirrors the editor's archive inspection gates: source archive at most 2 GiB, at most 20,000 entries, at most 4 GiB expanded, manifest.json at most 1 MiB, and each PNG within the 4 MiB preview limit. | ZIP entries and indexed image paths must use safe relative paths contained within the export directory; traversal paths are rejected. The Python validator rejects symlinks and Windows reparse points anywhere in the loose export tree, including unrelated custom entries. Regular custom files outside images/ remain permitted outside the generated archive. The Python validator checks PNG signatures, chunk boundaries and CRCs, and supported non-interlaced pixel layouts with valid bit-depth and color-type combinations. It requires a single first IHDR, valid PLTE placement and size when present, a palette before indexed image data, contiguous IDAT chunks, and an empty final IEND with no trailing bytes. It also checks the decoded byte count, complete compressed stream, and row filter values. Chunk types must contain four ASCII letters with an uppercase third letter. Unsupported critical chunks are rejected; unknown ancillary chunks remain permitted. Invalid structure is rejected even when CRCs and dimensions match. Native acceptance PASS does not verify ZIP contents, loose/packed parity, image integrity, or schema conformance. Use the Python artifact/package validator before distributing or importing an artifact. The editor can compact source archives larger than 512 MiB and rejects installed output that still exceeds its 512 MiB cache cap. Python PASS does not predict compacted-cache success or prove every VS Code extension import gate. Confirm acceptance through Import game data in the VS Code extension. The Python validator reads an export directory containing loose files and its .kdfdata archive; a standalone archive must first be extracted into a directory alongside that archive. Install Python dependency and validate one export from the modding workspace: python -m pip install jsonschema python Mods/GameFeatures/KDataForge/Tools/validate_reflection_export.py ` C:\Path\ReflectionExport For deterministic comparison, validate both exports with --compare: python Mods/GameFeatures/KDataForge/Tools/validate_reflection_export.py ` C:\Path\ReflectionExport --compare C:\Path\SecondReflectionExport Comparison hashes loose file paths and contents with SHA-256, excluding .kdfdata archives. It canonicalizes manifest.json and omits only its generatedAt field; other loose files are hashed as bytes. Each export must pass artifact validation before hashes are compared.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: - Blueprint load failures remain in manifest.json.failedLoads with reason. - Dedicated-server cooks or unsupported GPU formats may expose no readable pixels. Such records contain failure details instead of image bytes. - Per-class cap applies to non-texture classes. - All-mount exports can be large, especially with functions, flattened records, assets, or widgets. - Tick budget is checked between reflected records and Blueprint loads. One synchronous Asset Registry query, Blueprint load, garbage collection, or unusually large type can exceed budget by its own execution time because Unreal does not expose resumable versions of those operations. - Output determinism assumes identical game build, mod set, options, and registered content.

pages.title: VS Code Extension & LSP
pages.description: Install KDataForge Tools for completion, diagnostics, linting, Codex and typed KDataForgeJS authoring.

sections.heading: VS Code Extension & LSP
sections.text: KDataForge Tools adds KDataForge authoring support to VS Code. Extension ID: kmods.kdataforge. It bundles the Rust language server, project linter, Codex class browser, KDataForgeJS declarations, snippets and Explorer actions. No separate editor application is needed.

sections.heading: Install
sections.text: Install KDataForge Tools from VS Code Marketplace after the first public release, or install a platform-specific .vsix produced by the release workflow. Windows x64 and Linux x64 packages carry matching native sidecars. Remote workspaces run those sidecars on the workspace host. The extension requires a trusted filesystem workspace. Virtual and untrusted workspaces cannot run the native validators or create project files.

sections.heading: YAML language support
sections.text: Open a KDataForge project or any workspace containing DataForge/pack.yml. The extension provides: - schema and semantic diagnostics; - context-sensitive completion and hover; - go to definition, references and rename; - file, pack and project lint commands; - Codex search and class-reference insertion; - context actions for new KDataForge documents. The language server and CLI linter share the same validation core. A successful schema check does not prove that runtime classes, assets or functions exist when reflection data is unavailable.

sections.heading: Import and bind game data
sections.text: 1. Start a Satisfactory world with KDataForge and the mods your pack targets. After the world begins play, run: KDF.DumpReflection --assets --functions --flattened 2. Find the ISO-named .kdfdata archive under FactoryGame/KMods/ReflectionExport/, or the chosen --out directory. See Reflection Export for options and validation. 3. Run KDataForge: Switch datapack from the Command Palette and select or import the archive. 4. Confirm the effective datapack before relying on reflected completion or Codex results. Use an export matching the game build and installed mods. Missing or failed export records remain unknown; they are not proof that game content does not exist.

sections.heading: Schema-only mode
sections.text: Without usable game data, YAML schema and project validation remain available. Schema-only mode cannot establish whether a reflected class, property, function or asset exists. Reflection-dependent results state that limitation instead of treating missing metadata as success. For complete reflection-aware support, export classes with --flattened, functions with --functions, and non-texture assets with --assets.

sections.heading: KDataForgeJS projects
sections.text: Right-click a folder in Explorer and choose KDataForgeJS: Create Project Here. Generated projects receive the SDK bundled with the extension immediately, so TypeScript completion works before npm install. Available authoring actions: - KDataForgeJS: Create Script creates a typed handler without replacing existing files. - KDataForgeJS: Refresh Built-in SDK refreshes only the extension-managed SDK package. - kdf-handler, kdf-meta and kdf-item insert typed snippets. Generated package.json files retain @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs and @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli development dependencies. Install them when you need kdf check, kdf lint, kdf sync, kdf format or kdf validate outside VS Code.

sections.heading: Other LSP clients
sections.text: The kdf-language-server binary speaks LSP over stdio. A host can supply initializationOptions.kdf.datapackPath with a .kdfdata path; an empty string selects schema-only validation. The same setting is accepted through workspace/didChangeConfiguration. For applying YAML permanently to Unreal asset packages, see UE Editor Integration.

pages.title: YAML Schema
pages.description: Complete grammar for packs, document types, property paths, all 23 operations, conditions, and includes.

sections.heading: YAML Schema
sections.text: > This document is normative. Every construct here is implemented and covered by an example in > Examples.

sections.heading: File Discovery
sections.text: - Author root: <your-mod>/DataForge/. - Author glob: <your-mod>/DataForge/**/*.yml (and *.yaml). - Scanner root: the Unreal project directory, which is FactoryGame/ in a packaged game. - Up to six levels below the project root, a directory is a pack root when it is named DataForge, uses the legacy name data-editor, or directly contains pack.yml. Names are case-insensitive. Root discovery prunes Content, Saved, Intermediate, Binaries, DerivedDataCache, Plugins, Source, and Config. - Roots may nest. Each YAML file belongs only to its deepest enclosing root. - All *.yml / *.yaml files under a pack root are parsed as documents. A file normally holds one document, but may hold several separated by --- lines. See Multiple Documents Per File below. - Malformed YAML produces an Error and that file is skipped. The rest of the load continues.

sections.heading: Pack Manifest (`pack.yml`)
sections.text: Optional, at the pack root. Files without a manifest form an implicit pack whose ref and name come from the detected root's parent directory. Prefer an explicit stable ref; moving the root can otherwise change its implicit identity. ref: MyBalancePack # stable pack reference (save-persistence contract) required if present name: My Balance Pack # display name (default: ref) version: 1.2.0 # semver, informational + used by conflict reports priority: 100 # higher applies earlier within each stage (default 100) enabled: true # false disables the whole pack (default true) debug: false # true logs every applied op from every document in this pack (see Debug Logging) dependencies: # pack refs that must load before this pack - SomeOtherPack redirects: # id renames for generated content (see Content Creation) OldId: NewId # old save class paths resolve to the renamed class (FCoreRedirects) conditions: hasMod: - KAPI - KLib # optional same grammar as a document's `conditions:` (see # Conditions); gates every document in the pack (AND) conditions: on the manifest is evaluated once, before any file in the pack is even read, a failing pack is skipped entirely with one Info diagnostic, instead of every document failing its own copy of the same condition. Use it for "this whole pack is a compat layer for mod X" instead of repeating a conditions: block with hasMod: X at the top of every document. dependencies: are topological constraints. Missing or self-referential dependencies reject the pack, and invalidity propagates to transitive dependants. Dependency cycles are rejected. Among packs whose dependencies are ready, higher priority runs first and ref ascending breaks ties. redirects: maps old generated-content ids to new ones. Generated class names are id-based (Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>), so renaming an id would orphan save data. A redirect entry feeds FCoreRedirects so class paths in existing saves resolve to the renamed class. Renaming a _file_ never needs a redirect. Only id renames do.

sections.heading: Document Structure
sections.text: Every document is a YAML map with a root type: type: cdo # required (or use the `<name>.<type>.yml` filename convention) debug: true # optional log every applied op from this document (see Debug Logging) conditions: ? ... # optional see Conditions include: # optional same-pack files that must apply BEFORE this one - base-values.cdo.yml # … type-specific content priority: belongs to pack.yml, not individual documents. A document-level value is ignored by runtime and rejected by current standalone schemas. Within one pack, include dependencies apply first and remaining documents use deterministic relative-file order. Root type detection order: type: key → filename convention (iron.recipe.yml → recipe). Unknown types warn once and are skipped (they may belong to a handler from another mod or a later phase).

sections.heading: Multiple Documents Per File
sections.text: A file can hold more than one document by separating them with a --- line (the same convention Kubernetes multi-manifest YAML files use). This lets a small, self-contained pack live in one file instead of several: type: item items: - id: MySuperIngot parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties: - path: mDisplayName value: Super Ingot - path: mResourceSinkPoints value: 100 --- type: sinkpoints track: Default entries: - item: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot points: 100 - Every document still runs through the normal pipeline independently, with its own debug:, conditions:, and include:, staged and ordered exactly like a document from a separate file. - The <name>.<type>.yml filename convention only applies to single-document files. A file's name can't encode more than one type, so once a file holds multiple documents, every one of them must set its own type: key. A document with no type: in a multi-document file is skipped with a warning rather than falling back to the filename. - Diagnostics identify documents as file.yml[0], file.yml[1], … (zero-based, source order) so a warning always points at the right one. - include: file.yml (referencing a multi-document file by its bare name) waits for all of that file's documents to apply first. You don't need to know (or reference) how many documents it was split into. - A stray trailing --- with nothing after it produces a harmless empty document and is silently ignored. You don't need to trim it.

sections.heading: Root types
sections.text: Each root type is dispatched to its own stage-specific handler. The table below lists every built-in type, the stage it runs in during a load, and the page with its full grammar and worked examples: | Type | Stage | Detailed page | | gametag | GameTags | Game Tags | | asset | Assets | Data Assets | | dataasset | Assets | Data Assets | | curve | Assets | Float and Vector Curves | | localization | Localization | Localization | | cdo | CDOChanges | Patching (type: cdo) | | sublevel | CDOChanges | Sublevels | | item | Items | Items | | resource | Items | Resources | | building | Items | Buildings | | unlock | Items | Unlocks | | class | Items | Custom Classes | | recipe | Recipes | Recipes | | schematic | Schematics | Schematics | | research / mam | Research | Research Trees | | sinkpoints | SubsystemMods | Sink Points | | resourcenode | SubsystemMods | Resources | | eventrule | RuntimePatches | Event Rules | | custom (third-party) | handler-declared | registered via RegisterHandler, no page, it's yours | > All class generation types (item, resource, building, unlock, and the generic > class) run in the Items stage, priority-ordered > (class → unlock → item → resource → building), so > later stages (recipe, schematic, research) can reference every generated class.

sections.heading: Property Patches (`type: cdo`)
sections.text: Use actorSelector: with explicit actor targets and applyToSpawnedActors: true for instance-only tag, sphere, box and current-recipe selection. These entries never modify class defaults and cannot combine with asset/class scope filters. A cdo document patches properties on something that already exists: a class's default object, a live UObject such as a UDataAsset instance, or every asset matching a class/tag scan. It does not generate new content. One or more target selectors pick what gets patched, and one or more properties: ops describe the write: type: cdo patches: - # ---- one or more target selectors are required; matches accumulate ---- target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C # class path → patches the class default object # object path → patches that object directly (`UDataAsset` instances etc.) # a sequence of either → every entry resolved and patched independently # AND/OR: allAssetsOfClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDataAssetBase # every asset of that class (and subclasses) found in the asset registry # AND/OR an `ofClass:` scope narrowed by one or more filters (all filters must pass): ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe # the scope: this class, its subclasses, its assets # required for matchTag / matchName / where; producedIn / ingredient / product default # to /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe when omitted matchTag: KMods.AlternateRecipe # scalar or sequence (all must match) tagProperty: mGameplayTags # optional explicit tag container property matchAssets: true # also match data-asset instances (default true) classType: blueprint # any (default), blueprint, native; real class flags, not class names excludeClasses: [/Game/Example/Excluded.Excluded_C] # exact classes only; descendants remain eligible matchName: Recipe_Alternate_* # wildcard on the class name (full path when it contains '/'); # scalar or sequence (any may match) producedIn: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer # recipes whose mProducedIn # references this class or a subclass; scalar or sequence (any may match) ingredient: Desc_IronIngot_C # recipes with this item (or a subclass) in mIngredients product: Desc_IronPlate_C # recipes with this item (or a subclass) in mProduct where: # one map, or a sequence of maps that must all hold - path: mManufactoringDuration # property path; `[*]` = any element (read-only) greaterThan: 4 # exactly one operator per clause: # equals | notEquals | lessThan | lessOrEqual | greaterThan | greaterOrEqual # contains | notContains | in [any of] | notIn [any of] | matches (wildcard) | isEmpty (true/false) # ---- modifiers ---- applyToSubclasses: false # class targets: also patch every derived class CDO applyToSpawnedActors: false # actor classes: re-apply ops to every spawning instance deferOneGameTick: false # wait until one game tick after BeginPlay before resolving/applying # ---- the ops ---- properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration # see Property Paths op: multiply # see Operations (default: set) value: 0.5 An explicit target: accepts one non-empty scalar reference or a non-empty list of them. An empty or non-scalar member invalidates the entire patch entry, with a source-line diagnostic; other selectors on that entry do not bypass the error. See target lists.

sections.heading: Sublevel Blocking (`type: sublevel`)
sections.text: A sublevel document blocks RefinedRDLib or KBFL sublevel descriptor assets during the CDOChanges stage. block: must be a non-empty sequence. Each entry is an exact asset object path, or a map with target: (scalar or sequence), allAssetsOfClass:, and/or an ofClass: scope with filters (matchTag:, matchName:, where:; assets only, ofClass: is required): type: sublevel block: - /SomeMod/World/DA_OptionalSublevel.DA_OptionalSublevel - target: - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_A.DA_Nodes_A - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_B.DA_Nodes_B - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset - ofClass: /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset matchName: DA_Optional_* Exact paths use direct object loading. Bulk class scans include derived classes but depend on the Asset Registry being populated. Other asset families warn and must be patched through type: cdo. The provider mods are optional soft integrations. Full behavior and diagnostics: Sublevels.

sections.heading: Property Paths
sections.text: path: addresses a single property, or a nested member reached through arrays, sets, maps, or object references. It uses a small path grammar shared by every operation below: Segment(.Segment)* Segment = Name([<int>] | ["key"] | [key])* | Example | Meaning | | mManufactoringDuration | plain property | | mIngredients[0].Amount | struct member of array element 0 | | mSomeMap["Iron"].Value | struct member of map value for key Iron | | mSomeSet[2] | third element of a set (logical order) | | mMeshComponent.RelativeScale3D | dereference through an object-typed member (components, subobjects) | | mIngredients[*].ItemClass | any element (cdo where: filters only, never in properties: ops) | Blueprint-defined properties match on their authored name (case-insensitive), so mangled BP names never appear in YAML.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.text: op: values and their argument keys. Full worked examples: Operations. | Op | Applies to | Arguments | | set (default) | everything | value | | add, subtract, multiply, divide, min, max | numeric | value | | clamp | numeric | min, max | | append | array, set, map, string/name/text, tag container, bitmask | value (map for map; scalar or sequence otherwise) | | append_unique | array | value (one element or sequence); append only missing values, preserving existing duplicates | | prepend | array, set, string/name/text, tag container, bitmask | value (scalar or sequence) | | insert | array | index, value | | remove | array (by value), set (by value), map (by key), tag container, bitmask | value | | remove_at | array | index | | clear | array, set, map, string/name/text, tag container, bitmask | none | | swap | array | index, with | | replace | array | index, value | | duplicate | array | index | | sort, reverse | array | none | | unique | array (set: no-op) | none | | copy, move | everything | from (property path on the same object; move clears the source) | Unsupported op×type combinations are diagnostics at load time, never silent no-ops.

sections.heading: Special-cased properties
sections.text: A few properties need more than a plain reflected write. KDataForge handles them automatically: - FGameplayTagContainer: accepts set/append/prepend/remove/clear with plain tag names (no native-struct text form needed). - mStackSize (any FGItemDescriptor-derived target): this is an EStackSize enum (SS_ONE/SS_SMALL/SS_MEDIUM/SS_BIG/SS_HUGE/SS_FLUID), not a plain integer. Set it with an enum value name like any other enum property. The engine also caches item stack sizes, so writing the property alone would not change anything in-game. This is why KBFL ships a dedicated UKBFLCDOItemStackSize helper. Any op that writes mStackSize also resets the descriptor's cached stack size (mCachedStackSize), so the change takes effect out of the box. There are two caveats. Inventories that already contain the item may need the item re-added (or a game reload) before slots reflect the new limit. Also, if you use KBFL's own CDO assets for stack sizes, don't patch the same descriptor from both sides. Example with the full caveat: Balancing → Items.

sections.heading: Value Forms (by property type)
sections.text: Each reflected property type accepts its own YAML shape when used as an operation's value: (or min/max/with argument). The table below is the authoritative mapping from UE property type to accepted YAML form: | Property type | YAML form | | bool | true / false / yes / no / on / off / 1 / 0 | | int32, int64, uint*, uint8 | integer scalar | | float, double | number scalar | | enum | value name (RF_SOLID, EResourceForm::RF_SOLID) or numeric value (must be a valid ordinal, rejected otherwise) | | bitmask (int32/etc. with meta=(Bitmask, BitmaskEnum=...)) | one flag name (Above), a YAML sequence of names, an "Above|Left" string, or, for set only, a nonnegative unsigned decimal mask bounded by the property width. Named forms require available property metadata and a loaded enum, supporting declared mask values and bit indices. Export emits a name sequence. append/prepend OR-add flags, remove clears bits, and clear writes zero. See rules below. | | FString, FName | string scalar | | FText | string scalar, null (empty), localized {key, ns, source}, or StringTable reference {stringTable, key}; both table fields must be non-empty and must not mix with ns or source | | object reference | full object path; a bare generated-content id (e.g. SuperIngotIcon for a dataasset/asset entry, see Generated Content Short Ids); ""/none → null | | class reference | class path (/Script/Module.Class or /Game/....Asset_C; _C auto-retried), or a bare generated-content id (e.g. MySuperIngot for an item/resource/building/class/... entry, see Generated Content Short Ids), or, as a last resort, a bare class name (Desc_Water) resolved by name against every class currently loaded in memory; ambiguous bare-name forms log an error (LogKDataForge, listing every match) and use the first match (sorted by full class path), so prefer full paths in published packs when it matters | | TSoftObjectPtr / TSoftClassPtr | path string (not loaded) | | struct | native text form ("(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)"), block map with named fields, or block positional sequence | | FGameplayTag | tag name string | | FGameplayTagContainer | sequence of tag names | | TArray | sequence | | TSet | sequence | | TMap | map (keys converted via the key property type) | | nested structs | nested maps, any depth | For bitmasks whose enum has Bitflags metadata, available enum metadata distinguishes declared mask values (UseEnumValuesAsMaskValuesInEditor=true) from bit indices. Named bit indices 0..63 map to 1 << index and must fit the property width: 0..7, 0..15, 0..31, or 0..63 for 8-, 16-, 32-, or 64-bit properties, including signed properties. Plain integer bitmask handling requires WITH_METADATA, property Bitmask and BitmaskEnum metadata, and the referenced enum already loaded. If metadata is stripped or the enum cannot be resolved, conversion falls back to ordinary integer rules, including normal signed ranges; named bitmask forms and mutation operations are unavailable. Shipping builds must retain that metadata to use these forms. Enum-backed properties follow their separate enum conversion path: set one enum name or numeric value, with Bitflags values limited to declared bits. Pipe-joined names, sequences of flag names, and bitmask mutation operations are not supported for enum-backed properties. Reflection exports bitmaskMode for resolved enums with Bitflags metadata, including enum-backed property records, so editor validation can check their declared bits. Raw masks are accepted by set only; append/prepend and remove require named flags. Raw masks must contain only declared bits when the enum has Bitflags metadata; otherwise the resulting value must match a valid enum value. Both forms must fit the property width. Recognized signed bitmask properties accept the full unsigned bit pattern (0..4294967295 for int32, 0..18446744073709551615 for int64). Named flags must also fit that width. Negative enum values and declared mask values using bit 63 are unsupported because UEnum stores signed int64 values; bit-index 63 remains supported. Ordinary integer properties retain their normal signed ranges. See Property Types for examples and high-bit behavior.

sections.heading: Gameplay Tag Registration (`type: gametag`)
sections.text: A gametag document registers new FGameplayTag names with the engine's gameplay tag tree before any other document type runs. This matters because tags referenced from cdo targeting (matchTag:) or from a FGameplayTagContainer property write must already exist to resolve: type: gametag tags: - tag: MyPack.Machines.Special # map form with comment comment: Marks special machines - MyPack.Simple # scalar shorthand Tags are registered at runtime by appending to the gameplay-tag settings list in memory, never written to config files, with a tag-tree rebuild when needed. This is the only runtime channel that survives the engine's own tree reconstructs. Register tags before using them in cdo documents: the GameTags stage always runs first.

sections.heading: Content Creation (`item`, `resource`, `building`, `recipe`, `schematic`, `research`, `unlock`)
sections.text: These seven root types generate new classes at runtime. All share the same entry grammar. Only the plural list key and the default parent differ: type: item # or resource / building / recipe / schematic / research / unlock items: # plural key per type see table below - id: MySuperIngot # required stable id, the save-persistence contract parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C # optional properties: # identical op entries to cdo patches, applied to the new class's CDO - path: mDisplayName value: Super Ingot - path: mStackSize value: SS_HUGE # EStackSize enum, not a plain integer see Special-cased properties | Type | Plural key | Default parent | | item | items | /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor | | resource | resources | /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor | | building | buildings | /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildingDescriptor | | recipe | recipes | /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe | | schematic | schematics | /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic | | research | research | /Script/FactoryGame.FGResearchTree | | unlock | unlocks | none: a concrete FGUnlock subclass must be given as parent |

sections.heading: Generated class identity (save-persistence contract)
sections.text: - Classes live in package /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef> and are named Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>: deterministic and id-based, never derived from file paths or load order. - Reference a generated class elsewhere (recipes, unlocks, sinkpoints, other YAML) as /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> with no _C suffix. - The id is the contract. Renaming a file is safe. Renaming an id needs a pack redirect (redirects: in pack.yml). - Classes are created during GameInstance INITIALIZATION strictly before any save loads, so save class-path resolution finds them in memory. - Constraint: generated classes have the parent's layout, with no new reflected properties or components. All variation lives in CDO defaults (which is exactly what properties: sets).

sections.heading: Generated Content Short Ids
sections.text: Anywhere a class or object reference is accepted (parent:, properties: values, target:, item: on sinkpoints, class:, …), a bare id (just the id: a document gave the content, e.g. MySuperIngot) resolves in addition to the full /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> path. Both forms always work; use whichever reads better: type: item items: - id: PureSuperIngot parent: SuperIngot # short id same as /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_SuperIngot - Resolution order: the id is looked up in the current document's own pack first (the common case: most references are to something the same pack just generated). If it isn't there, every pack's generated content is searched; a match in exactly one other pack still resolves. Matches in more than one pack log an error (LogKDataForge, listing every match) and apply to the first match (sorted by full path), the same ambiguity handling as the bare class-name shortcut above. Qualify with the full path to remove any ambiguity or to reference another pack's content unambiguously. - Covers both generated classes (item/resource/building/recipe/schematic/research/ unlock/class) and generated asset instances (dataasset/asset, e.g. an icon's id in mSmallIcon: SuperIngotIcon instead of /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotIcon). - Only tried for name-only input (no / and no . at all). Anything that looks like a path is always treated as a path, never as an id. - Works everywhere a class/object reference is resolved: properties: values, target:, allAssetsOfClass:, ofClass:, parent:, register-only class:, item: on sinkpoints, and spawn-time actor patches (applyToSpawnedActors: true) re-applied to newly spawned actors.

sections.heading: Registration (`recipe`, `schematic`, `research`)
sections.text: type: recipe recipes: - id: Recipe_MySuperIngot register: true # default omit unless you want registration off properties: - path: mManufactoringDuration value: 4

sections.heading: Removing registered content (`recipe`, `schematic`, `research`)
sections.text: These three document types also accept a document-level remove: sequence. It may be the whole document or appear beside the normal entries list. An entry is either a bare class reference (full path, bare class name, or generated-content short id) that removes exactly that class, or a **filter map** using the scope filters — matchTag:, matchName:, producedIn:, ingredient:, product:, where:, optional ofClass: — that removes every class of the type passing all of them: type: schematic remove: - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C - Schematic_ObsoleteFromAnotherPack - where: # filter map: ofClass defaults to FGSchematic here path: mTechTier greaterOrEqual: 8 # Optional: registration/generation entries can coexist. Explicit removal runs after registration. schematics: - id: Schematic_Replacement - Only recipe, schematic, and research (including type: mam) support this key. item, resource, building, unlock, and class do not have a live registry-removal path. - A bare reference matches by exact class; removing a parent does not remove its subclasses. A filter map's ofClass: defaults to FGRecipe / FGSchematic / FGResearchTree and must stay within that base; a map without any filter key is an error. - Filter rules are stored as predicates and evaluated against every class of the kind the game presents (recipes: on every grant; schematics/research: at world registration), so classes that load later are still caught. - Schematic and research-tree removal is save-clean and reverses on the next session after the pack is removed. Existing purchase/unlock state is not revoked. - Recipe removal prevents future adds and sweeps recipes restored from the server save. The available-recipe list is saved, but it self-heals on a later load without the pack when purchased schematics reapply their unlocks. - Removing a schematic does not remove recipes it already granted. Pair schematic and recipe removal rules when the content itself must become unavailable. See Removing Content for the consolidated guide, and Recipes, Schematics, and Research Trees for kind-specific notes. - register: true (default) queues the class for per-world registration into SML's UModContentRegistry, before the registry freezes at world begin play. Auto-propagation applies: registering a schematic registers its recipes. Recipes register their items. - Register-only mode: use class: instead of id: to register an existing class without generating one: type: schematic schematics: - class: /Game/SomeMod/Schematics/Schematic_Hidden.Schematic_Hidden_C # register, don't generate

sections.heading: Nodes: placing a schematic in a research tree
sections.text: A research entry modifies its visual M.A.M. graph directly. addNodes: appends node instances; it does not update or deduplicate an existing node with the same schematic. A usable node normally supplies the displayed schematic: and a coordinate:. parents: creates prerequisite relationships; with autoPath: true on the research entry, KDataForge also creates straight roads for those relationships: type: research research: - id: MyResearchTree autoPath: true addNodes: - schematic: Schematic_First coordinate: X: 0 Y: 0 - schematic: Schematic_Second coordinate: X: 2 Y: 0 parents: - schematic: Schematic_First - schematic: accepts a generated short id or a full UFGSchematic class path. - coordinate: is a block map with numeric X: and Y: fields. Supply it for a node that participates in graph relationships or roads. - parents:, nodesToUnhide:, and unhiddenBy: are optional. Each reference may name another node's schematic: or a literal coordinate. References may point forward or backward within the same addNodes: list, or to a node already present on the target tree. - autoPath: defaults to false. When enabled, each resolved parents: relationship gets a straight, two-point visual road. Leave it off and provide childrenAndRoads: on the parent for a bent or otherwise custom route. - class: optionally selects a UFGResearchTreeNode subclass; properties: applies ordinary property operations to that node. A convenience field missing from a custom node logs a warning and is skipped rather than failing the whole document. A custom road uses a child coordinate and every point along the path. childrenAndRoads: can be one a block map with key and points fields, or a sequence of those maps when a node has multiple children: addNodes: - schematic: Schematic_First coordinate: X: 0 Y: 0 childrenAndRoads: - key: X: 2 Y: 0 points: - X: 0 Y: 0 - X: 0 Y: 1 - X: 2 Y: 1 - X: 2 Y: 0 - key: X: 0 Y: 2 points: - X: 0 Y: 0 - X: 0 Y: 2 Use tree-entry-level removeNodes: to remove nodes by schematic class or short id. Each selector may be a scalar (Schematic_Obsolete) or a block map with schematic: Schematic_Obsolete. KDataForge performs all removals before appending the same entry's addNodes: list and removes every surviving Parents, NodesToUnhide, UnhiddenBy, and ChildrenAndRoads reference to each removed coordinate. The same entry may remove one node and add another; autoPath: applies to additions: research: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C register: false autoPath: true removeNodes: - Schematic_Obsolete addNodes: - schematic: Schematic_Replacement coordinate: X: 3 Y: 1 parents: - schematic: Schematic_ExistingParent autoPath: is a sibling of addNodes: on the research entry and generates straight roads for its resolved parents: relationships. To move a node, select and re-add the same schematic with its new coordinate. nodes: remains a legacy alias. If both keys exist, addNodes: wins and KDataForge warns that nodes: was ignored.

sections.heading: Instanced Dependencies on Research Trees
sections.text: Research entries accept unlockDependencies: and visibilityDependencies:. Both use the block maps containing class: and properties: in the instanced FGAvailabilityDependency shape; they append to mUnlockDependencies and mVisibilityDependencies, respectively. research: - id: MyResearchTree unlockDependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: - path: mSchematics value: - Schematic_MyPrerequisite visibilityDependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGGamePhaseReachedDependency properties: - path: mGamePhase value: EGP_EarlyGame

sections.heading: Instanced Unlocks on Schematics (`unlocks:`)
sections.text: Schematic entries accept an unlocks: list. Each entry creates an instanced FGUnlock subobject on the schematic's CDO. This works with any concrete FGUnlock subclass the base game ships, not just FGUnlockRecipe; see the Base-Game Unlock Classes for the full list: type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_MySuperIngot properties: - path: mDisplayName value: My Super Ingot unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties: - path: mRecipes value: - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Recipe_MySuperIngot Known native FactoryGame/KMods class paths automatically remap to their Blueprint implementation. Exact Blueprint paths remain valid. Concrete native classes without Blueprints stay native; abstract classes without concrete variants cannot be instanced.

sections.heading: Schematic shortcut unlocks
sections.text: In addition to generic unlocks:, schematic entries accept recipes: (sequence of UFGRecipe classes), schematics: (sequence of UFGSchematic classes), positive-integer handSlots: and inventorySlots:, and scannableResources: (sequence of block maps containing resource: and nodeType:, with nodeType: Node by default). Each shortcut creates the corresponding normal FGUnlock instance; class references resolve exactly like every other generated, vanilla, or mod class reference.

sections.heading: Instanced Dependencies on Schematics (`dependencies:`)
sections.text: Schematic entries also accept a dependencies: list (the same instanced-object mechanism as unlocks:), targeting mSchematicDependencies instead of mUnlocks. Each entry creates an instanced FGAvailabilityDependency subobject on the schematic's CDO: type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_AdvancedSuperIngot properties: - path: mDisplayName value: Advanced Super Ingot dependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: - path: mSchematics value: - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Schematic_MySuperIngot - path: mRequireAllSchematicsToBePurchased value: true Pair it with mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess/mHiddenUntilDependenciesMet (ordinary properties:) to control whether the schematic is merely blocked from purchase or hidden entirely until the dependency is met. See Type: schematic → Gating a schematic on prerequisites for the full worked example and other FGAvailabilityDependency subclasses worth knowing about.

sections.heading: Generic Class Generation (`type: class`)
sections.text: The seven preset types above are the recommended, ergonomic forms. class is the **escape hatch for everything else: it generates a new class from any** parent, whether native C++ (/Script/Module.Class) or Blueprint (/Game/....Thing_C). Examples include equipment descriptors, vehicle descriptors, item/schematic categories, FGUnlock subclasses, other mods' classes gated behind hasMod, reparented buildables, and more. type: class debug: true # optional (see Debug Logging) classes: - id: MyCustomThing parent: /Script/FactoryGame.FGEquipmentDescriptor # ANY class: native C++ or /Game/...Thing_C registerAs: recipe # OPTIONAL: recipe | schematic | research queues SML content # registration for kinds that need it; omit for everything else properties: - path: mDisplayName value: My Equipment # cdo-style op entries applied to the new class's CDO - Same save-stable identity as the preset kinds: /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. Manifest, tombstones, and redirects: all apply identically. - Runs in the Items stage (same as item/resource/building/unlock), so recipe, schematic, and research documents can reference the generated classes. - registerAs: queues the class into SML's UModContentRegistry like the corresponding preset type would. It's only needed for the three registered kinds. Everything else just needs to exist. - The constraint stays: generated classes copy the parent's layout, with no new reflected properties or components. All variation is CDO defaults. Worked examples (equipment descriptor, category, modded parent behind hasMod) live at Custom Classes. For reparenting a buildable as part of a complete building, see A Complete Building.

sections.heading: 2D Image Assets (`type: asset`)
sections.text: Loads image files from the pack and turns them into real, referenceable UTexture2D assets: type: asset assets: - id: MyIcon file: icons/my-icon.png # relative to the pack root; png / jpg / tga / bmp - Decoded at load into a transient UTexture2D at /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> and announced to the asset registry. - Reference it from any properties: entry like any other object path: value: /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MyIcon. - Image files are decoded during the next GameInstance initialization after they change. - 2D only: no FBX/glTF, ever, by design. DDS and WAV image formats aren't supported yet (PNG/JPG/TGA/BMP are). Icon usage example (item mSmallIcon / mPersistentBigIcon): Data Assets → 2D image assets.

sections.heading: Dynamic DataAsset Instances (`type: dataasset`)
sections.text: Creates real UDataAsset instances (not classes) at runtime, using package /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef> and name Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. It announces them to the asset registry so scanning subsystems can find them. UPrimaryDataAsset subclasses are the common consumer-facing case, but the runtime validator accepts any UDataAsset subclass. type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: CleanerItem_MyFluid class: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription # any UDataAsset subclass properties: - path: mProductionTime value: 4.0 - path: mInFluid value: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount: 1000 After the initial load, KDataForge automatically triggers consumer rescans when data assets were modified or added: - KAPI: called via reflection only when the KAPI mod is loaded, no hard dependency needed. - RefinedRDApi: called via reflection only when the RefinedRDApi mod is loaded, with no dependency needed. It covers RefinedPower / FicsitFarming boiler/cooler/heater/turbine/generator/dirt data assets. Existing data assets (KAPI's, RRDA's, any mod's) are already editable via cdo documents (target: object path, allAssetsOfClass:, matchTag:). The dataasset type is only for creating new instances. Data-asset entries may also contain unlocks: and dependencies: lists. They append instanced objects to mUnlocks and mTaskDependencies when selected class exposes those arrays. This is intended for UKAPIDeliveryTask; incompatible classes report missing array at runtime. Entry shape and native-to-Blueprint remapping match schematic lists.

sections.heading: Float and Vector Curve Assets (`type: curve`)
sections.text: Creates new or edits existing UCurveFloat and UCurveVector assets. keys: replaces complete key set on each entry. type: curve curveType: float # float | vector curves: - id: DamageFalloff # exactly one of id or target # target: /Game/Curves/Curve_Damage.Curve_Damage defaultValue: 0 # vector defaults use X/Y/Z fields in a block mapping preInfinityExtrap: constant postInfinityExtrap: linear isEventCurve: false # float only keys: - time: 0 value: 1 # vectors also accept block X/Y/Z fields or block sequence items interpMode: cubic # constant | linear | cubic tangentMode: auto # auto | smartAuto | user | break tangentWeightMode: none # none | arrive | leave | both arriveTangent: 0 leaveTangent: 0 arriveTangentWeight: 0 leaveTangentWeight: 0 preInfinityExtrap and postInfinityExtrap accept none, constant, linear, cycle, cycleWithOffset, or oscillate. Times must be finite and unique within one entry. Vector values and tangent fields accept an X/Y/Z map or three-number sequence. Generated curves use object path /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> and have no _C suffix. See Float and Vector Curves for full examples and troubleshooting.

sections.heading: AWESOME Sink Point Values (`type: sinkpoints`)
sections.text: A sinkpoints document sets the AWESOME Sink point value for one or more items on a named track. The FGResourceSinkSubsystem consults this whenever it looks up how many points an item is worth: type: sinkpoints track: Default # Default | Exploration entries: - item: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C points: 100 overridden: 50 # optional - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor # filter form instead of `item:` — every loaded where: # item descriptor passing the filters gets these points path: mForm in: [RF_LIQUID, RF_GAS] points: 0 An entry names one item:, or replaces it with an ofClass: scope (default FGItemDescriptor) plus filters (matchTag:, matchName:, where:, …). Filter entries expand against the item descriptor classes loaded when the document applies. Not live-reloadable (registry freeze): sinkpoint changes need a session restart.

sections.heading: Resource Nodes (`type: resourcenode`)
sections.text: A resourcenode document requires at least one non-empty remove:, add: or replace: sequence. For placement identities, KBFL-style range checks, node reuse, replacement, mesh/material overrides and save/occupied-node constraints, see Resource Node Placement. Within remove:, a scalar is shorthand for a map with only resource:. Valid entries still apply when another entry reports an error: type: resourcenode remove: - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Uranium/Desc_OreUranium.Desc_OreUranium_C - resource: MyGeneratedResource nodeTypes: [Node, FrackingCore] allowOccupied: false removeFromScanner: true - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor # filter form instead of `resource:` matchName: Desc_OreUranium* # every loaded descriptor passing the filters nodeTypes: [Node] - resource: must resolve to a UFGResourceDescriptor class. Generated-content short ids work. Alternatively an entry carries an ofClass: scope (default FGResourceDescriptor) plus filters (matchTag:, matchName:, where:, …) and applies its options to every loaded descriptor class that passes. - nodeTypes: is optional. Omitted or empty means all types; accepted values are Node, FrackingSatellite, FrackingCore, Geyser, and Deposit, with or without the EResourceNodeType:: prefix. - allowOccupied: defaults to false. The default skips and warns about node groups used by an extractor. true can invalidate an extractor's node reference. - removeFromScanner: defaults to true. It also strips vanilla scanner pairs and matching KAPI allow-list data, then refreshes scanner/radar caches. :::danger Vanilla can persist level-placed node destruction in the save. Deleting the YAML does not reliably restore those actors. Back up the save and read the full persistence and deferred-pass limitations under Resources and Resource Nodes. :::

sections.heading: Runtime Text Entries (`type: localization`)
sections.text: A localization document injects or overrides FText string table entries at runtime. It is scoped to a namespace and optionally a single culture, and it needs no separate localization asset shipped: type: localization namespace: MyPack culture: de # optional; prefix-matched against current language; omit = all entries: SimpleKey: 'Übersetzter Text' KeyWithSource: source: 'Original English' text: 'Deutscher Text' # override existing texts - culture: is prefix-matched against the current language (de matches de-DE). Omitting it applies the entries for every language. - The scalar form sets the text for namespace/key. A block map with source and text fields overrides existing texts by their original source string. - Localization documents apply during GameInstance initialization. Restart the session after edits.

sections.heading: Debug Logging
sections.text: Every applied op can be traced. Three levels, from narrow to global: | Level | How | Effect | | Document | debug: true top-level key in any document type | Every applied op from that document logs | | Pack | debug: true in pack.yml | Every applied op from every document of the pack logs | | Global | console variable KDF.Debug 1 (or launch arg -KDFDebug) | Everything logs, including editor-originated ops | Log lines go to the game log at Log verbosity, one per applied op: [KDF DEBUG] <file>: <target path>.<property path> <op> : <pre value> -> <post value> Walkthrough (where the log file lives, reading the lines): Getting Started → Debugging.

sections.heading: Conditions
sections.text: Condition objects use AND by default; conditionBehaivor: OR opts into alternatives. A failing combined result skips the document with an Info diagnostic. conditions: gameVersion: '>=416000.0.0' # semver range vs the game version, reported as <changelist>.0.0 # (SML convention) gate on the game's build changelist, e.g. the # CL from the game's main menu / `>=491125.0.0` for the SML baseline hasMod: KAPI # scalar… # hasMod may instead use a block sequence; `Ref@<range>` pins a version modVersion: # explicit map form for version constraints SML: '>=3.12.0' hasClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator # hasClass may instead use a block sequence conditions: may also be an array of condition objects. Within each object, condition keys are AND-combined first; ifNotMatch: true then negates that object. Top-level conditionBehaivor combines the object results using AND or OR (case-insensitive) and defaults to AND. Correctly spelled conditionBehavior is accepted as an alias. ifNotMatch defaults to false. conditionBehaivor: AND # optional; default conditions: - hasMod: - KAPI - KLib # require both - hasMod: IncompatibleMod # require this mod to be absent ifNotMatch: true - modVersion: # reject this version range if mod is loaded OptionalIntegration: '^2.0.0' ifNotMatch: true An inverted hasMod: Mod@<range> object matches when the mod is absent or its loaded version does not satisfy <range>. Inversion never hides malformed condition keys, types, or version ranges. Because inversion applies to the entire object, use separate inverted objects when excluding multiple mods independently. conditionBehaivor: OR conditions: - hasMod: RefinedPower - hasMod: FicsitFarming OR passes when at least one object matches; AND requires every object.
