Smelts like Iron Ingot at 2.0x speed. {cfg:texts.motto} and {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} are replaced before anything is applied. {item:<class>:GetItemName} is read from the game when the property is written: the item provider calls the engine function GetItemName on the Iron Ingot class and returns the localized name. See Templates .

sections.heading: Step 6: a cold value
sections.text: The milestone’s tier is read when the game registers the schematic, so it is a cold value. In the schematic document the tier property takes the field like any other value: properties : - path : mTechTier value : cfg:features.tier features.tier has apply: cold , which is also the default. Changing it in the values file changes the saved value immediately, but the running game keeps the tier it started with and reports restart required .

sections.heading: Step 7: test it
sections.text: Load a save and open the chat. /kdf config dump KDFSample The fields are listed in no particular order, one line each, with the value, the default and the effective value: KDFSample:balance.ironSpeed [hot] = 2.0 (default 2.0, effective 2.0) KDFSample:features.enableBonus [hot] = true (default true, effective true) KDFSample:features.tier [cold] = 1 (default 1, effective 1) KDFSample:tags.extra [hot] = [KDF.Sample.Test] (default [KDF.Sample.Test], effective [KDF.Sample.Test]) KDFSample:texts.motto [hot] = Forged from YAML. Stacks high, sinks well. (default Forged from YAML. Stacks high, sinks well., effective Forged from YAML. Stacks high, sinks well.) 5 configuration field(s) Change a hot value and apply it: /kdf config set KDFSample:balance.ironSpeed 3 /kdf config apply KDFSample The reply says Saved: yes, reloaded: yes and lists the changed key. The Iron Ingot recipe now takes a third of its original time, and the Super Ingot description shows 3.0x . Turn the bonus off the same way ( /kdf config set KDFSample:features.enableBonus false ) and the recipe’s output returns to normal after the apply, because the element condition removed the operation. Now the cold value: /kdf config set KDFSample:features.tier 2 /kdf config apply KDFSample The reply ends with Restart required: KDFSample:features.tier (in yellow). The file now says tier: 2 , and /kdf config dump shows the value 2, restart required , and an effective value that is still 1. After the next start the milestone sits in tier 2. You can also edit FactoryGame/Configs/Packs/KDFSample.config.yml with a text editor and run /kdf reload : hot values apply, cold values report restart required. To try templates and expressions without touching any file: KDF.Template "{cfg:texts.motto} x{cfg:balance.ironSpeed}" KDFSample KDF.Config.Expr "features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed >= 2" KDFSample

sections.heading: Step 8: validate in the editor
sections.text: Open the project in the VS Code extension, or run kdf lint on the folder that contains DataForge/ . The editor checks the definition (required name and description , ids, ranges, defaults, categories), every cfg: reference and config: expression, template syntax, and whether a hot value feeds a cold place. Try breaking something: Edit Diagnostic cfg:balance.ironSped config.unknown-id config: !features.enableBonus config.expression-quote value: {cfg:texts.motto} text template.unquoted-start remove description from a field schema.required icon: nope.png pack.icon-missing See Lint Your Pack and the VS Code extension .

sections.heading: Step 9: let players change it in game
sections.text: Players can use the chat commands above, or edit the file. For a real settings screen, build a widget with the Blueprint Config API : list the packs with Get All Pack Infos , the fields with Get Config Descriptions Flat , create a slider, a checkbox, a dropdown and a text box per Get Kind , and call Apply Config Changes from an Apply button. The reference describes the full node flow.

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: On a listen server , the host changes values and they are sent to the clients while connected. Clients cannot edit them. On a dedicated server , edit the server’s values file and run /kdf reload , or change values as an administrator from a settings screen or with /kdf config set and /kdf config apply . A client whose cold features.tier differs from the host’s keeps its loaded content, reports a host mismatch, and can adopt the host’s values from the UI. A client never writes the host’s values to its own file, and leaving the session restores the local values. All players still need the same packs installed. See Pack Configuration .

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Symptom Fix /kdf config dump lists 0 fields The *.config.yml file is outside the pack, or a field has an error. Run /kdf report . The recipe did not change after apply The field is cold (restart), or the patch target is wrong. Check apply: hot and /kdf report . The description still shows {cfg:texts.motto} The scalar was not quoted, or the id is misspelled. A pre-pass token that cannot be resolved stays as written and logs a warning. Restart advised after applying a hot value The hot field also feeds a cold place. Use a cold field there, or restart. The category shows as FGCategory The category class was not found. Check the id in category: and that the .class.yml is in the same pack.

sections.heading: Where to go next
sections.text: Templates and Typed References : all providers, function calls, nesting and escaping Config Expressions : the full config: grammar Blueprint Config API : build the settings screen Conditions & Packs : where config: conditions can go

pages.title: Renaming Content Safely
pages.description: What you can rename in a pack for free, what needs a redirects entry, and the one rename redirects genuinely can't fix.

sections.heading: Renaming Content Safely
sections.text: Sooner or later you’ll want to rename something in a pack that’s already shipped. Three different things can be “renamed,” and only one of them is free. This walks through all three, the exact mechanism behind the safe one, and a worked before/after so you can copy-paste the real fix.

sections.heading: The three renames
sections.text: What you rename Changes the generated class path? Safe by default? Fix A file ( super-ingot.item.yml → ingot.item.yml ) No Yes, always Nothing: the filename is never part of any generated identity An id ( id: MyItem → id: MyItemV2 ) Yes No Add a redirects: entry in pack.yml (see below) A pack’s ref Yes, for every id in the pack No, and there’s no fix Don’t. See “Renaming the pack ref ” below Generated classes live at /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef> and are named Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> . This naming is deterministic and built from PackRef + id , never from a file path ( Generated class identity ). That’s why the file is free and the other two aren’t: the file was never part of the identity to begin with.

sections.heading: What redirects: actually does
sections.text: Syntax, in pack.yml : ref : MyPack version : 2.0.0 redirects : OldId : NewId # OldId: NewId, one entry per renamed id Under the hood ( FKDFDynamicContentRegistry::ApplyRedirects in Source/KDataForge/Private/Content/KDFDynamicContent.cpp ), each entry becomes one FCoreRedirect built from the pack’s current ref : const FString OldPath = MakeClassPackageName (PackRef) + TEXT ( " . " ) + MakeClassName (PackRef, Redirect . Key ); const FString NewPath = MakeClassPackageName (PackRef) + TEXT ( " . " ) + MakeClassName (PackRef, Redirect . Value ); Redirects . Emplace (ECoreRedirectFlags::Type_Class, OldPath, NewPath); So a MyPack redirect MySuperIngot: SuperIngotMk2 registers a Type_Class redirect from /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot to /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotMk2 via FCoreRedirects::AddRedirectList . When an old save deserialises a reference to the old class path, the engine’s own class-path resolution walks through FCoreRedirects first and lands on the new class instead. The object loads normally, with no missing-class warning. It has to ship in the same version bump as the rename. ApplyRedirects runs once per pack ref, every session, right before any generated class can be referenced ( UKDFSubsystem::ApplyStages , guarded by mRedirectedPacks so a live a session restart doesn’t re-register it). There’s nothing baked into the save. The redirect is re-derived from pack.yml on every load. That has one important consequence: if you ever delete the redirects: entry in a later version, the redirect stops being registered on the very next launch, and any save that still references the old class path breaks again. There’s no expiry or “safe after N versions” in the code. Keep the entry in redirects: for as long as you want to support saves made before the rename. In practice that means indefinitely, unless you’re certain every player has re-saved since.

sections.heading: Worked scenario: MySuperIngot → SuperIngotMk2 in v2.0.0
sections.text: Before (pack version 1.0.0), generates /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot : super-ingot.item.yml type : item items : - id : MySuperIngot parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Ingot After: rename the id , bump pack.yml , and add the redirect in the same version: super-ingot.item.yml type : item items : - id : SuperIngotMk2 # renamed parent : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties : - path : mDisplayName value : Super Ingot pack.yml ref : MyPack name : My Content Pack version : 2.0.0 redirects : MySuperIngot : SuperIngotMk2 # OldId: NewId The class is now generated as /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotMk2 . Any reference elsewhere in your own YAML (recipes, schematics, sink points) needs updating to the new path too. redirects: only fixes resolution of old save data : it doesn’t rewrite your other documents for you. Any save made under v1.0.0 that still has Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot embedded resolves straight through to Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotMk2 on load, with no warning. A second worked copy of this exact scenario also lives in End-to-End Pack → Renaming an id later if you want to see it next to a full multi-file pack.

sections.heading: Renaming the pack ref
sections.text: Don’t. This is the one case where the honest answer is “unsupported,” not “here’s the workaround.” ApplyRedirects takes a single PackRef and builds both the old and new class paths from it: MakeClassPackageName(PackRef) is the same call for OldPath and NewPath . There is no code path that builds an old path from one ref and a new path from a different ref . Since a ref rename changes /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef> for every single generated class in the pack simultaneously, there’s no mechanism, redirects: or otherwise, that bridges an old ref’s package to a new ref’s package. Every id in the pack would need its own cross-package redirect, and the feature simply doesn’t build one. Treat ref: as permanent once you’ve shipped a version with real players. If you genuinely need a different display name, change name: instead. ref: is the save-persistence contract, and name: is cosmetic.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Shipped an id rename, then got reports of missing items in old saves: you forgot the redirects: entry. Add it retroactively in a follow-up version. It’s read fresh at every load, never baked into the save, so adding it late still fixes existing saves the next time they load. No save wipe needed. Added a redirect, but old saves still show a missing class: check direction and spelling first. The map is OldId: NewId , not the reverse, and both sides are the raw id: value (not the display name), matched exactly. SanitizeToken only swaps non-alphanumeric characters for underscores, so it doesn’t fix a typo or a case mismatch. How to verify a redirect actually took effect: ApplyRedirects logs one line per entry to the game log at Log severity (visible without enabling KDF.Debug ): [LogKDataForge] Redirect: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_OldId -> /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_NewId . /kdf report shows load diagnostics (errors/warnings/tombstones) but doesn’t list applied redirects directly, so the log is the source of truth here. Accidentally renamed a pack ref : there’s no redirect fix (see above). The practical options are reverting the ref back, or accepting that saves made before the change lose those generated objects. They’ll come back as tombstones with a warning if the old ref ’s YAML still exists somewhere, otherwise they’re gone. The generated class identity contract is the normative persistence reference. Conditions & Packs has the compact redirects: syntax, while End-to-End Pack shows the same rename inside a complete multi-file pack.

pages.title: Custom Research Trees
pages.description: Build a named M.A.M. research tree and place a MAM-type schematic in its visual node graph entirely from YAML.

sections.heading: Custom Research Trees
sections.text: KDataForge can generate and register a M.A.M. research tree, create MAM-type schematics, and place those schematics into the tree’s visual graph. You can then extend an existing tree or remove a branch without leaving dangling graph links. No Unreal Editor step is required. Use type: research (or the filename-convention alias mam , such as my-tree.mam.yml ).

sections.heading: Step 1: create the tree
sections.text: kdf-sample.research.yml type : research research : - id : KDFSampleTree properties : - path : mDisplayName value : KDF Sample Research - path : mPreUnlockDisplayName value : ' ??? ' - path : mPreUnlockDescription value : Complete the HUB milestone that reveals this tree. - path : mPostUnlockDescription value : Research refined ingot processing. This generates a real UFGResearchTree subclass. register: true , the default, queues it into SML’s UModContentRegistry . The pre-unlock fields appear before the tree is revealed; the normal display name and post-unlock description appear afterward.

sections.heading: Step 2: create a MAM-type schematic
sections.text: mType: EST_MAM uses the same generation, registration, cost, and unlocks: mechanisms as a HUB milestone. It marks the schematic as research: pure-super-ingot.schematic.yml type : schematic schematics : - id : Schematic_PureSuperIngot properties : - path : mType value : EST_MAM - path : mDisplayName value : Refined Ingot Processing - path : mDescription value : Research a purer smelting process for the Super Ingot. - path : mTechTier value : 1 - path : mTimeToComplete value : 30 - path : mCost value : - ItemClass : /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlateReinforced/Desc_IronPlateReinforced.Desc_IronPlateReinforced_C Amount : 10 unlocks : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties : - path : mRecipes value : - /KDataForge/Gen/KDFSample.Gen_KDFSample_Recipe_PureSuperIngot Build the item and recipe behind this schematic with the pattern from Item + Icon + Recipe + Tier-1 Unlock .

sections.heading: Step 3: place the schematic in the tree
sections.text: Add addNodes: to the research entry. Each entry creates an instanced research-tree node: kdf-sample.research.yml type : research research : - id : KDFSampleTree properties : - path : mDisplayName value : KDF Sample Research - path : mPreUnlockDisplayName value : ' ??? ' - path : mPreUnlockDescription value : Complete the HUB milestone that reveals this tree. - path : mPostUnlockDescription value : Research refined ingot processing. addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_PureSuperIngot coordinate : X : 0 Y : 0 KDataForge creates the shared base-game BPD_ResearchTreeNode , writes the schematic and coordinate into its Blueprint data struct, and appends it to the tree’s mNodes array.

sections.heading: Step 4: add prerequisites and roads
sections.text: Reference another node by schematic id in parents: . Set autoPath: true on the research entry to generate straight roads automatically: type : research research : - id : KDFSampleTree autoPath : true properties : - path : mDisplayName value : KDF Sample Research addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_PureSuperIngot coordinate : X : 0 Y : 0 - schematic : Schematic_PureSuperIngotAdvanced coordinate : X : 1 Y : 0 parents : - schematic : Schematic_PureSuperIngot References can point forward or backward in the same addNodes: list because KDataForge records all coordinates before resolving relationships. It also indexes nodes that already exist on the target tree. Following example adds one node to vanilla Mycelia tree; register: false prevents redundant content-registry registration while still applying node mutation: type : research research : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C register : false autoPath : true addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_MyExtension coordinate : X : 4 Y : 2 parents : - schematic : Schematic_ExistingParent nodesToUnhide : - X : 5 Y : 2 nodesToUnhide: and unhiddenBy: use the same literal-coordinate or block-map schematic: reference form as parents: . A custom UFGResearchTreeNode subclass can be selected with class: ; use its properties: list for any additional reflected fields. For a custom route, keep autoPath: false and define childrenAndRoads: on the parent: addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_PureSuperIngot coordinate : X : 0 Y : 0 childrenAndRoads : key : X : 1 Y : 0 points : - X : 0 Y : 0 - X : 0 Y : 1 - X : 1 Y : 1 - X : 1 Y : 0 See the addNodes: schema for nodesToUnhide: , unhiddenBy: , multiple children, and custom node classes.

sections.heading: Step 5: add, remove, or move nodes safely
sections.text: Use tree-entry-level removeNodes: when a branch is no longer part of your pack. Select each node by its schematic class; a generated short id works when it resolves unambiguously. Put addNodes: beside it to add a replacement or another branch in the same mutation. autoPath: true generates roads for newly added parent relationships: type : research research : - class : /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C autoPath : true removeNodes : - Schematic_ObsoleteExtension addNodes : - schematic : Schematic_NewExtension coordinate : X : 6 Y : 3 parents : - schematic : Schematic_ExistingParent KDataForge removes the selected node and cleans every surviving reference to its coordinate: Parents , NodesToUnhide , UnhiddenBy , and ChildrenAndRoads . In one tree entry, removals run before the new addNodes: list is appended, so example above removes obsolete branch before adding new one. Omit addNodes: when node should disappear completely. To move or replace a node, use same schematic in both lists and give addNodes: entry its new coordinate. Legacy nodes: remains accepted, but addNodes: wins when both keys exist.

sections.heading: How the Blueprint node data is writable
sections.text: The base C++ node exposes GetNodeSchematic() as a BlueprintImplementableEvent . The shared BPD_ResearchTreeNode class also stores its data in the Blueprint variable mNodeDataStruct . KDataForge resolves the struct’s authored member names through reflection, including Blueprint members whose internal storage names contain GUIDs. This is the same property-resolution mechanism used elsewhere in KDataForge. A custom UFGResearchTreeNode subclass can be selected with class: and can receive extra operations through the node’s properties: list.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: The tree does not appear: Confirm register: true and inspect /kdf report . A node field is missing: Check /kdf report or KDF.Debug 1 for an unresolved schematic or authored field name. A custom class: fails: It must derive from UFGResearchTreeNode . Automatic roads are not shaped correctly: autoPath only creates straight two-point roads. Use manual childrenAndRoads: for bends. The MAM schematic is not purchasable: Verify its cost item, registration, and unlock classes. The Research Trees and Schematics feature pages explain the two capabilities independently. The node schema is the normative field reference. If the item, recipe, and schematic chain is new to you, start with Item + Icon + Recipe + Tier-1 Unlock .

pages.title: Tag-Based Bulk Balancing
pages.description: Register your own gameplay tag, mark a pile of content as yours or as needing rebalancing, and bulk-edit everything carrying that tag in one patch instead of one cdo patch per target.

sections.heading: Tag-Based Bulk Balancing
sections.text: You’re rebalancing a dozen recipes and you don’t want a dozen target: patches to keep in sync as the list grows. This tutorial builds a small, reusable tag, marks a handful of recipes with it across separate files, and bulk-edits every one of them with a single matchTag: patch. That’s the same mechanism the Balancing page shows in miniature. Here it’s worked all the way through with real files, covering the exact matching rules end to end.

sections.heading: The problem this solves
sections.text: One target: patch per recipe works fine for three recipes. It stops working once you’re maintaining thirty: every new tuned recipe needs its own patch entry, and nothing tells you which recipes are “yours” versus vanilla, untouched ones. A gameplay tag fixes both problems. Tag every recipe you touch as you create or edit it, then write one patch that matches the tag and applies to whatever currently carries it. That covers today’s four recipes or next month’s forty, with no patch-list maintenance required. ℹ️ Tags are for sets the game does not already describe. If the recipes you want share a producer building, an ingredient, a product, a naming convention, or a property value, you don’t need a tag at all: producedIn: , ingredient: , product: , matchName: and where: select on those directly, and combine with matchTag: on the same patch. See Targeting → scope filters . This tutorial is about the case where the set is defined by you , not by the data.

sections.heading: Step 1: register your own tag
sections.text: myoverhaul-tags.gametag.yml type : gametag tags : - tag : MyOverhaul.Rebalanced comment : Recipes tuned by MyOverhaul's balance pass Full mechanics are in Game Tags , but the short version matters here. UKDFGameTagHandler does not write a tag .ini file anywhere. Instead it appends a row straight onto the UGameplayTagsSettings CDO’s GameplayTagList array, in memory only, never saved to disk, then calls DestroyGameplayTagTree() / ConstructGameplayTagTree() so the engine’s tag tree picks it up. That rebuild is what makes FGameplayTag::RequestGameplayTag("MyOverhaul.Rebalanced") resolve to a valid tag afterward. Registration is idempotent, so an already-listed tag is skipped. This needs GameplayTags.ImportTagsFromConfig = true , which Satisfactory ships with enabled, so you don’t need to configure anything for that part. GameTags is always the first stage , ahead of every other document type in the same load. That means this tag is already registered and usable by the time any cdo document in the same pack runs, so no include: is needed for the gametag file itself.

sections.heading: Existing content (vanilla or another mod’s): a plain cdo patch
sections.text: myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronPlate.Recipe_IronPlate_C properties : - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronRod.Recipe_IronRod_C properties : - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml type : cdo patches : - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_Wire.Recipe_Wire_C properties : - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced - target : /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_Screw.Recipe_Screw_C properties : - path : mGameplayTags op : append value : - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced That’s two files and four recipes, with no coordination between them beyond both existing. This is the point: tagging is additive, and it doesn’t care which file or which pack a given target was tagged from.

sections.heading: Your own freshly generated content: tag it in its OWN document, not a separate cdo patch
sections.text: If a recipe is one you’re generating in this same pack ( type: recipe , id: form), put mGameplayTags straight into that document’s own properties: instead of writing a follow-up cdo patch for it: my-recipe.recipe.yml type : recipe recipes : - id : Recipe_MyThing properties : - path : mDisplayName value : My Thing - path : mGameplayTags value : - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced # … mIngredients, mProduct, mManufactoringDuration, mProducedIn … This isn’t a style preference. It’s the only version guaranteed to work on the very first load. See Step 3 and Troubleshooting for why a separate cdo patch targeting a same-pass generated recipe doesn’t resolve on that first load.

sections.heading: Step 3: the bulk patch: matchTag + ofClass + tagProperty
sections.text: myoverhaul-rebalance.cdo.yml type : cdo include : - myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml - myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml patches : - matchTag : MyOverhaul.Rebalanced ofClass : /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe tagProperty : mGameplayTags properties : - path : mManufactoringDuration op : multiply value : 0.8 # 20% faster myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml and myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml are both cdo documents, in the same CDOChanges stage as the bulk patch, so they need explicit include: ordering here. That’s different from the gametag file in Step 1. GameTags is a stage that always finishes before CDOChanges even starts, so it never needs an include: entry. Two cdo documents in the same stage need one whenever one depends on the other having already run.

sections.heading: The worked scenario, end to end
sections.text: Four vanilla recipes, tagged from two files, sped up 20% by one bulk patch: myoverhaul-tags.gametag.yml registers MyOverhaul.Rebalanced . myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml tags Recipe_IronPlate and Recipe_IronRod . myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml tags Recipe_Wire and Recipe_Screw . myoverhaul-rebalance.cdo.yml scans FGRecipe with matchTag for the tag and multiplies mManufactoringDuration by 0.8 . Add a fifth recipe to the tag next month. That’s one more target: line in whichever tagging file makes sense, with zero changes to myoverhaul-rebalance.cdo.yml . The patch keeps applying to “everything tagged MyOverhaul.Rebalanced ,” not to a fixed list. A self-contained version of this exact pattern uses four real vanilla recipes, one gametag file, and one cdo file. It applies tag-then-matchTag in a single document instead of splitting across files, since ops inside one document’s patches: list apply top-to-bottom. It looks like this: rebalance-tags.gametag.yml + rebalance-vanilla-recipes.cdo.yml .

sections.heading: When to reach for a native KMods.* tag instead of your own
sections.text: KAPI already registers a set of native tags: KMods.AlternateRecipe , KMods.EventOnly , KMods.Deprecated , KMods.WIP , KMods.Cheat , KMods.Disabled , KMods.ExcludeFromNodeRandomization , KMods.PlannerExclude , and KMods.WikiExclude . See the full list in Data Assets → KMods native gameplay tags , and a worked matchTag example against them in Balancing → Buffing all alternate recipes . Use a native KMods.* tag when… Register your own tag when… You want content that’s ALREADY carrying the tag (e.g. every alternate recipe in the game, tagged by KAPI/other KMods) You’re marking content you’re touching: nothing upstream tags it for you The category is a general, cross-pack concept (deprecated, WIP, event-only, cheat) The category is specific to your pack’s own balance pass or content set You’re fine gating the whole document behind hasMod: KAPI You don’t want a KAPI dependency at all The two aren’t mutually exclusive. A single matchTag: list can include both, for example matchTag: with block-sequence entries KMods.AlternateRecipe and MyOverhaul.Rebalanced , remembering that’s an AND: “alternates that are ALSO mine.” Native tags always require a conditions: block with hasMod: KAPI on the document, since they don’t exist without KAPI loaded. Your own tags never need any hasMod gate.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Tag not registering / “Invalid tag” at load time. The error includes the engine’s own suggested fix, usually a stray space or extra dot in the dotted tag string. Fix the YAML string, not the tag. See Game Tags → Troubleshooting . matchTag matched no objects: check ofClass first. ofClass has to be the class the tagged content actually is, or an ancestor of it. ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic will never match a recipe’s tags, even if the tag name is identical. Confirm with /kdf report which classes were actually scoped. matchTag matched no objects: check tagProperty next. If a class exposes a tag container under a non-standard name, an unnamed or mis-typed tagProperty silently finds nothing rather than erroring. The lookup fails closed, not loud. matchTag matched no objects, and the target is content YOU generated in the SAME pack. type: cdo runs before the content-generation stages. A matchTag scan cannot discover a class that this initialization pass has not generated yet. Put the tag and initial property values in the generated entry’s properties: block. Do not rely on a later session: short-id and tag discovery still happen before generation. An exact canonical generated-class path can be watched and patched when that class is created, but this is a narrow lazy-resolution mechanism, not general cross-stage ordering. Inline properties are the predictable solution. A KMods.* tag “doesn’t exist”, or the whole document silently skips. You forgot a conditions: block with hasMod: KAPI . Without KAPI loaded, KAPI’s own tags never register, so matchTag: KMods.AlternateRecipe fails with “unknown gameplay tag.” If you did gate the document, a missing KAPI install just skips it quietly, an Info diagnostic in /kdf report , not an error, rather than breaking your pack. Game Tags covers registration mechanics, ordering, and session initialization. Targeting catalogs every selector, including matchTag with ofClass , target: , and allAssetsOfClass: . For more bulk-edit examples, including the native KMods.* alternate-recipe buff, see Balancing .
